surprises.text: The ddim sampler name gives the same pixels as euler (same seed, same graph). Core maps the name to Euler; only the inpaint noise option differs.
CFGNorm at strength 1 with CFG 14 washed an SDXL render to pale grey on this seed, while Rescale and APG at the same CFG stayed usable.

The linear_quadratic schedule with dpmpp_2m smeared an SDXL render at 20 steps, with rainbow speckle. On this model its last non-zero sigma at 20 steps is 2.67, against 0.03 for karras, so the last step jumps a long way to zero.
ddim_uniform starts lower than the rest: sigma 11.03 at 20 steps on SD and SDXL, where the others start at 14.61. It rendered brighter, with a different layout.
Karras at 20 steps broke SD 3.5 Medium with Euler (brown and unfinished), while simple, beta and kl_optimal held together on the same seed.
dpmpp_2s_ancestral_cfg_pp subtracts stage-2 uncond from stage-1 guided x0: the second model call overwrites temp[0] before the final update reads it, so the update uses D₁−U₂.

uni_pc replaces final σ=0 with 0.001 through a view (sigmas[:]), mutating sigmas. KSAMPLER then applies inverse_noise_scaling at 0.001, so on CONST models the result is divided by 0.999; sampling also stops at σ=0.001. One-step runs never move x (read, not run).

dpm_fast and dpm_adaptive throw away the schedule. Only sigmas[0], the last non-zero σ (and for dpm_fast the length) are used, sampling stops at sigmas[-2] with no denoise-to-zero, and sigmas [σ,0] give zero movement (read, not run).
SamplerEulerCFGpp version=alternative ends with 2D−U rather than D: the last step adds the guidance gap again. Regular version is different code.
cfgpp_ud10_ab does not return the model's last x0: at σ'=0 it replaces x with a linear extrapolation of D to σ=0 (zero_weight=1.0). It also keeps the cfg=1 shortcut, unlike other CFG++ samplers.

Flow-model handling is uneven. Only euler_ancestral, dpm_2_ancestral and dpmpp_2s_ancestral dispatch to RF code; res_multistep_ancestral and dpmpp_2s_ancestral_cfg_pp run VE ancestral maths on flow σ; dpmpp_2m uses −log σ while 2M SDE uses logit. The 2S RF path also sets its midpoint to 0.9999 at σ=1.0.
deis coefficients use fixed EDM constants (σ_min 0.002, σ_max 80), not the model's schedule, on every model including flow.

The ddim name runs Euler with different inpaint noise; an unknown sampler name given to KSampler silently becomes euler; KSampler alone discards the penultimate σ for dpm_2, dpm_2_ancestral, uni_pc and uni_pc_bh2, so a SamplerCustom graph gets a different schedule. The only literal DDIM loop is VOID_DDIM.

NAG scale is off by one between camps: core and the ComfyUI-NAG forks use z₊φ − z₋(φ−1), while sd-perturbed-attention, Anima-NAG and Krea2-NAG use z₊ + φ(z₊−z₋). The same number is not the same strength.
"NAG" in RT-RareTools never touches attention: it runs the formula on whole denoised predictions.
belgiangurista SMC-CFG has no sliding surface or state; lambda and warm-up inputs are unused, and it adds −k·sign(e).
S²-Guidance: ceil wraps only pct/100, so any non-zero percentage skips every block.
bvhari PerpNeg's variable "perp" is the parallel projection of positive on negative, the reverse geometry of core.
Negative-attention builds a new randomly initialised nn.Linear on each attention call, so its effect depends on RNG state.
sd-perturbed-attention FDG calls project and then adds both parts straight back, so the projection is a no-op.
Core CFGNorm's strength multiplies the whole x0 (0 gives x̂=0), and its pre_cfg=true mode installs a cfg function, not a pre-CFG hook.

SECURITY, not a maths method. `` holds a base85 blob decrypted with AES-CBC using a key embedded in the file, decompressed, then passed to `exec(compile(...))`, and it calls `exit()` when a `gettrace` debugger check is true. A comment on the following lines says logic lives in the "internal payload", and the node display name is set to "uiltnode". The module names are hidden as char-code lists. Status is library, not installed. Not decoded or run. Owner should review before this pack is ever enabled.

RISK: eval/exec in shared workflows. A static scan found `eval(`/`exec(` in 103 of 865 section-28 packs (some false positives). Real text-widget cases: ``, `` (passes real `__builtins__` beside a "restricted scope" comment), `` (numpy namespace in eval globals). Core uses simpleeval instead, ``.

Frequency bands inverted: both mask an unshifted FFT with a centre-based radius, so "low" and "high" are swapped. `` and `TensorVizion__OmniNodes/Creative Intelligent Nodes`. Reasoned from code, not run.

Core lanczos is unsafe for latents: it clips to 0..1 and quantises to 8 bits, ``. LatentUpscale hides it from its combo, but any pack passing it to common_upscale hits it. FlowMatching-Upscaler guards at ``.
Core LatentInterpolate norm lacks keepdim, ``, so by broadcasting rules batch>1 errors, and batch==channels silently pairs the wrong axes. Reasoned from code, not run.
WAS BlendLatents rescales every output to 0..1, ``; soft_light takes sqrt of raw values at :75, giving NaN on negatives.
"bislerp" blend in PPFN/Apt_Preset is lerp plus min-max rescale, ``; bleh keeps the formula under the name bislerp_wrong at ``. Also PPFN adjust truncates to 4 channels, ``.

In-place writes and hijacks: MTB lerp overwrites the upstream tensor through `out=` after a shallow copy, ``; ReSharpen monkeypatches latent_preview at import and edits sampler x in a preview callback, ``.
PowerNoiseSuite "blue", "green" and "pink" are one filter with different default alpha: all divide the FFT by |f|^(α/2), so "blue" (α=2) has a 1/f² power spectrum, the reverse of real blue noise.
Sonar's named "white" is only ±1 (sign(n)·|n|⁰) and "velvet" reduces to Gaussian (sign(n)·|n| = n): the color names here mean pointwise remaps with a flat spectrum, not a spectrum shape.
SUNoise is not uniform noise at every step: even steps are plain Gaussian, and odd steps are uniform that skip both s_noise and σ_up.
City96's "LatentGaussianNoise" is uniform draws in hardcoded per-channel ranges (for example −22 to 33), far from unit variance.
Restart sampling in auto mode at 20+ steps discards your schedule and rebuilds sigmas as Karras.
Core s_churn on euler and heun uses torch.randn_like and ignores noise_sampler, so custom-noise nodes never reach it.
PPFN's Brownian hijack swaps the core class in module scope and mixes its fancy noise at a fixed 0.03 weight, so the "power noise" contribution per step is small by construction.
CADS adds its noise to prompt embeddings, not latents, then restores embedding mean and std; the latent is untouched.

ppm's Euler SMEA Dy gates its extra calls with `i + 1 // 2 == 1` and `== 0`. Python precedence makes these fire only on steps 1 and 0. . Same file's Euler Dy gate `i // 2 == 1` fires only at steps 2 and 3. Same file line 89.
Three of the TCD forks (licyk, dfl, SeedV) compute `sigma_to_s` from (1−γ)t and never use it, so gamma only toggles the DDPM variance on or off.

Euler extended sigmas' churn term is `(sigma_hat ** 2 - sigma_hat ** 2) ** 0.5`, always zero, and it divides by n_sub−1 which is zero for unsubdivided steps when s_churn>0. comfyui-lopi999-nodes sampler_list.py:223 (repo path in the entry).
MD AMED has no mean-value midpoint: it is Heun with a sigma-dependent derivative blend. . Boyo "Richardson" is a weighted x0 average, not extrapolation. See entry richardson-x0-accumulator for path.
MD PingPong imports `pingpong_sampler_core_bin` first and uses the source only as fallback, so a compiled binary would take priority if present.

Extra-Samplers-Plus ships two `sample_ttm_jvp` bodies differing only in φ₂ (h vs h_η).  vs other_samplers. The Clyb 4M docstring blames Bard and ChatGPT if its citation is wrong, extra_samplers.py:438.
Clyb BDF has no backward-difference table; it is a lerp predictor with elementwise atan and projection scaling.
SADA's docstring says Adams-Bashforth 23/12,−16/12,5/12 simplifies to 0.625,0.75,−0.375; the code uses the latter and they are not equal.
Core ToMe merges only the queries: `return m(q), k, v` leaves keys and values at full length, despite the name.
Core HyperTile tiles q but returns k and v in whole-image layout, so the backend views them into the larger batch in raster order (inference from attention.py:1096-1123).
Negative Attention builds a new untrained torch.nn.Linear on every attention call, so its correction term is random each call.
TurboTeaCache's Wan polynomial is all positive with constant 0.4945; default threshold is 0.15, so on Wan it should never skip at defaults (inference).

benjiyaya Spectrum truth-tests a sigma tensor with `or`; swallowed in spectrum_core.py:36, uncaught at nodes.py:130, while core always sets sample_sigmas, so a normal run should raise (inference, not run).
FreeU_Advanced and Sonar FreeU Extreme register `middle_block_patch`, a name nothing in this core reads, so their middle-block option does nothing.
Animemory replaces comfy.k_diffusion.sampling.sample_euler_ancestral at import, changing that sampler for every job if the pack is installed.
bleh's global Sage node overwrites __code__ on the live optimized_attention function, reaching code that imported it by name; KJNodes WanVideoTeaCacheKJ is now a no-op returning the model.

Same names, different curves. MD Hybrid's `ays`, `beta` and `simple` modes are a logistic blend, 1−(1−t^α)^β and smoothstep, and MD's GITS is a tanh warp with no tables; Adept's "AYS SDXL" table is near-uniform, not NVIDIA's.
Flux "shift" is the log of SD3 "shift": flux_time_shift with σ=1 equals time_snr_shift with α=e^μ, so the same number gives very different curves.  and :414
`denoise` means two things in core. BasicScheduler stretches and keeps `steps` steps; AYS, GITS and Optimal Steps cut to round(steps·denoise) steps.

Step counts that don't match the widget: ddim_uniform can return more than asked (read: N=1000, steps=30 gives 31 steps), beta can return fewer after removing repeats, and pack presets beta_32, beta_43 and beta_42 quietly add steps.
Core Laplace is the only core get_sigmas_* with no trailing zero, so it stops at sigma_min with residual noise.
Random inference schedules: the ai-toolkit-style `sigmoid` type draws unseeded torch.randn and sorts, so sigmas change each run.
A hard-coded Z-Image preset rises mid-run (.92 then .935), and core's ExtendIntermediateSigmas labels its sine curve 'cosine' and its cosine curve 'sine'.
Named schedulers that add nothing: TCDScheduler is core ddim_uniform and LCMScheduler is core sgm_uniform; "logSNR uniform" in Adept equals exponential when σmax>1.

Core's H3 PDD heads treat rows after the first as offsets from a full head, while CineConIA's loader says the official heads are full velocities and averages them all. The two may describe different file layouts (inference).
A hook-based LoRA is silently dropped on int8 H3 mlp.fc2, since core's fused call reads the weight and skips the module's forward. The live Turbo pack routes those layers to merge.

The NKD audio shift curve changes only the transformer option per step; ModelSamplingAV's audio_scale stays fixed, so the stream's effective schedule is not a plain re-shift (inference from reading both, not measured).

fxai-toolkit replaces comfy.model_base.MiniMaxH3 at import, so video noise scaling becomes σε + x for every H3 in the process. Core's MiniMaxH3SigmaShift builds a fresh sampling object, which would drop it (inference).
DaSiWa's H3 cache was filed under first-block-cache but runs no block to decide; it compares the stack's input, and it carries a full copy of core's H3 _forward to get a patch point.
CachedSearch uses a step cache only for ranking seeds, then re-renders the winner with the cache off, so the delivered latent is uncached.
ROCm's H3 EasyCache tooltip reads start_percent as a step fraction, but core converts the percent to a sigma, which does not map that way on a shift-12 schedule (reading core, not measured).
Kayarte's AudioNoiseMapper, with NOISE in its name, generates no noise: it returns a dict of parameters computed from audio energy.
LanPaint's Friction input still flows into Gamma, but only the commented-out damped scheme used Gamma, so the knob does nothing.
SUPREME adds its inner substep noise to z_k after z_avg was accumulated, and z_k is reset next substep, so it never reaches the output.
SUPREME substeps all restart from the same x, so with one method and no history term they average identical results.
Gigachad's CFG rescale divides x.std() by itself plus epsilon, so it is a no-op at any strength.
Radiance's apply_cfg_plus_plus is a cosine decay of the scale toward 1, unrelated to the CFG++ update.
RALU's Flux path calls forward_orig itself, so CFG, patches and ComfyUI samplers do not apply.
LatentTools' DownsampledLatentGuidance has its downscale lines commented out and now feeds a re-noised reference latent, at three extra cond calls.
TwinFlow ignores graph sigmas apart from their count, and with r=1 discards the noise estimate each step.

entries.name: AR Video (autoregressive block sampler)
entries.plain: Denoises a video one block of frames at a time using a model with key-value caches, in the style of Causal Forcing and Self-Forcing. Each sub-step jumps to x0 and re-noises on the flow line with fresh noise, then a final call at σ=0 writes the block into the cache. It refuses to run on models without the cache API.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
Block b frames; for each σ_i: D=model(block,σ_i). If σ'=0: block←D. Else fresh ε seeded by torch.manual_seed(seed+1000·b+i); block←(1−σ')D+σ'ε; rewind cache end by frames·seq_len.
After block: output frames←block; rewind cache; one more model call at σ=0.
I2V: an initial latent from transformer_options ar_config is fed at σ=0 first.

props.stages: N+1 per block (N=len(sigmas)−1), plus 1 for I2V seed
props.final_sigma0: σ'=0 returns D for the block; a σ=0 call is always made per block to update the cache.
props.flow_const: Assumes flow: re-noise uses (1−σ')D+σ'ε with no model_sampling lookup; noise_scale is ignored. Requires 5-D latents and init_kv_caches, init_crossattn_caches; raises otherwise.

entries.name: CFG++ UD10 AB (history CFG++)
entries.plain: A CFG++ Euler with three additions: a small history term on the unconditional slope, a 25% blend toward a variable-step second-order Adams-Bashforth step, and a final step that extrapolates x0 down to σ=0. It can be picked by name in the sampler list, but no node exposes its parameters, which are fixed. Unlike the other CFG++ samplers it keeps the cfg=1 shortcut, and at cfg=1 it uses the cond prediction as U. The name is not explained in the code.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
α_s,α_t as in Euler CFG++ (α_t=1 at σ'=0). dt=σ'−σ. d_u=(x−α_sU)/σ; for i>0 d̃_u=d_u+0.1·(dt/(σ−σ_{i−1}))(d_u−d_u,old).
E=α_tD+σ'd̃_u−x; store E/dt. First step uses E.
Later: H=c₀(E/dt)+c₁(prev), c from linear_multistep_coeff order 2; step=lerp(E,H,0.25); x'=x+step.
Final step when σ'=0 and history exists: x'=D−σ(D−D_old)/(σ−σ_{i−1}) (replaces x', zero_weight=1.0).

props.prediction_space: half-logSNR factors, σ step, eps from U
props.final_sigma0: Explicit: σ'=0 replaces x' with a linear extrapolation of D to σ=0, not D. If only one step ran there is no history and x'=E+x, which equals D.
props.flow_const: Handled through α factors.

audit.note: "No node exposes it" is wrong as written: cfgpp_ud10_ab is in KSAMPLER_NAMES (ComfyUI/comfy/samplers.py:974), so KSampler and KSamplerSelect can pick it; only its parameters are unexposed (sampling.py:483-484). Also omitted: unlike the other CFG++ samplers it does not disable the cfg=1 shortcut (sampling.py:437), and U falls back to cond_denoised at cfg=1 (sampling.py:433).

entries.name: DDIM (alias of Euler)
entries.plain: The name ddim does not have its own loop in core: the registry builds the Euler sampler with one extra inpaint option. The update is the same deterministic Euler line; only the noise used to re-noise the protected area of an inpaint mask differs. In σ coordinates Euler already has the η=0 DDIM form x'=(σ'/σ)x+(1−σ'/σ)D, so the name is not wrong, but no extra algorithm exists behind it.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
Same as Euler: x'=x+d·(σ'−σ).
Inpaint-only difference: KSamplerX0Inpaint gets a fresh noise tensor drawn on CPU with torch.manual_seed(seed+1), seed defaulting to 41, instead of the sampling noise tensor.

props.final_sigma0: Same as Euler: dt=−σ gives x'=D.
props.flow_const: Same as Euler.

entries.name: DDPM
entries.plain: The classic DDPM posterior step written in VP coordinates: scale the latent into VP space, compute the mean from ε, add posterior noise, scale back. One model call per step.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
ᾱ=1/(σ²+1), ᾱ'=1/(σ'²+1), a=ᾱ/ᾱ'. ε=(x−D)/σ; x_vp=x/√(1+σ²).
μ=(1/√a)(x_vp−(1−a)ε/√(1−ᾱ)). If σ'>0: μ+=√((1−a)(1−ᾱ')/(1−ᾱ))·n. x'=μ·√(1+σ'²).

props.final_sigma0: σ' =0 skips noise and the final rescale; algebra gives μ=D.
props.flow_const: No CONST branch: VP scaling √(1+σ²) is used on flow models too.

entries.name: DEIS (tab mode)
entries.plain: A multistep exponential integrator: past slopes are weighted by coefficients integrated numerically along a VP noise schedule. In core that schedule is fixed by hard-coded EDM-to-VP constants. No node exposes its options, so sampler name means order 3, tab mode.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
edm2t maps σ to VP time t with ε_s=1e-3, σ_min=0.002, σ_max=80 constants. Each step: order=min(3,i+1), forced to 1 when σ'≤0; weights c_j=Σ over 10000 points of I(τ)·L_j(τ)·Δτ, with L_j the Lagrange basis in t and I(τ)=−½(dlogᾱ/dτ)/√(ᾱ(1−ᾱ)).
Order 1: x'=x+(σ'−σ)d; otherwise x'=x+c₀d+c₁d₁(+c₂d₂).

props.prediction_space: slopes in σ, interpolated in VP time t
props.final_sigma0: t_next≤0 forces order 1, so the last step is Euler and equals D; coefficients for that interval are computed but not used.
props.flow_const: No CONST branch. The fixed VP constants apply to all models.

entries.name: DPM++ 2M
entries.plain: Second-order multistep DPM++ on x0 in −log σ: reuse the previous x0 prediction to correct the current step for one call per step. Deterministic, and the step formula has no special flow-model handling.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
t=−log σ, h=t'−t, r=h_last/h, D̄=(1+1/(2r))D−(1/(2r))D_old.
x'=(σ'/σ)x−(e^{−h}−1)D̄. First step and σ'=0 step use D̄=D.

props.final_sigma0: σ'=0 uses the first-order branch; t'=inf gives e^{−h}=0 and σ_fn(t')=0, so x'=D through IEEE inf with no separate return.
props.flow_const: No CONST branch. Uses −log σ, not logit, even on flow models; first-order form is the Euler line. Compare 2M SDE which does switch to logit.

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: dpmpp_2m and dpmpp_2m_sde step in different time variables on flow models: −log σ here, logit-based half-logSNR there. At η=0 on CONST the first-order part coincides algebraically but the second-order term differs.

entries.name: DPM++ 2M CFG++
entries.plain: A CFG++ rewrite of 2M: the exponential term carries the unconditional prediction while the guided x0 is added directly. The second-order correction here takes the difference between the current guided x0 and the previous unconditional x0. So unlike normal 2M it does not shrink to zero on a smooth path when guidance is on.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
t=−log σ, h=t'−t, r=h_last/h.
First step or σ'=0: x'=D+e^{−h}(x−U).
Else: x'=D+e^{−h}(x−U)+(1−e^{−h})/(2r)·(D−U_old).

props.prediction_space: x0 in −log σ, eps from U
props.final_sigma0: σ'=0 branch; e^{−h}=0 so x'=D.
props.flow_const: No CONST branch.

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Correction term is D−U_old, guided minus previous unguided, so it carries the guidance gap into the extrapolation; plain 2M uses D−D_old.

entries.name: DPM++ 2M SDE (Heun correction)
entries.plain: The same code as 2M SDE with solver_type=heun, which changes the coefficient of the second-order correction. There is no second model call despite the name: still one call per step.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
Same as 2M SDE except correction: x'+=α'(((1−e^{−h_η})/(−h_η))+1)(1/r)(D−D_old).

props.final_sigma0: Explicit: σ'=0 returns D.
props.flow_const: half-logSNR via sigma_to_half_log_snr: λ=−log σ normally, λ=log((1−σ)/σ) on CONST; α=σe^{λ} (1 normally, 1−σ on CONST). First σ≥1 on CONST replaced by percent_to_sigma(1e-4); s_noise×noise_scale.

entries.name: DPM++ 2M SDE (midpoint)
entries.plain: The 2M idea with a noise term: an exponential update on x0 in half-logSNR, a second-order correction from the previous x0, and Brownian noise. Default solver_type midpoint. η=0 removes the noise. One model call per step.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
λ=half-logSNR, h=λ'−λ, h_η=h(1+η), r=h_last/h, α'=σ'e^{λ'}.
x'=(σ'/σ)e^{−hη}x+α'(1−e^{−h_η})D.
From step 2: x'+=½α'(1−e^{−h_η})(1/r)(D−D_old).
If η,s_noise>0: x'+=n(σ,σ')·σ'·√(1−e^{−2hη})·s_noise.

props.final_sigma0: Explicit: σ'=0 returns D.
props.flow_const: half-logSNR via sigma_to_half_log_snr: λ=−log σ normally, λ=log((1−σ)/σ) on CONST; α=σe^{λ} (1 normally, 1−σ on CONST). First σ≥1 on CONST replaced by percent_to_sigma(1e-4); s_noise×noise_scale.

entries.name: DPM++ 2S Ancestral (flow / RF branch)
entries.plain: Flow-model path of dpmpp_2s_ancestral. It uses logit-based midpoint noise levels and linear interpolation toward x0, then the flow rescale and renoise. A hard-coded branch makes the first step degenerate when σ is exactly 1.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
RF step: ratio=1+(σ'/σ−1)η; σ_down=σ'·ratio; α'=1−σ'; α_down=1−σ_down; c=√(σ'²−σ_down²α'²/α_down²).
λ=log((1−σ)/σ); midpoint σ_s=1/(e^{(λ(σ)+λ(σ_down))/2}+1), except σ=1.0 uses σ_s=0.9999.
u=(σ_s/σ)x+(1−σ_s/σ)D; D₂ at σ_s; x_d=(σ_down/σ)x+(1−σ_down/σ)D₂.
If σ'>0 and η>0: x'=(α'/α_down)x_d+n·s_noise·c.

entries.name: DPM++ 2S Ancestral (VE path)
entries.plain: A two-stage single-step DPM++ method on x0 with ancestral noise. It evaluates at the midpoint in log σ toward σ_down and uses that second prediction for the full step. Non-flow branch; flow models use the RF entry.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
get_ancestral_step: σ_up=min(σ', η·√(σ'²(σ²−σ'²)/σ²)); σ_down=√(σ'²−σ_up²); η=0 returns (σ', 0).
t=−log σ, t_d=−log σ_down, h=t_d−t, s=t+h/2.
x₂=(σ(s)/σ)x−(e^{−h/2}−1)D; D₂ at σ(s); x'=(σ_down/σ)x−(e^{−h}−1)D₂. If σ'>0: x'+=n·s_noise·σ_up.

props.final_sigma0: Explicit: σ_down=0 Euler branch, equals D, no noise.
props.flow_const: Dispatches to sample_dpmpp_2s_ancestral_RF on CONST.

entries.name: DPM++ 2S Ancestral CFG++
entries.plain: A CFG++ version of 2S that shifts x by the guidance gap before each exponential step. Nothing is dispatched to RF, so flow models run the −log σ formula. Reading the code shows the second update mixes values from two different model calls.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
get_ancestral_step: σ_up=min(σ', η·√(σ'²(σ²−σ'²)/σ²)); σ_down=√(σ'²−σ_up²); η=0 returns (σ', 0).
t=−log σ, t_d=−log σ_down, h=t_d−t, s=t+h/2.
U₁,D₁ from first call. x₂=(σ(s)/σ)(x+D₁−U₁)−(e^{−h/2}−1)D₁. Second call at σ(s) gives D₂ and overwrites stored U to U₂.
x'=(σ_down/σ)(x+D₁−U₂)−(e^{−h}−1)D₂. If σ'>0: x'+=n·s_noise·σ_up (s_noise×noise_scale).

props.stages: 2 (2 network passes each, cfg=1 shortcut off); 1 when σ_down=0
props.final_sigma0: Explicit: σ_down=0 gives x'=D+d·0=D.
props.flow_const: No CONST branch, no RF dispatch; σ_up uses the VE get_ancestral_step on flow σ.

entries.name: DPM++ 3M SDE
entries.plain: Extends the multistep SDE to two previous x0 values for a third-order correction, building up from first to second order over the early steps. One model call per step, Brownian noise.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
λ=half-logSNR, h, h_η, α' as in 2M SDE. x'=(σ'/σ)e^{−hη}x+α'(1−e^{−h_η})D.
φ₂=(e^{−h_η}−1)/h_η+1, φ₃=φ₂/h_η−½.
Two histories: r₀=h₁/h, r₁=h₂/h; d₀=(D−D₁)/r₀; d₀₁=(D₁−D₂)/r₁; d₁=d₀+(d₀−d₀₁)r₀/(r₀+r₁); d₂=(d₀−d₀₁)/(r₀+r₁); x'+=α'φ₂d₁−α'φ₃d₂.
One history: x'+=α'φ₂(D−D₁)/(h₁/h).
Noise: x'+=n(σ,σ')σ'√(1−e^{−2hη})s_noise.

props.flow_const: half-logSNR via sigma_to_half_log_snr: λ=−log σ normally, λ=log((1−σ)/σ) on CONST; α=σe^{λ} (1 normally, 1−σ on CONST). First σ≥1 on CONST replaced by percent_to_sigma(1e-4); s_noise×noise_scale.

entries.name: DPM++ SDE
entries.plain: A two-stage stochastic DPM++ method: noisy intermediate stage, model call, then a blended x0 for the full step with more noise. Noise comes from a Brownian tree seeded from the run seed, so each draw is a function of its σ interval. Costs two model calls per step.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
λ=half-logSNR, h=λ'−λ, λ₁=λ+r·h, σ₁=σ(λ₁), r default ½, fac=1/(2r).
Stage 1: sd,su=get_ancestral_step(e^{−λ},e^{−λ₁},η); h₁=−log sd−λ; x₂=(α₁/α)e^{−h₁}x−α₁(e^{−h₁}−1)D; if η,s_noise>0 add α₁·n(σ,σ₁)·s_noise·su. D₂ at σ₁.
Stage 2: sd,su for e^{−λ}→e^{−λ'}; h₂=−log sd−λ; D̄=(1−fac)D+fac·D₂; x'=(α'/α)e^{−h₂}x−α'(e^{−h₂}−1)D̄; add α'·n(σ,σ')·s_noise·su.

props.final_sigma0: Explicit: σ'=0 returns D.
props.flow_const: half-logSNR via sigma_to_half_log_snr: λ=−log σ normally, λ=log((1−σ)/σ) on CONST; α=σe^{λ} (1 normally, 1−σ on CONST). First σ≥1 on CONST replaced by percent_to_sigma(1e-4); s_noise×noise_scale.

entries.name: DPM-2
entries.plain: A midpoint method: step to the geometric middle of σ and σ', evaluate, and use that slope for the whole step. Two model calls per step. In the KSampler path the schedule is built one step longer and the second-to-last sigma is dropped.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
σ_m=exp(lerp(log σ̂, log σ', ½)); x₂=x+d(σ_m−σ̂); D₂ at σ_m; d₂=(x₂−D₂)/σ_m; x'=x+d₂(σ'−σ̂).
Optional churn before the model call (defaults off; no core node exposes s_churn): γ=min(s_churn/N, √2−1) when s_tmin≤σ≤s_tmax, N=len(sigmas)−1; σ̂=σ(1+γ); x←x+ε·s_noise·√(σ̂²−σ²), ε from torch.randn_like (global RNG, not the seeded noise sampler). All later σ in the step are σ̂.

props.prediction_space: σ with midpoint in log σ
props.final_sigma0: Explicit: σ'=0 one Euler step, equals D.
props.flow_const: No branch. Midpoint is in log σ on every model, not logit.

entries.name: DPM-Solver Adaptive (12/23)
entries.plain: An embedded pair (order 2 inside order 3, or 1 inside 2) runs with a PID step-size controller. The step count is not used at all: only the first and the last non-zero σ, and it stops there instead of jumping to zero. Rejected attempts cost model calls and the time taken varies with the error tolerance.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
t=−log σ; attempt interval [s,s+h_pid]. Order 3: x_low=DPM-2 with r₁=⅓, x_high=DPM-3. Order 2: x_low=DPM-1, x_high=DPM-2.
δ=max(atol, rtol·max(|x_low|,|x_prev|)); err=‖(x_low−x_high)/δ‖₂/√numel.
PID factor from inverse errors, passed through 1+atan(f−1); accepted if factor≥accept_safety (0.81); h always multiplied by factor.
On accept x'=x_high(+su·s_noise·n if η>0), x_prev=x_low.

props.stages: order per attempt (3 or 2), including rejected attempts; total unknown ahead of time
props.final_sigma0: Wrapper replaces a 0 end with sigmas[-2]; stops there with residual noise, no denoise-to-zero.
props.flow_const: No CONST branch.

entries.name: DPM-Solver-Fast
entries.plain: The DPM-Solver fixed-budget driver. It takes the requested step count as a model-call budget, spreads order-3 stages uniformly in log σ, and ignores the schedule apart from its end points. It stops at the last non-zero sigma instead of jumping to zero.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
t=−log σ; h=t'−t. N=len(sigmas)−1 is the NFE budget; m=⌊N/3⌋+1 uniform t-intervals; orders [3]*(m−2)+[2,1] if 3|N else [3]*(m−1)+[N%3].
ε=(x−D)/σ. Order 1: x'=x−σ'(e^h−1)ε.
Order 2 (r₁=½): u=x−σ(s₁)(e^{r₁h}−1)ε; x'=x−σ'(e^h−1)ε−(σ'/(2r₁))(e^h−1)(ε₁−ε).
Order 3 (r₁=⅓,r₂=⅔): u₁ as above; u₂=x−σ(s₂)(e^{r₂h}−1)ε−σ(s₂)(r₂/r₁)((e^{r₂h}−1)/(r₂h)−1)(ε₁−ε); x'=x−σ'(e^h−1)ε−(σ'/r₂)((e^h−1)/h−1)(ε₂−ε).

props.stages: 1,2 or 3 per interval; total exactly N
props.final_sigma0: Wrapper replaces a 0 end with sigmas[-2]; loop ends there, no denoise-to-zero, residual noise at that σ remains.
props.flow_const: No CONST branch; uses −log σ on all models. First-order term is the same Euler line.

entries.name: ER-SDE
entries.plain: Extended Reverse-Time SDE solver: first-order core with second and third stage corrections from history, using numerically integrated terms under a configurable noise scaler. The node can switch that scaler to reverse-time SDE or to plain ODE, and η controls it. One model call per step.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
ρ=σ/α=e^{−λ}, half-logSNR λ. ψ default ρ(e^{ρ^0.3}+10). r=ψ(ρ')/ψ(ρ), dt=ρ'−ρ, α'=σ'/ρ', α=σ/ρ.
Stage 1: x'=(α'/α)r·x+α'(1−r)D.
Stage 2 (i≥1): grid ρ_j=ρ'+j(−dt/200), S=Σ(1/ψ(ρ_j))(−dt/200); D₁=(D−D_old)/(ρ−ρ_{i−1}); x'+=α'(dt+Sψ(ρ'))D₁.
Stage 3 (i≥2): S_u=Σ((ρ_j−ρ)/ψ(ρ_j))(−dt/200); D₂=(D₁−D₁,old)/((ρ−ρ_{i−2})/2); x'+=α'(dt²/2+S_uψ(ρ'))D₂.
Noise: x'+=α'·n·s_noise·√(ρ'²−ρ²r²), NaN→0.
Node scalers: ER-SDE ψ=ρ(e^{ρ^0.3}+10)^η; reverse-time ψ=ρ^{η+1}; ODE ψ=ρ with s_noise=0.

entries.name: Euler
entries.plain: The plain first-order step: ask the model for the clean image, compute the slope toward it, walk to the next noise level. With the default churn of 0 it is deterministic and costs one model call per step. It is the simplest solver in core, and several other entries reduce to this line.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ.

entries.name: Exponential Heun 2 (x0)
entries.plain: Thin preset of the SEEDS-2 code with r=1 and no noise, giving a deterministic exponential Heun method working on x0 in logSNR. The second model call is made at the next sigma rather than a midpoint. Two calls per step like Heun.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
λ=half-logSNR, h=λ(σ')−λ(σ), α=σe^{λ}.
x₂=(σ'/σ)x−α'·(e^{−h}−1)·D, D₂=model(x₂,σ').
b₂=(e^{−h}−1+h)/(−h) [ei_h_phi_2(−h)/r, r=1]; b₁=(e^{−h}−1)−b₂; x'=(σ'/σ)x−α'(b₁D+b₂D₂).

props.final_sigma0: Explicit (seeds_2): σ'=0 returns D.
props.flow_const: Half-logSNR via sigma_to_half_log_snr (logit on CONST) with first σ≥1 offset to percent_to_sigma(1e-4).

entries.name: Exponential Heun 2 (x0, SDE)
entries.plain: Same preset with noise on (η=1). Because r=1 the intermediate stage already sits at σ', so the noise drawn for it is carried straight through to the final state. Default noise is plain seeded Gaussian, not a Brownian tree.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ.

h_η=h(1+η); x₂=(σ'/σ)e^{−hη}x−α'(e^{−h_η}−1)D; x' uses b₂=ei_h_phi_2(−h_η), b₁=(e^{−h_η}−1)−b₂.

entries.name: Gradient Estimation
entries.plain: Euler plus a correction from the change in slope between steps, scaled by γ=2 by default. One call per step, deterministic. With γ=2 the correction makes the step use 2d−d_old from step 2.

x_e=x+d·dt, dt=σ'−σ. From i≥1: x'=x_e+(γ−1)(d−d_old)dt, γ=2.

entries.name: Gradient Estimation CFG++
entries.plain: Same correction with slope taken from the unconditional prediction, and the base step using the CFG++ form. The cfg=1 shortcut is off. No α factors, so on flow models it differs from euler_cfg_pp.

Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
d_u=(x−U)/σ; x_e=D+σ'd_u; from i≥1: x'=x_e+(γ−1)(d_u−d_u,old)(σ'−σ), γ=2.

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Heun
entries.plain: Predicts with Euler, re-evaluates the model at the landing point, and averages the two slopes. That second call is why it costs about twice as many model calls as Euler for the same step count. Deterministic unless churn is used.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
x₂=x+d·dt, dt=σ'−σ̂; D₂=model(x₂,σ'); d₂=(x₂−D₂)/σ'; x'=x+dt·(d+d₂)/2.
Optional churn before the model call (defaults off; no core node exposes s_churn): γ=min(s_churn/N, √2−1) when s_tmin≤σ≤s_tmax, N=len(sigmas)−1; σ̂=σ(1+γ); x←x+ε·s_noise·√(σ̂²−σ²), ε from torch.randn_like (global RNG, not the seeded noise sampler). All later σ in the step are σ̂.

props.stages: 2; 1 when σ'=0 (total 2N−1 if schedule ends in 0)
props.final_sigma0: Explicit: σ'=0 falls to one Euler step, which equals D.
props.flow_const: No branch; works from d, as in Euler.

entries.name: Heun++2
entries.plain: Looks two schedule entries ahead, evaluates the model at both, and blends three slopes with weights set by how far σ has fallen from the very first sigma. Weight shifts toward the first slope as σ drops, so late steps move toward Euler. Costs three model calls for most steps but moves x only one step each time.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
x₂=x+d·dt, dt=σ'−σ̂; D₂ at σ'. x₃=x₂+d₂(σ''−σ'), D₃ at σ''=sigmas[i+2].
w₂=σ'/(3σ₀), w₃=σ''/(3σ₀), w₁=1−w₂−w₃, σ₀=sigmas[0]. x'=x+dt(w₁d+w₂d₂+w₃d₃).
Near end (σ''=s_end): two-slope w₂=σ'/(2σ₀), w₁=1−w₂. Last step (σ'=s_end): Euler.
Optional churn before the model call (defaults off; no core node exposes s_churn): γ=min(s_churn/N, √2−1) when s_tmin≤σ≤s_tmax, N=len(sigmas)−1; σ̂=σ(1+γ); x←x+ε·s_noise·√(σ̂²−σ²), ε from torch.randn_like (global RNG, not the seeded noise sampler). All later σ in the step are σ̂.

props.stages: 3; 2 on penultimate; 1 on last (total 3N−3 for N≥2)
props.final_sigma0: Test is against s_end=sigmas[-1], not zero. With σ'=0 the Euler step equals D. With a nonzero end the last step is still Euler.
props.flow_const: No branch; weights use raw σ.

entries.name: iPNDM
entries.plain: Improved pseudo-numerical method: Adams-Bashforth history on slopes with fixed textbook coefficients, up to order 4, one call per step. The coefficients assume even step size in σ, whatever the schedule actually is. The sibling ipndm_v adapts them.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
Order=min(4,i+1). x'=x+(σ'−σ)·G, with G=d; (3d−d₁)/2; (23d−16d₁+5d₂)/12; (55d−59d₁+37d₂−9d₃)/24.

entries.name: iPNDM-v (variable step)
entries.plain: The variable-step version of iPNDM: same history idea, but coefficients depend on the ratios of recent step sizes in σ. Uneven steps are therefore reflected in the weights. One call per step.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
Order 2: h=σ'−σ, h₁=σ−σ_{i−1}; c₁=(2+h/h₁)/2, c₂=−(h/h₁)/2; x'=x+h(c₁d+c₂d₁).
Orders 3 and 4 add terms in h, h₁, h₂, h₃ through temp, temp1, temp2 at lines 1253–1269; form is x'=x+h·Σc_jd_j.

entries.name: LCM
entries.plain: Each step jumps directly to the model's x0 and then adds fresh noise for the next level, using the model's own noise scaling. The code states no model requirement. A node adds a noise multiplier ramp and a clamp on the injected noise.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
x_d=D. If σ'>0: n, optionally clamped to ±noise_clip_std·std(n); multiplied by s_i=s_noise+(s_noise_end−s_noise)·i/(N−1); x'=model_sampling.noise_scaling(σ',n,x_d) with max_denoise=False.
EPS-like: x'=x_d+σ'n. CONST: x'=σ'·(noise_scale·n)+(1−σ')x_d.

entries.name: LCM Upscale (node only)
entries.plain: An LCM-style loop that enlarges the latent on a schedule between steps, so sampling and upscaling happen together. Not in the sampler list; only reached through its node. It adds noise with a raw VE formula rather than the model's noise scaling.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
x_d=D; if i<len(upscales): resize of x_d by upscale_method to orig×upscales[i]; upscales=linspace(1,total_upscale,K)[1:], K default max(len(sigmas)//2+1,2).
If σ'>0: x'=x_d+σ'·ε, ε from torch.randn_like.

entries.name: LMS (linear multistep)
entries.plain: Reuses slopes from previous steps instead of extra model calls: one call per step, up to fourth order by default. Coefficients are computed by numerically integrating Lagrange polynomials over the actual σ spacing. Deterministic.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
cur_order=min(i+1,order), order default 4. c_j=∫_{σ}^{σ'} ∏_{k≠j}(τ−σ_{i−k})/(σ_{i−j}−σ_{i−k}) dτ via scipy quad, epsrel 1e-4.
x'=x+Σ_j c_j·d_{i−j}.

props.flow_const: No branch; slopes d are used as in Euler.

entries.name: RES Multistep
entries.plain: Second-order exponential multistep on x0, one call per step; the first step and last step are Euler. Calls the shared res_multistep function with η=0. Deterministic.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
t=−log σ, φ₁(z)=(e^z−1)/z, φ₂(z)=(φ₁(z)−1)/z. t_d=−log σ_down, h=t_d−t, c₂=(t_{i−1}−t_old)/h where t_old=−log(previous σ_down). b₁=φ₁(−h)−φ₂(−h)/c₂, b₂=φ₂(−h)/c₂ (NaN→0).
σ_down=σ'. First step or σ'=0: x'=x+d(σ'−σ). Otherwise x'=e^{−h}x+h(b₁D+b₂D_old).

entries.plain: RES aimed at σ_down, with fresh noise added back to σ' each step. The multistep history uses the previous σ_down rather than the σ the noise landed on. Default η=1.

Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ.

entries.name: SA-Solver
entries.plain: Stochastic Adams predictor-corrector: uses a window of past x0 predictions with coefficients from exponential integrals, and noise only inside a chosen band of σ. One model call per step, because the corrector reuses the prediction at the predicted state. The node lets the band and orders be set.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
tau: τ(σ)=η if start_σ≥σ≥end_σ else 0; default start=percent_to_sigma(0.2), end=percent_to_sigma(0.8), η=1.
Predictor toward σ': b from solving a Vandermonde system in λ over the exponential integrals (compute_exponential_coeffs), scaled by α'; x_p=(σ'/σ)e^{−τ²h}x+Σb_kD_k; noise e=n·σ'√(1−e^{−2τ²h})·s_noise; x_p+=e.
Corrector at current i: x=(σ/σ_{i−1})e^{−τ²h}x+Σb_kD_k (includes D at x_p)+e reused from the predictor. Corrector is skipped at i=0, and at σ'=0 unless PECE.
Orders: predictor default 3, corrector default 4; limited by history, and lowered toward the end if the schedule ends in 0.

props.final_sigma0: Explicit: σ'=0 sets x_pred=D, returned as the result, after the last evaluation.
props.flow_const: half-logSNR via sigma_to_half_log_snr: λ=−log σ normally, λ=log((1−σ)/σ) on CONST; α=σe^{λ} (1 normally, 1−σ on CONST). First σ≥1 on CONST replaced by percent_to_sigma(1e-4); s_noise×noise_scale.

entries.name: SEEDS-2
entries.plain: Two-stage stochastic exponential solver on x0 in half-logSNR, from the SEEDS paper. Noise is drawn per sub-segment and the stage noise is carried forward with a decay factor, rather than drawn independently. Default phi_1, r=0.5. Uses plain seeded Gaussian, not a Brownian tree.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
h=λ'−λ, h_η=h(1+η), λ₁=lerp(λ,λ',r), σ₁,α₁. φ₁(z)=e^z−1; φ₂(z)=(e^z−1−z)/z.
x₂=(σ₁/σ)e^{−rhη}x−α₁φ₁(−rh_η)D; e₁=√(1−e^{−2rhη})n; x₂+=e₁σ₁s_noise. D₂ at σ₁.
phi_1: D̄=lerp(D,D₂,1/(2r)); x'=(σ'/σ)e^{−hη}x−α'φ₁(−h_η)D̄.
phi_2: b₂=φ₂(−h_η)/r, b₁=φ₁(−h_η)−b₂; x'=(σ'/σ)e^{−hη}x−α'(b₁D+b₂D₂).
s=(r−1)hη; e₂=e₁e^{s}+√(1−e^{2s})n'; x'+=e₂σ's_noise.

props.final_sigma0: Explicit: σ'=0 returns D and continues.
props.flow_const: half-logSNR via sigma_to_half_log_snr: λ=−log σ normally, λ=log((1−σ)/σ) on CONST; α=σe^{λ} (1 normally, 1−σ on CONST). First σ≥1 on CONST replaced by percent_to_sigma(1e-4); s_noise×noise_scale.

entries.name: SEEDS-3
entries.plain: Three-stage version of SEEDS. It makes three model calls per step and chains stage noise across the sub-segments. Final x uses the first and third x0 predictions; the second feeds only the third stage. No dedicated node, so r₁=⅓, r₂=⅔, η=1 come from defaults.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
λ₁,λ₂=lerp at r₁=⅓, r₂=⅔. x₂=(σ₁/σ)e^{−r₁hη}x−α₁φ₁(−r₁h_η)D+e₁σ₁s_noise; D₂ at σ₁.
a₃₂=(r₂/r₁)φ₂(−r₂h_η), a₃₁=φ₁(−r₂h_η)−a₃₂; x₃=(σ₂/σ)e^{−r₂hη}x−α₂(a₃₁D+a₃₂D₂)+e₂σ₂s_noise; D₃ at σ₂.
b₃=φ₂(−h_η)/r₂, b₁=φ₁(−h_η)−b₃; x'=(σ'/σ)e^{−hη}x−α'(b₁D+b₃D₃)+e₃σ's_noise.

entries.name: UniPC (B1, bh1)
entries.plain: Unified predictor-corrector working on x0 in VP coordinates. Each step's corrector call also serves as the history for the next step, which gives one model call per step at up to third order. The default bh1 variant uses B(h)=h with a sign flip.
entries.math:
Symbols: x current latent; σ=sigmas[i]; σ'=sigmas[i+1]; D=denoised (x0 prediction after CFG); U=uncond_denoised; d=(x−D)/σ. 
VP-wrapped: x_vp=x/√(1+σ²), ε=(x_ve−D)/σ, data prediction m=(x_vp−s ε)/a, a=1/√(1+σ²), s=σa, λ=log(a/s)=−log σ.
h=λ_t−λ_0; x*=(s_t/s_0)x−a_t(e^{−h}−1)m₀; r_k=(λ_k−λ_0)/h; D_k=(m_k−m₀)/r_k.
Predictor: x_p=x*−a_tB(h)Σρ_p,kD_k. Corrector: m_t=model(x_p,t); x'=x*−a_tB(h)(Σρ_c,kD_k+ρ_c,last(m_t−m₀)).
ρ from solving R·ρ=b; order 2 predictor uses ρ=½ directly; order 1 corrector uses ρ=½.
Variant: B(h)=−h (hh).
Driver order=min(3,len(sigmas)−2). Step 0 evaluates only and does not move x; last index does 2 updates, the second without corrector. Total calls=N, total updates=N; orders lowered at end.
End: sigma 0 replaced with 0.001; after loop x/=a(last).

entries.name: AccelDiff AdaptiveDiff step skipping
entries.plain: Forks core solvers and tracks mean absolute change of the latent per step. When the second difference of that change is small relative to the last change, it reuses the previous x0 prediction with no model call. A guard forces a real call after max_skip_steps skips.
entries.math: Δ_k = mean|x_k − x_{k−1}|. Skip next if |(Δ_k + Δ_{k−2})/2 − Δ_{k−1}| ≤ threshold·Δ_{k−1}. Force a call if len(mask)>4 and none of the last max_skip_steps masks are true. On skip denoised = last real denoised (stale x0, not extrapolated). First 4 steps always call. Defaults max_skip_steps=3, threshold=0.01.

entries.name: AccelDiff EasyCache solver fork
entries.plain: Forks core solvers with an EasyCache state object that accumulates a predicted-change estimate; while it stays under a threshold, model calls return x plus a cached output delta. This is in the sampler loop itself, not a model patch like core EasyCache nodes.
entries.math: cache = denoised − x from the last real call. k = |Δdenoised|/|Δinput| between real calls. err += k·|x − x_prev|/|prev_output|. If err < threshold: denoised = x + cache. Else real call, err=0. First ret_steps and last step always real. Defaults threshold=0.025, ret_steps=5. Multi-eval solvers share the should_calc decision over one step.

entries.name: AccelDiff SADA step skipping
entries.plain: Forks core solvers and adds a stability test: after each step it compares the real next state against a three-term predictor, and if a momentum indicator is non-positive it skips the next model call. The skipped call uses an extrapolated x0 or a Lagrange fit over stored x0 anchors. It trades model calls for approximation error.
entries.math:
f = (x−x0)/σ. pred = x + Δσ·(0.625 f + 0.75 f₋₁ − 0.375 f₋₂). residual = x_next − pred. accel = (f−f₋₁) − (f₋₁−f₋₂). momentum = mean(residual·accel).
Skip next call if momentum ≤ 0 and acc_start ≤ i < acc_end, at most max_interval in a row. Replacement x0 = pred − σ_next·f, or Lagrange interpolation over lagrange_term stored x0 values once i ≥ lagrange_step (then skip when i % lagrange_int ≠ 0).
The base solver's update then runs unchanged on the substituted x0.

entries.name: AccelDiff ZEUS step skipping
entries.plain: Forks core solvers with a fixed modular skip pattern: steps whose index mod denominator is in a set trigger a skip of the next call, and the derivative is linearly extrapolated in ODE-derivative space. Real outputs alone stay in the history. It is schedule-based, not error-based.

Skip next if i % denominator ∈ modular and acc_start ≤ i < acc_end, with cons_skip < max_interval. Defaults denominator=3, modular={0,1}, acc_start=10, acc_end=45, max_interval=4.
d̂ = d₋₁ + (d₋₁ − d₋₂); x0̂ = x − σ·d̂. caching_mode reuse_interp reuses the same d̂ on odd consecutive skip counts; interp_all recomputes it. Optional Lagrange on x0 past lagrange_step.

audit.note: Formula matches the line, but "linearly extrapolated" holds only for the first skip in a run. A skipped step shifts history and re-appends the latest real d, so prev_d[-2]==prev_d[-1] (jiajianxie__ComfyUI-AccelDiff/sampler/zeus.py:188-199). A second consecutive skip therefore gives d̂ = d₋₁ + 0, plain reuse (zeus.py:168). With defaults {0,1}/3 runs are at most 2 skips long, so every second skip is reuse and interp_all "recomputes" the same stale d. acc_start is also clamped to ≥3 (line 111).

entries.name: Adept ancestral solver
entries.plain: Euler ancestral with optional time-varying eta, a phase noise multiplier, a modified derivative, and an adaptive noise calibration. Adaptive noise can restart the whole run once it has measured enough samples.
entries.math: η_t=η·1.08 (p<0.3), ·0.95 (p<0.7), else ·1.02. σ↑=min(σ′,η_t√(σ′²(σ²−σ′²)/σ²)), σ↓=√(σ′²−σ↑²). x=x+d(σ↓−σ)+n·s·σ↑. Phase noise: multiplier by piecewise progress. Adaptive: excess=(|Δx0_k|/|Δx0_{k−1}|)/(σ′/σ), collected by bins; after calibrating, x reset to x_initial and i=0.

entries.name: Adept solver
entries.plain: A deterministic multistep in sigma space with a compensated derivative history and an optional Heun corrector. Adds clamps on extreme derivatives, NaN recovery, and dynamic thresholding when cond_scale exceeds 7.
entries.math:
Order 2: d̃=d+c(d−d₋₁), c from compute_compensation_ratio(h,i,N). Order 3: r=h₀/h₁, c0=1+r/2, c1=−r/2, c2=0, normalized, d̃=c0d+c1d₋₁+c2d₋₂. x_pred=x+d̃dt.
Corrector: x=x+½(d+d_pred)dt, except last step. Dynamic thresholding at percentile 0.995 on x0 when cond_scale>7. Clamp |d| at 1000(1+σ/10).

entries.name: Akashic solver
entries.plain: Marked experimental in its own print. A sigma-space Adams-Bashforth step inspired by SA-Solver with a tau-controlled noise, plus phase schedules for tau, eta and noise, a SMEA factor and a Native Detail Boost option. It is not the core sa_solver algorithm.
entries.math: τ_t=compute_tau_eqvae(p,τ,phase). η_t by piecewise p. s_eff=s·η_t·smea(p)·phase multiplier. sa_solver_step: dt=σ′−σ, r=min(|dt/h_prev|,2), AB combination of d history up to order, noise via τ. Optional combat_cfg_drift on x0.

entries.name: Clyb BDF
entries.plain: A predictor-corrector that uses a faux state at the lower sigma. Every step makes exactly one model call: step 0 calls at σᵢ only, and later steps reuse the prior x0 and call at σ↓. It averages two x0 predictions and then passes them through a scaling function; the projection and default atan2sin modes do not keep that average as-is.
entries.math:
σ↓=√(σᵢ₊₁²/(1+log(1+|σᵢ₊₁−σᵢ|)η)), σ↑=√(σᵢ²−σ↓²).
x̃=lerp(x0₁,x,σ↓/σᵢ); x0₂=model(x̃,σ↓); D=(x0₁+x0₂)/2.
projection: D′=D·(x0₂·D)/D² elementwise. atan2sin: D′=sin(atan x0₂)/cos(atan D). atan2sin+projection (default): both.
x=lerp(D′,x,σ↓/σᵢ). Noise: VP +n·s·σ↑; flow: x=(α_{i+1}/α↓)x+n·s·√(σᵢ₊₁²−σ↓²α²_{i+1}/α↓²). prev x0 := D′.

entries.name: Clyb CFG++ sampler wrapper

entries.name: Clyb geometric extrapolation
entries.plain: A three-evaluation single-step: evaluates at the geometric mean sigmas between current and σ↓ and extrapolates x0 to σ↓ with Newton divided differences. Three model calls per step.
entries.math:
σ_g1=√(σ·σ↓), σ_g2=√(σ_g1·σ↓). x0₁=model(x,σ). x_m1=lerp(x0₁,x,σ_g1/σ). x0₂=model(x_m1,σ_g1). x0_pred=x0₂+s₁₂(σ↓−σ_g1). x_m2=lerp(x0_pred,x_m1,σ_g2/σ_g1). x0₃=model(x_m2,σ_g2).
x0_f=x0₃+d2(σ↓−σ_g2)+d2_div(σ↓−σ_g2)(σ↓−σ_g1) except on final step. x=lerp(x0_f,x_m2,σ↓/σ_g2). Noise as Clyb BDF.

entries.name: DDRK flow-correct ancestral and restart jump
entries.plain: Noise injection that respects flow matching, where the signal must be scaled as well as adding noise. On EDM it uses the usual split, and restart jumps reuse this same flow-correct form when moving up in sigma.
entries.math:
EDM: σ_up=min(σ_n, η√(σ_n²(σ²−σ_n²))/σ), σ_down=√(σ_n²−σ_up²).
Flow: σ_d=σ_n(1+(σ_n/σ−1)η), ratio=(1−σ_n)/(1−σ_d), renoise=√(σ_n²−(σ_d·ratio)²).
Restart up: x′=x·(1−σ′)/(1−σ)+n·√(σ′²−(σ(1−σ′)/(1−σ))²).
SDE noise is multiplied by flat_mask=(1−edge)·flatness, flatness=1−sigmoid(2·z(local var)), window 5.

entries.name: DDRK HC2 and HC3 multistep (full read of hc2_step, extends ddrk-omega)
entries.plain: A one-call multistep solver in the same family as DPM++ 2M and 3M, with guards: the higher-order correction is limited elementwise to the size of the first-order move. HC3 adds a trust factor that shrinks the extrapolation when consecutive slopes disagree, and a free UniC-like correction of the previous step after the next model call. The code comments report a bench on an analytic mixture, not on images.
entries.math:
λ=−log σ (EDM) or log((1−σ)/σ) (flow). h=λ_next−λ; α=1 EDM, 1−σ_next flow.
First order F=(1−e^(−h))(D−x) EDM, (1−σ_next/σ)(D−x) flow.
r=(D−D₋₁)/h₋₁. c₂=r α(h−1+e^(−h)).
Order 3 if history and ratio |c₃|/|c₂|<1, dd=(r−r₋₁)/(h₋₁+h₋₂): c₃=dd α(h²−2h+2−2e^(−h)+h₋₁(h−1+e^(−h))), clamped to ±|c₂|.
x⁺=x+F+clamp(c₂[+c₃], ±κ|F|). Default order 2, κ=1.
HC3 (hc2_step with damping and free_corrector on): θ=clamp(1−‖r−r₋₁‖/(‖r‖+‖r₋₁‖),0,1), r←θ r, dd←θ²dd.
Free corrector at the next step: x+=α φ₂(h)(D_now−D)/h [+ dd·α(2φ₃(h)−hφ₂(h))] − previous applied correction; skipped if the latent did not arrive by that step.
Optional paid corrector: if activity>corrector_thresh, one extra model call at x⁺.
max_order≥3 bootstraps the first step with Heun.

entries.name: DDRK Omega sampler
entries.plain: One sampler for Flow Matching and EDM, routing steps by phase: integrator choice from Euler, Heun, RK4, or its own one-call multistep HC2 and HC3. Layered with a latent fuse (SABER), ancestral renoise, restart inserts, sharpening and a schedule adapter. Auto mode tweaks params by step count.
entries.math:
HC2: exponential-style update in λ=−log σ (EDM) or log((1−σ)/σ) (flow), with φ₂ weights and a derivative of x0 from history; limiter_kappa bounds it. free_corrector redoes the last step by interpolation, UniC-style, at zero cost.
Phases 1,2,3 via AdaptivePhaseRouter; auto picks rk4 for curvature>0.15 with ≥10 steps, heun for >0.05, else hc2.
Flow SDE in phase 1: _ancestral_split_flow. Restart: _insert_restarts in window [0.10,0.35]σ_max. Only key routing and hc2 head were read, tableaux not checked.

entries.name: DDRK SABER2 fuse and perceptual sharpen
entries.plain: Two latent filters that run inside the sampler. SABER on images blurs flat areas of the latent with a 3×3 average, keeping edges. On video, it pulls unstable pixels toward a running average of past steps, not past frames. The sharpen adds fine and coarse detail back, weighted away from flat areas.
entries.math:
z(t)=(t−mean)/std per batch item; gate g(t)=sigmoid(2z).
Image: w=f(1−g((|Lap₃x|+|x−blur₅x|)/2)); x←x(1−w)+blur₃(x)·w. f=fusion 0.35.
Video: chaos=g(var over last 3 step latents); e=.7e+.3x; x←x(1−chaos·f)+e·chaos·f.
Sharpen: x+=s(.6 clamp(d₃)+.4 clamp(d₅)), d_k=(x−blur_k)·(1−flatness), clamp ±.6, flatness weight off on the final step.
Dynamic threshold used elsewhere: only under σ≤ratio·σ_max; pixels above the 99.5th percentile of |x̂₀| are pulled to that value, a per-pixel cap with no division by s.

entries.name: DDRK step-count overrides
entries.plain: Rules that change the requested settings based on step count and model family. Some of them run even with auto off, and the code prints a message saying so. Below is what actually fires.
entries.math:
Flow, auto on: steps≤10 → SABER 0, SDE 0, momentum 0, sharp≤.12, auto→hc2. Steps≤20 → SABER≤.05, SDE 0, momentum≤.10, sharp≤.15.
Any mode: steps≤6 and integrator not hc2/hc3 → euler. EDM steps≤10 and rk4 → heun.
Phase split: p1≥60%, p2≤22% EDM; p1≤55%, p2≥35% flow. Auto picks: phase 1 by curvature (>.15 and ≥10 steps rk4; >.05 heun; else hc2); with no previous x0 yet, flow ≥10 steps rk4 if σ>.3σmax else heun, otherwise heun. Phase 2 heun if ≥8 steps else euler, phase 3 hc2.

entries.name: DPM++ 3M SDE dynamic eta
entries.plain: Core 3M SDE with no structural change except eta follows a cosine anneal across the step index. Starts more stochastic and ends more deterministic with default values.
entries.math: ηᵢ = η_min + ½(η_max−η_min)(1+cos(π·i/(N−1))), N=len(sigmas). Otherwise the 3M SDE update, with h_η=h(ηᵢ+1) and Brownian noise.

entries.name: DPM++ dual SDE momentumized
entries.plain: Core dpmpp_sde's two-stage midpoint with momentum blended into both stage updates, then a further 3M-style SDE history correction on top. Two model calls per step plus history.
entries.math: s=t+rh, fac=1/(2r). x₂ = (σ(s_)/σ(t))x − v₂((e^{t−s_}−1)·x0₁) + su·n. D=(1−fac)x0₁ + fac·x0₂. x ← (σ(t_next_)/σ(t))x − v₁((e^{t−t_next_}−1)·D). Then history correction with φ terms using h_η, blended by a third velocity. Final noise n·su. v = m·(t + off)·v_prev + (1 − m·(t + off))·diff with t = σᵢ/σ_max, off = −m/2, m = momentum.

entries.name: DPM++ Ns (Chebyshev-Lobatto collocation)
entries.plain: Single-step p-stage solver: places collocation nodes at Chebyshev-Lobatto points inside the step, evaluates the model at each, and integrates the interpolant.
entries.math: nodes=chebyshev_lobatto_nodes(p,h_η). τ₀=0, x_k=collocation_step(x,τ,x0s,τ_k); σ_k=e^{−(t+τ_k)}; x0_k=model. x=collocation_step(x,τ,x0s,h_η). none, ancestral or sde noise.

entries.name: DX policy (grid or polynomial)
entries.plain: The model predicts N clean-image estimates laid out across one time segment. The policy interpolates between them, or uses them as polynomial coefficients. It ignores where x has moved when choosing x̂₀, unlike GMFlow.
entries.math:
x̂₀ᵢ=x_src−σ_src·outᵢ. raw t=σ/(s+(1−s)σ).
Grid: τ=(raw t−raw_dst)/segment, linear interpolation over the N points.
Polynomial: first coefficient kept, others stored as differences from it; x̂₀=Σ (raw_src−raw t)ⁱ cᵢ.
π=(x−x̂₀)/σ.

entries.name: Dynamic oversampling
entries.plain: Euler with extra crop-level model calls at finer resolution on regions chosen by a high-pass FFT of x0. Each selected crop is upscaled, renoised, predicted at √2σ, and pasted back.
entries.math: filt=ifft2(mask·fft2(x0)). Focal crops h//4 with score >1000. subx=interp(crop, resolution_mult); subx+=randn·(1−√2)σ̂; x0_sub=model(subx,√2σ̂); interp back, blend by sub_weight.

entries.name: Euler A2
entries.plain: Rectified-flow ancestral step that draws two noise samples each step, averages, then extrapolates the merged noise away from the deterministic base. The default extrapolation brings the total noise variance back close to one.
entries.math:
ratio=1+(σᵢ₊₁/σᵢ−1)η. σ↓=σᵢ₊₁·ratio. D=(σ↓/σᵢ)x+(1−σ↓/σᵢ)x0. base=(α′/α↓)D. c=√max(0,σᵢ₊₁²−σ↓²α′²/α↓²). p_k=base+n_k·s·c. merged=½(p₁+p₂). x=merged+e(merged−base). Default e=0.425.
So noise = (1+e)/2·(n₁+n₂)·s·c, variance (1+e)²/2·(s·c)² ≈ 1.015(s·c)².

entries.name: Euler ancestral dancing
entries.plain: An Euler ancestral step leaps to a sigma several steps ahead, then a second ancestral step with the same x0 returns to the next planned sigma. With eta_dance above 0, the split collapses: x lands on x0 and is re-noised to the next sigma, based on reading the code. One model call per step.
entries.math: (σ↓,σ↑)=ancestral(σᵢ,σ_{i+leap},η). x+=d·(σ↓−σᵢ)+n·s·σ↑. Then (σ↓₂,σ↑₂)=ancestral(σ_{i+leap},σᵢ₊₁,η_dance); d₂=(x−x0)/σ_{i+leap}; x+=d₂(σ↓₂−σ_{i+leap})+n·s·σ↑₂. η_dance>0: root of a negative gives σ↓₂=0, σ↑₂=σᵢ₊₁, so x=x0+n·s·σᵢ₊₁. η_dance=0: σ↓₂=σᵢ₊₁, no noise. Not danceable near the end falls back to plain Euler ancestral.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The second half-step moves sigma upward (σ_{i+leap} < σᵢ₊₁) while reusing the same x0.

audit.note: Literal formula matches extra_samplers.py:698-714, but σ_leap<σᵢ₊₁ makes core get_ancestral_step take a root of a negative (comfy/k_diffusion/sampling.py:73). By reading, not run: NaN, min() keeps σ↑₂=σᵢ₊₁, σ↓₂=0, so at default eta_dance=1 x lands on x0, then gets noise at σᵢ₊₁. Only eta_dance=0 walks up deterministically.

entries.name: Euler Dy
entries.plain: Euler with noise churn-like sigma inflation, plus an extra half-resolution model call taken on a downscaled 2×2 corner lattice of the latent. The extra step updates one pixel of every 2×2 block only. It is a port of the A1111 Dy idea, with extra steps gated by index.
entries.math:
γ=max(s_churn/(N−1),√2−1), or scaled by 1−(i/(N−2))^s_dy_pow, N=len(sigmas). σ̂=σᵢ(1+γ). x ← x − ε√(σ̂²−σᵢ²) (subtracts noise). x+=d·(σᵢ₊₁−σ̂).
Extra step when i//2==1: c = x[...,1,1] of each 2×2 block, x0_c = model(c,σ̂), c += d_c·dt, write c back.

entries.name: Euler extended sigmas
entries.plain: Euler that subdivides sigma intervals inside a set range into pass_steps linear substeps. So you get extra model calls at high sigma with a fixed schedule. Variants exist for ancestral and CFG++.

entries.name: Euler gamma and DPM++ 2M gamma

entries.name: Gen2 soft denoise around LanPaint
entries.plain: Wraps the LanPaint sampler so it can use a soft mask, since LanPaint itself binarises the denoise mask at 0.5. The wrapper blends the input toward a noised reference before the call, and blends the output toward a reference after. The reference can be the source, the latest generated output, or an EMA of generated outputs.
entries.math:
s=soft mask·hard envelope (after any denoise_mask_function).
x_w = x·mᵢ + N(ref,σ)·(1−mᵢ), mᵢ=effective_edit_mask(s, strengthᵢ(step)).
raw = LanPaint(x_w,σ,binary mask).
out = raw·mₒ + ref_out·(1−mₒ).
x is overwritten with x_w. ref is original_source, latest_generated or ema_generated (default EMA momentum 0.7); mixed_original_latest picks a per-pixel mix of original and latest through a curve on s, with its own step or sigma schedule.

entries.name: GMFlow policy
entries.plain: The model predicts a Gaussian mixture over the clean image at the start of the step. At any later point the policy works out the mean of that mixture given where the latent has moved, then turns it into a velocity. So the policy adapts as it integrates, at no model cost.
entries.math:
From output (means u_k, logstds, logweights): μ_k=x_src−σ_src u_k, v_k=e^(2·logstd)σ_src².
ζ=(α/σ)²−(α_s/σ_s)², ν=(α/σ)x/σ−(α_s/σ_s)x_s/σ_s, α=1−σ.
μ′_k=(v_k ν+μ_k)/(v_k ζ+1). logw′_k=logw_k+Σ_c μ_k(ν−½ζ μ_k)/(v_k ζ+1).
x̂₀=Σ softmax(logw′)_k μ′_k; π=(x−x̂₀)/σ.
Temperature T<1: logw←log_softmax(logw/T), v←v·T.

entries.plain: Ends the inner relaxation of one outer step once the predicted image inside the mask stops changing. It watches the unknown area and a one-pixel ring next to the kept area, and also checks that many small changes have not added up to a large drift. Off by default: the nodes set the threshold to 0.0.

entries.name: LanPaint overdamped inner loop (full read, replaces name-level lanpaint-langevin)
entries.plain: Before each outer sampler step, LanPaint runs a few inner steps of a noisy relaxation over the whole latent, so the masked area and the kept area can agree before the outer step moves on. The kept region is pulled toward the source image and also nudged by a second guided prediction, the "BIG" one. The code uses an exact Ornstein-Uhlenbeck step, the overdamped limit; the second-order damped oscillator is commented out.
entries.math:
Time conversion. Flow: abt=(1−σ)²/((1−σ)²+σ²), σ_VE=σ/(1−σ). VE: abt=1/(1+σ²).
m=1−(denoise_mask>0.5), 1 on kept pixels. Replace step: x←x(1−m)+noise_scaling(σ,noise,y)·m.
x_t=x·(√abt+√(1−abt)) on flow, x/√(1+σ²) on VE. Convert back for each model call.
Score: s=−(x_t−x̂₀)(1−m) + [−(1+λ)(x_t−y)+λ(x_t−x̂₀ᴮ)]m, x̂₀ at cfg, x̂₀ᴮ at cfg_BIG.
Drift: A=1/(1−abt) unknown, (1+λ)/(1−abt) known. C=(√abt(x_t+s)−x_t)/(1−abt)+A x_t. D=√2.
Step: dt=η·max(1−abt,f)·(1 unknown, β known), η=StepSize, f=MinStepFrac.
OU(dt): x←e^(−A dt)x+k C+√(D²k₂)·n, k=(1−e^(−A dt))/A, k₂=(1−e^(−2A dt))/(2A).
First inner step: OU(dt). Later: OU(dt/2); C′=C(x); x+=(C′−C)dt; OU(dt/2).
End: x̂₀ from one more model call at the converted x, kept region overwritten by y; the in-place x carries the relaxed latent back to the outer sampler.

entries.name: LCM dual noise
entries.plain: Blends two x0 predictions per step: the normal one, and one from re-noising an earlier x0 at the same sigma with fresh noise. That earlier x0 is this step's by default and the previous step's in parallel mode. Optional pre-normalization loops at max sigma.
entries.math: x₂=noise_scaling(σᵢ,n,x0_r), x0_r=this step's x0 (parallel: previous step's). x0₂=model(x₂,σᵢ). x0=(1−w)x0+w x0₂, w=weight(1−σᵢ₊₁/σᵢ) or static 1−weight. x=x0+σᵢ₊₁·(x−x0₁)/σᵢ. σᵢ₊₁=0: x=x0.

entries.name: LCM parallel geometric median
entries.plain: Runs several noisy copies at the same sigma and merges their x0 predictions with a geometric median. A robust aggregate for one step, at K model calls per step.
entries.math: For K noises: x_k=noise_scaling(σᵢ,n_k,x0). x0_k=model(x_k,σᵢ). x0=geomedian(x0_k) with up to 100 iterations. n_k=(x_k−x0)/σᵢ for next step.

entries.name: LCM TTM JVP

entries.name: pi-Flow outer loop and substep integrator (full read, replaces name-level piflow-policy-sampler)
entries.plain: A pi-Flow model outputs a small closed-form velocity function, the policy, instead of one velocity. One model call per step gives that policy; the sampler then runs many Euler substeps through it with no further model calls. The diffusion_coefficient setting optionally adds noise by stopping the policy short of the target and adding noise to land on it. It has no CFG: the guider is set to cfg 1 and only positive conditioning is used.
entries.math:
Outer: raw t = linspace(1, (f−1)/(N+f−1), N, no endpoint).clamp(≥0)·denoise, f=final_step_size_scale; σ=warp_t(raw t), then 0.
Substeps: count=⌈(raw_start−raw_end)·total_substeps⌉≥1. So total_substeps is per unit of raw t, shared between steps, not per step.
x←x+π(x,σ)·(σ⁻−σ), with σ⁻=warp_t(raw t−Δ). Mask: u=π·m+(x−y)/σ·(1−m).
Noise: m_h=(σ_to(1−σ_src)/(σ_src(1−σ_to)))^(h²), h=diffusion_coefficient. σ_dst=σ_to m_h/((1−σ_to)+σ_to m_h).
x_to=((1−σ_to)+σ_to m_h)x_dst+σ_to√(1−m_h²)·n. h=0 gives m_h=1, deterministic.
GM temperature: auto=clamp(0.1(N−1),0,1), applied on every step but the last, and only if the policy has temperature_.

entries.name: RALU three-stage mixed resolution (full read, replaces name-level ralu-staged-sampling)
entries.plain: Starts at half resolution, then upscales only the patches with the most edges, then upscales the rest. Noise is added at each jump so the latent matches the noise level of the next stage. This saves model time because early steps run on far fewer tokens. On Flux, the mixed stage really uses fewer tokens, with half-offset position ids; on SD3 it stays a full grid with blocks repeated.
entries.math:
Stage k: σ_lin=linspace(u(1−s_k),u(1−e_k),N_k+1), u(v)=v/(h−(h−1)v); t=hσ_lin/(1+(h−1)σ_lin); x←x+v·(t_{j+1}−t_j) (plain Euler).
s_{k+1}=e_k/(Z(1−e_k)+e_k). Jump: x←β x+α n; β=1/(Z(1−e_k)+e_k), α=1−s_{k+1}.
Stage 1 latent is nearest-downsampled by 2. Stage 2 selection: x̂₀=x−v σ, top ⌊r·patches⌋ by Canny edge sum on the VAE decode (thresholds 100,200), or energy+½|grad| on latent x̂₀ if no VAE or if it fails. Selected patches repeat ×4 in tokens.
Correlated noise option: blocks of 4 tokens with Σ=I+γ11ᵀ, γ=−1/Z²+1e-6, by Cholesky.
Flux: calls forward_orig directly, no CFG, first conditioning entry only, guidance embed default 3.5. SD3: optional cfg_scale through _predict_sd3_velocity.
Presets: level 4 N=[5,6,7], e=[.3,.45,1], Z=6.317, r=.3; level 7 N=[2,3,5], e=[.2,.3,1], Z=6.261, r=.1.

entries.name: RALU-aligned SD3 two stage
entries.plain: A simpler low-res then high-res SD3 pass that reuses the Flux Z value. It upsamples everything by nearest neighbour, injects block-correlated noise at the matching level, and continues with plain Euler. It can split across two nodes because the seed travels with the latent.
entries.math:
e₁=.35, Z=6.317, N=[10,20], shifts [5.8741,3.1334] by default.
s₁=e₁/(Z(1−e₁)+e₁); β=1/(Z(1−e₁)+e₁); α=Z(1−e₁)/(Z(1−e₁)+e₁).
x_hi=β·up₂(x_lo)+α·n, n from 2×2 blocks with Σ=I+γ11ᵀ, γ=−1/Z²+1e-6.
Then x←x+v Δσ with optional CFG.

entries.name: REAL sampler (WeightFerry)
entries.plain: Euler with a look-ahead velocity at the next point; when mismatch is small it advances multiple steps using that velocity. If it stays at one step, the second call is reused as the next step's first call. Near the end it is plain Euler with no look-ahead.
entries.math: z=x+Δσ·u. Tail (σ′<0.15 or fewer than min_k steps left): x=z, no look-ahead. Else w=v(z,σ′). r_loc=rel_mismatch(u,w). If r_loc≤q_loc: try skipping candidates k with r_seg=(s_ik/h)r_loc≤q_seg; x=z+Δ·w, b=None (b=w if carry_policy always). Else k*=1: x=z, reuse b=w.
entries.label: from code

audit.note: Omits the tail path and overstates reuse. real_sampler.py:79-81: if σ′<0.15 or fewer than min_k steps remain, plain Euler with no look-ahead. Second call is reused only on the 1-step fallback, unless carry_policy='always' (line 132; default fallback_only).

entries.name: Rectified flow controlled forward/reverse
entries.plain: Inverts then re-generates by blending the unconditional vector field with a straight-line field to a target, per RF-Inversion formula in comments. Forward goes to noise; reverse returns to a guide.
entries.math:
Forward: v̂=u(Y,σ)+γ_i((y1−Y)/(1−t_i)−u), t_i=σ/σ_max, Y+=v̂(σᵢ₊₁−σᵢ).
Reverse: v̂=−u+η_i((y0−X)/(1−t_i)+u), t_i=i/N, X+=v̂(σᵢ−σᵢ₊₁).

entries.plain: A rewrite of 2M and 3M with explicit history lists and a separate 2-point warmup for 3M. Adapted from research-unipc-dpmpp. Optional sharpness on stored x0.
entries.math: x_decay=(σᵢ₊₁/σᵢ)e^{−ηh}. order 2: x=x_decay x+α(1−e^{−h_η})x0+½α(1−e^{−h_η})d1. order 3 with 2 history: φ₂, φ₃ terms over h_η. Warmup via _warmup_3m.

entries.name: Restart sampler (Neo)
entries.plain: Karras restart: runs a Heun pass, then re-noises back up to a higher sigma and repeats a segment. When no list is given it picks restart counts from the step count.
entries.math:
No list given and steps≥20: restart_steps=9,times=1 (steps≥36: steps//4, 2), base Karras over remaining; restart_list={0.1:[restart_steps+1,times,2]}.
Steps list inserts Karras segments from σ_restart_max=2 to σ=0.1. On each upward jump: x+=randn·s·√(σ_old²−σ_last²). Each segment: Heun step.

entries.name: Sampler Adaptive step sizing
entries.plain: Ignores the incoming schedule and picks sigma steps from the agreement of successive x0 velocities, driving any inner sampler one step at a time.
entries.math: σ_t=max(σ−Δ,σ_min). inner(x,[σ,σ_t]). v=x0−x. err=1−|cos(v_prev,v)| or MSE. Δ′=base/(err+bias), Δ=clamp(smooth·Δ+(1−smooth)Δ′,min,max). Defaults base 0.0004, min 0.005 on the node (0.01 in the function), max 0.2, bias 0.002.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Sigma steps are linear additive from sigma_max, so step sizes of 0.01–0.2 assume a flow-like sigma range.

audit.note: Default min differs by layer: function signature min_step_size=0.01 (adaptive_sampler.py:26), but the node widget default is 0.005.

entries.name: Scheduled-eta SEEDS-2 and ER-SDE
entries.plain: Core seeds_2 and er_sde with eta computed per sigma by a tau function, by default active between 20% and 80% of the sigma percent range. Injection stops outside that window.
entries.math: τ(σ)=get_tau_interval_func(percent_to_sigma(0.2),percent_to_sigma(0.8)). seeds_2: h_η=h(τ+1) per step. er_sde: noise scaler x·(e^{x^0.3}+10)^{τ}; τ=0 uses identity scaler. Both solve core's update otherwise.

entries.name: SEEDS-2 Sharp
entries.plain: Core seeds_2 where the combined x0 has a sharpness-scaled term subtracted, using the same factor.
entries.math: f=1+s(i/N)². phi_1: D=lerp(x0₁,x0₂,fac) − fac(f−1)x0₁. phi_2: D=b1x0₁+b2x0₂ − b2(f−1)x0₁.

entries.name: Selective Sigma Detailer
entries.plain: Detail Daemon idea with a spatial mask: two model calls at told and true sigma, composited by a mask built from the normal x0. So only parts of the latent get the lie.
entries.math: x0_d=model(x,σ_adj). x0_n=model(x,σ). m=mask_fn(x0_n,x,σ). x0=m·x0_d+(1−m)x0_n. Full coverage path uses a single call. schedule from sample_schedule interpolates a table by sigma.

entries.name: SelfRefineVideo
entries.plain: Euler with repeated stochastic passes per step on a step map. Each extra pass re-noises from previous x0 at the same sigma, with an uncertainty mask taken from x0 difference. Handles combined video+audio latent.
entries.math: for ii<m: x_in=x or (1−σ)x0_prev+σn. x0=model(x_in,σ). x_next=x+(σ′−σ)d. uncertainty=√Σ(diff²)/C; certain_mask=uncertainty<thresh; fix certain voxels; exit early if fraction > certain_percentage(0.999).

entries.name: Sonar momentum samplers
entries.plain: Euler, Euler A and DPM++ SDE with a blended history of derivative or x0, configurable by mode and a separate history rate. Optional guidance toward a reference latent.
entries.math: d_m=blend(hist,d,momentum); x=x+d_m(σ↓−σ). hist updated with hd_ratio from momentum_hist. Mode DENOISED applies on x0, else on d. Defaults momentum_hist 0.75, direction 1.0.

entries.name: SPEED multi-scale sampling

entries.name: SUN samplers (scaled uniform noise)

entries.name: SUPREME multi-method sampler
entries.plain: A configurable loop: pick a step method per substep (euler, dpm_1s/2s/3s, rk4, reversible Heun, RKF45, Bogacki-Shampine, trapezoidal, RES, dynamic or adaptive order), plus denoised enhancements and noise modulation. It averages substep results with weights. It auto-disables noise on flow schedules.
entries.math:
For each σᵢ, k substeps: z_k from x, step by selected method, z_avg += w_k z_k, then optionally re-noise. x=z_avg + noise_mod(σ↑).
dynamic/adaptive_rk pick order from an error of x0 vs previous (thresholds 3.75e-2, 7.5e-2, 1.5e-1). Weights table: {1:[1],2:[½,½],3:[⅙,⅔,⅙],4:[⅛,⅜,⅜,⅛]}.
Denoised enhancements: bilateral blur + unsharp edge term scaled by (σᵢ−σᵢ₊₁), channel centralize and normalize, perpendicular addition of previous x0. Noise modulation: none, intensity, frequency, spectral_signum.
If σ_max ≤ 1.001: η=0, s_noise=0, modulation none.

entries.name: SUPREME substep and enhancement details (extends supreme-sampler)
entries.plain: Details the first pass left out, from a full read of the function up to the final step cases. Substeps all restart from the same x and are averaged, so they only differ through the history term or a differing substep method. The denoised enhancement runs inside every model call, including RK stages, with strength divided by the expected calls per step.
entries.math:
For k substeps: z_k=x, step, z_avg+=(1/k)z_k. Weights are uniform; the ⅙,⅔,⅙ table is only for adaptive_rk.
After the average: x=z_avg+noise_mod(σ↑).
Error for dynamic: e=‖d(x_pred,D)−d₋₁‖/‖d₋₁‖ with x_pred an Euler step from the previous x. e<.01→order 6 (rkf45), <.0375→4, <.075→3, <.15→2, else 1. Step 0 uses rkf45.
Enhance per call, n=calls per step: D+=(unsharp(D)−D)(σᵢ−σᵢ₊₁)E/n + (jointbilateral(x,D)−x)(σᵢ−σᵢ₊₁)E/n.
Centralize per channel: D−=mean·c/n·√σ. Normalize: D+=(D/std−D)·N/n·√σ.
Perp-hist: a=x−(D−x), b=x−(D₋₁−x), b⊥=b−a·Σ(a b)/‖a‖², D+=(p/n)·b⊥.
Final step always euler.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The substep noise is added to z_k after z_avg was already accumulated and z_k is reset next substep, so the inner noise never reaches the output; it only advances the noise sampler.

entries.name: TBG Flux2 mask sampler

entries.name: TCD (alpha-table form)
entries.plain: Trajectory consistency sampling written with an alpha table computed in the node. Rescales the x0 and predicted noise by alpha sqrt values at the next step and renoises by eta.
entries.math: x′=√ᾱ_{s}·x0+√(1−ᾱ_{s})·ε, at the next-index ᾱ. If η>0 and σᵢ₊₁>0: x=x′/√ᾱ + n·√(σᵢ₊₁²+1−1/ᾱ). Else x=x′√(σᵢ₊₁²+1).

entries.name: TCD Euler ancestral
entries.plain: Euler ancestral where σ↓ comes from scaling the timestep by (1−γ) instead of the usual ancestral formula. Larger gamma means bigger noise replacement.
entries.math: t=timestep(σ). σ↓=min(sigma((1−γ)t),σ′). σ↑=√(σ′²−σ↓²). x+=d(σ↓−σ). If σ′>0, γ>0: x=noise_scaling(σ↑,n,x).

entries.name: TDNodes resumable k-diffusion fork
entries.plain: Fork of older core k-diffusion where each solver takes a SamplingConfig that holds extra args, callback and a cache. History like old_denoised and denoised_1 is fetched and stored there, so a sampling run can stop and resume across calls.
entries.math: Same update as core at fork date; x0_prev = config.get_noise_from_cache('old_denoised'), and config.step in heunpp2.

entries.name: Timesaver inpaint think sampler
entries.plain: Before each step in the mask region it repeats think_steps re-noising loops mixing old and fresh eps, then proceeds with a step.
entries.math: for think: x0=model(x,σ); ε_old=(x−a·x0)/b; mix=keep·ε_old+strength·fresh; x_re=a·x0+b·mix; x=x(1−m)+x_re·m.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Truncated Taylor method (JVP)
entries.plain: Second-order truncated Taylor method: it takes the total derivative of the denoiser along the trajectory with forward-mode autodiff, instead of a second model call or history. Same formula as the k-diffusion TTM idea. Needs a model that supports torch.func.jvp.
entries.math:
ε=(x−x0)/σ. x0′ = JVP of model(x,σ) along (−σε, −σ). h=log(σᵢ/σᵢ₊₁), h_η=h(η+1).
x ← e^{−h_η}x + (1−e^{−h_η})x0 + φ₂x0′, plus noise σᵢ₊₁√(1−e^{−2hη})·n·s_noise.
φ₂ = e^{−h}+h in extra_samplers.py; φ₂ = e^{−h_η}+h_η in other_samplers/sample_ttm.py.

entries.surprise: Same-named function in one pack has two φ₂ forms: h in extra_samplers.py, h_η in sample_ttm.py.

entries.name: TwinFlow unified sampler
entries.plain: A one-step style model loop that predicts x₀ and noise at once, then re-noises fully with fresh noise, as consistency sampling does. The model also gets a target time. The node keeps only the length of the sigmas it is given: the pack rebuilds its own schedule, using the official preset per the comment.
entries.math:
F=(x−D)/t; ẑ=x+(1−t)F; x̂=D.
x⁺=(1−t⁺)x̂+t⁺(ẑ√(1−r)+n√r), r=stochast_ratio=1, so ẑ is dropped.
Target time: 0 for few, t for mul, t⁺ for any.
Seeded per step: seed+1+i.
