entries.surprise: Sigmas from the graph are ignored apart from their count.

entries.name: VEnhancer SDEdit solvers
entries.plain: Standalone heun and 2M SDE using c_in scaling and handling σ=inf at the first step. Used by a wrapper model.
entries.math: σ=inf: x0=model(noise,inf); x=x0+σ′·noise. Else model(x·c_in,σ), then standard update.

providers.author: vjumpkung
providers.note: Adds variant_info arg

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Align Your Steps (AYS)
entries.plain: Uses NVIDIA's published 10-step tables for SD1, SDXL and SVD (the file header links the source page), and log-linearly resamples them for any other step count. The denoise behaviour differs from BasicScheduler: it keeps only the last round(steps·denoise) steps rather than stretching to preserve the step count.
entries.math:
Table τ (11 values). If steps+1 ≠ 11:
σ_i = exp(interp(i/steps, j/10, ln τ_rev)) reversed (piecewise-linear in ln σ).
Keep last round(steps·denoise)+1 values; last value forced to 0.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The SVD table is 700→0.002, and all tables ignore the loaded model; picking the wrong model_type is not detected (no MODEL input, nodes_align_your_steps.py:34).

entries.name: BasicScheduler / KSampler denoise truncation
entries.plain: How partial denoise works for named schedulers: compute a longer schedule and keep only its tail, so the model still runs the requested number of steps at lower noise.
entries.math: total = ⌊steps/denoise⌋ (denoise<1). σ = schedule(total)[−(steps+1):]. denoise≤0 → empty.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: AYS, GITS and OSS implement denoise the other way: they drop to round(steps·denoise) steps, so the same widget means different step counts (nodes_align_your_steps.py:51 vs nodes_custom_sampler.py:38).

entries.name: beta
entries.plain: Picks table indices from the inverse CDF of a Beta distribution, per the code comment on arXiv 2407.12173. With the default α=β=0.6 the indices pile up near both ends, so steps are small at high and low noise and fast in the middle. Indices are rounded to integers and repeats are removed.
entries.math:
M=len(S)−1. u_i = 1 − i/steps, i=0..steps−1.
t_i = rint(BetaPPF(u_i; α, β)·M).
σ_i = S[t_i], skipping a t_i equal to the previous one, then 0.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Repeat removal means beta can silently return fewer steps than asked when many indices round alike, as with extreme alpha/beta (samplers.py:703-706).

entries.name: ddim_uniform
entries.plain: DDIM-style stride through the model's sigma table: integer stride from index 1 upward, then reversed, with a 0 at the end. Because the walk starts at the bottom and stops wherever the stride ends, the top sigma is usually not the model's sigma_max.
entries.math:
N=len(S). If S[1]≈0: steps+=1 and no 0 is prepended; this happens before the stride. ss = max(⌊N/steps⌋,1). Indices x = 1, 1+ss, 1+2ss, … while x<N.
σ list = [0] + S[x…] (or S[x…] without the 0), reversed.

props.shape: integer stride from index 1 upward, reversed

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Output length is not fixed to steps+1 when N is not a multiple of steps: reading the loop, N=1000 and steps=30 gives stride 33 and 31 nonzero sigmas, so 31 steps (samplers.py:664-668).

audit.note: Order of operations: the steps+=1 for S[1]≈0 happens before the stride is computed (ComfyUI/comfy/samplers.py:658-664), but the math lists it after ss, implying the stride ignores it.

entries.name: Discard penultimate sigma (KSampler rule)
entries.plain: For dpm_2, dpm_2_ancestral, uni_pc and uni_pc_bh2, KSampler builds the schedule with one more step and removes the second-to-last sigma, so the last jump goes straight to 0. This is an automatic shaper tied to the sampler name; a SamplerCustom workflow with its own sigmas does not get it.
entries.math: σ = schedule(steps+1); σ' = σ[:−2] + [σ[−1]].
entries.label: from code

entries.name: exponential
entries.plain: Sigmas evenly spaced in log sigma between the model's range, then zero. Karras with ρ→∞ in the limit; the plainest noise-level spacing and the one log-SNR solvers take equal steps on.
entries.math: σ_i = exp(linspace(ln σmax, ln σmin, n)), then 0.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: ExtendIntermediateSigmas
entries.plain: Inserts extra sigmas between neighbours in a chosen sigma range, adding steps only where you want them. Spacing inside each gap is linear or one of two eased forms. The default end_at_sigma of 12 only subdivides the very top of an SD-style range.
entries.math:
x = linspace(0,1,steps+1)[1:−1]; f linear: x; 'cosine': sin(xπ/2); 'sine': 1−cos(xπ/2).
For each gap with end_at ≤ σ_i ≤ start_at (start_at<0 means ∞): insert σ_i + f(x)·(σ_{i+1}−σ_i).
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The spacing named 'cosine' is the sine curve and 'sine' is 1−cosine (nodes_custom_sampler.py:321-322).

entries.name: FlipSigmas
entries.plain: Reverses a schedule so sampling runs from low noise to high, which is how unsampling or inversion is done. A leading zero is replaced by 0.0001 so the model is never called at sigma 0.
entries.math: σ' = reverse(σ). If σ'[0]=0: σ'[0]=1e-4.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Flow shift (time_snr_shift, ModelSamplingSD3 / AuraFlow)
entries.plain: The shift used by SD3-class flow models. It bends the whole flow time axis so more of it sits at high noise; every schedule read from the model inherits the bend. Shift 1 is no bend. AuraFlow's node is the same code with multiplier 1 (the model's timestep is in 0..1, not 0..1000).
entries.math:
time_snr_shift(α,t) = α·t/(1+(α−1)·t), α=shift, t=timestep/multiplier.
Table: σ_k = time_snr_shift(α, k/1000), k=1..1000. timestep(σ)=σ·multiplier.
Denoised (CONST): x − v·σ. Noise: σ·s·ε + (1−σ)·x0.

props.params: SD3 shift=3.0 multiplier=1000; AuraFlow shift=1.73 multiplier=1

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: flux_time_shift with σ=1 equals time_snr_shift with α=e^μ, so Flux 'shift' is the log of SD3's shift, and the same number means very different curves (model_sampling.py:292 and :414).

entries.name: Flux shift (flux_time_shift, ModelSamplingFlux)
entries.plain: Flux's table uses an exponential shift μ. The node computes μ from image area on a line through two reference points, so larger images get more shift. The table has 10000 entries and timestep equals sigma.
entries.math:
flux_time_shift(μ,1,t) = e^μ/(e^μ + (1/t−1)).
Node: tokens = w·h/(8·8·2·2); μ = tokens·m + b, m=(max_shift−base_shift)/(4096−256), b=base_shift−256m.
Table: t=k/10000, k=1..10000.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Flux2Scheduler
entries.plain: Flux 2 schedule. μ depends on both resolution and step count using two fitted lines, with empirical constants written directly in the code. Above 4300 tokens only the 200-step line applies. The sigmas are a linear ramp through the same exponential shift.

props.shape: linear ramp, shift from steps and resolution

family_fit.why: node name and fixed 16 px patch divisor
family_fit.label: from code

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: μ moves with step count, so fewer steps means more shift at the same resolution; the only core schedule whose curve changes shape with steps this way (nodes_flux.py:199-203).

entries.name: GITS
entries.plain: Looks up a precomputed schedule by coeff (15 values, 0.80 to 1.50 in 0.05 steps) and step count (19 rows per coeff, for 2 to 20 steps). Above 20 steps it log-linearly stretches the 20-step row. Header comment cites zju-pi/diff-sampler gits-main. All rows span the SD1-style 14.6146 to 0.0292 range.
entries.math:
If steps ≤ 20: σ = T[coeff][steps−2].
Else: σ = loglinear_interp(T[coeff][−1], steps+1).
Keep last round(steps·denoise)+1 values; last forced to 0.

providers.author: pamparamm
providers.note: _gits_scheduler same lookup, src/schedulers.py:27

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The tables are not resampled below 20 steps, so each row is its own schedule, and rows share long common tails of table sigmas (nodes_gits.py:363).

entries.name: Ideogram4Scheduler
entries.plain: Schedule from a logit-normal quantile: equal probability mass per step under a logit-normal, with the mean shifted by resolution. Clamped by a fixed logSNR range then forced to end at 0.
entries.math:
mean = μ + ½·ln(w·h/512²). u=linspace(0,1,n+1).
t(u) = 1 − expit(mean + std·Φ⁻¹(u)), clamped to [1/(1+e^9), 1/(1+e^−7.5)].
σ = flip(1 − t), last = 0.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: karras
entries.plain: The EDM schedule: interpolate linearly in σ^(1/ρ) between the top and bottom sigma, so steps bunch up at low noise as ρ rises. Only sigma_min and sigma_max are read from the model, so sigmas are off-table values. Available both as a scheduler name and as a standalone node with typed-in range.
entries.math:
ramp r_i = linspace(0,1,n).
σ_i = (σmax^(1/ρ) + r_i·(σmin^(1/ρ) − σmax^(1/ρ)))^ρ, then 0. ρ=7 default.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: kl_optimal
entries.plain: Spaces steps uniformly in arctan(σ), which the code credits to an A1111 webui pull request. Because arctan is close to linear for small σ and flat for large σ, the jump from the top is large and low-noise steps are fine.
entries.math:
w_i = i/(n−1).
σ_i = tan(w_i·atan σmin + (1−w_i)·atan σmax), i=0..n−1, then 0.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: At steps=1 the code divides arange(1) by n−1=0, which reads as a NaN first sigma (samplers.py:733).

entries.name: Laplace
entries.plain: Places log sigma on a Laplace-shaped curve so steps cluster around exp(μ), a mid-range noise level, and clamps the result to the given range. Node only.
entries.math:
x_i = linspace(0,1,n), ε=1e-5.
λ_i = μ − β·sign(0.5−x_i)·ln(1 − 2|0.5−x_i| + ε).
σ_i = clamp(exp(λ_i), σmin, σmax). No trailing zero is appended.

props.shape: Laplace quantile in ln σ, clamped

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Unlike every other core get_sigmas_*, Laplace appends no zero: it returns n values, so n−1 steps, ending at sigma_min with residual noise (sampling.py:58-59).

entries.name: LCM distilled table (ModelSamplingDiscrete lcm)
entries.plain: Selecting lcm in ModelSamplingDiscrete replaces the table with 50 entries at a stride of T/50 and changes the denoised formula, so schedulers now walk a shorter table. The prediction mix is a consistency-style skip and output.
entries.math:
Keep every (T//50)th sigma from the top. timestep = argmin index·skip + skip−1.
x0 = x − ε·σ; t' = 10t; c_skip = 0.25/(t'²+0.25); c_out = t'/√(t'²+0.25); denoised = c_out·x0 + c_skip·x.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: linear_quadratic
entries.plain: The Mochi video schedule, per the code comment: the first half of the steps move noise only a tiny amount (down to threshold_noise), then a quadratic takes the rest. Most of the step budget is spent near full noise. The result is scaled by sigma_max.
entries.math:
t=threshold_noise, L=linear_steps=⌊steps/2⌋, Q=steps−L, D=L−t·steps.
For i<L: u_i = i·t/L.
For i≥L: u_i = a·i² + b·i + c, a=D/(L·Q²), b=t/L−2D/Q², c=a·L².
u_steps = 1. σ_i = (1−u_i)·σmax. steps=1 → [1,0]·σmax.

family_fit.why: code comment cites genmoai models infer.py as source
family_fit.label: from code

entries.label: from code

entries.name: LTXV scheduler
entries.plain: LTX Video schedule: a linear ramp pushed through the Flux-style exponential shift, with μ from token count. An optional stretch rescales 1−σ so the last nonzero sigma lands exactly on terminal. Tokens come from the latent's spatial and temporal size, or 4096 with no latent.
entries.math:
tokens = ∏ latent.shape[2:] (or 4096).
μ = tokens·m + b; m = (max_shift−base_shift)/(4096−1024), b = base_shift − m·1024.
σ_i = e^μ/(e^μ + (1/u_i − 1)), u=linspace(1,0,steps+1), keeping 0 at u=0.
Stretch: z=1−σ (nonzero); s=z_last/(1−terminal); σ'=1−z/s.

props.shape: linear ramp, exponential shift, optional stretch to terminal

family_fit.why: node is in the LTXV extension
family_fit.label: from code

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Token count multiplies frames too, so longer video gives more shift; μ is unbounded and extrapolates outside the 1024..4096 reference line (nodes_lt.py:807-816).

entries.name: ManualSigmas
entries.plain: Parses numbers out of a text string into a schedule, with nothing checked: no descending check and no required trailing zero. Marked experimental.
entries.math: σ = numbers matched by a regex over the input string.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The regex has no exponent form, so '1e-3' parses as two numbers, 1 and -3 (nodes_custom_sampler.py:1141).

entries.name: ModelNoiseScale
entries.plain: Keeps the schedule and multiplies the noise inside CONST flow noise scaling. It rebuilds the model sampling with the same shift and multiplier. The tooltip gives HiDream-O1 values.
entries.math: Noise step: x = σ·(s·ε) + (1−σ)·x0, s=noise_scale. Schedule unchanged.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: ModelSamplingAV / MiniMaxH3SigmaShift
entries.plain: A flow table for packed audio-video latents. The video shift drives the schedule; the audio shift is stored and sets an audio scale, and both go to the model through transformer options so it can derive the audio schedule. The vsaan212 fallback differs: it uses the plain flow table, so it stores no audio shift or audio scale and passes the audio shift only through transformer options.
entries.math: σ table: time_snr_shift(shift_video, k/1000). audio_scale = shift_video/shift_audio (1.0 if shift_audio is None). transformer_options carries both. vsaan212 fallback: same table on ModelSamplingDiscreteFlow, no audio_scale.

providers.author: PGCRT
providers.note: Docstring: mirror of the native MiniMaxH3SigmaShift

providers.author: vsaan212
providers.note: fallback file; patch line seen, surroundings not read

providers.author: Chargeuk
providers.note: patch line seen, surroundings not read

family_fit.why: node is H3 specific; display name ModelSamplingMiniMaxH3
family_fit.label: from code

entries.label: from code

audit.note: The math does not hold for every listed provider. The vsaan212 fallback builds ModelSamplingDiscreteFlow and calls set_parameters(shift=shift_video) (Lazy_minimax/_nodes_minimax_h3_fallback.py:309-314), so it has no audio_shift or audio_scale; only the transformer options carry the audio shift. Core and PGCRT use ModelSamplingAV. Also audio_scale is 1.0 when audio_shift is None (ComfyUI/comfy/model_sampling.py:355-356).

entries.name: ModelSamplingContinuousEDM
entries.plain: Continuous EDM sigma range with the 1000 point log-spaced table only for compatibility. Option list: eps, edm (σ_data 0.5), v_prediction, edm_playground_v2.5 (also replaces latent format), cosmos_rflow (changes base class).
entries.math:
Table: exp(linspace(ln σmin, ln σmax, 1000)). timestep(σ)=¼ ln σ; sigma(t)=e^{4t}.
Cosmos RFlow: timestep(σ)=σ/(σ+1), sigma(t)=t/(1−t) capped at σmax.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: ModelSamplingContinuousV
entries.plain: Continuous v-prediction with an arctan time map, plus a log-spaced compatibility table.
entries.math: timestep(σ)=atan(σ)·2/π; sigma(t)=tan(t·π/2). Table log-uniform in [σmin, σmax].
entries.label: from code

entries.name: ModelSamplingDiscrete base table + zero terminal SNR
entries.plain: The sigma table every discrete SD-style model carries. It comes from a β schedule and is the source for simple, normal, ddim_uniform and beta. The ModelSamplingDiscrete node also switches prediction type (eps, v, lcm, x0, img_to_img, img_to_img_flow) and can rescale the table to zero terminal SNR.
entries.math:
linear default: β_t = (linspace(√start, √end, T))², start 0.00085, end 0.012, T=1000. ᾱ=∏(1−β). σ_t=√((1−ᾱ)/ᾱ).
zsnr: √ᾱ' = (√ᾱ−√ᾱ_T)·√ᾱ_0/(√ᾱ_0−√ᾱ_T), σ'=√((1−ᾱ')/ᾱ'), with ᾱ'_T fixed to 4.897e-8.
Other β shapes: cosine, squaredcos_cap_v2, sqrt_linear, sqrt in make_beta_schedule.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: With zsnr the terminal value is not infinite but the constant 4.8973451890853435e-08, giving a very large finite sigma (model_sampling.py:21).

entries.name: ModelSamplingLTXV
entries.plain: Same exponential shift class as Flux, with μ from latent size on a 1024..4096 line. Used so the model's table matches LTX video length and resolution.
entries.math: tokens=∏ latent.shape[2:] or 4096. μ = tokens·m+b, m=(max_shift−base_shift)/3072, b=base_shift−1024m. Then flux_time_shift.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Name-only wrappers of core schedules (TCD, LCM)
entries.plain: Nodes whose names suggest a new scheduler but which call a core one. TCDScheduler returns core ddim_uniform. LCMScheduler returns core sgm_uniform, with BasicScheduler-style denoise.
entries.math:
TCDScheduler: σ=calculate_sigmas(ms,'ddim_uniform',steps).
LCMScheduler: σ=calculate_sigmas(ms,'sgm_uniform',⌊steps/denoise⌋)[−(steps+1):].

providers.author: licyk
providers.note: not compared

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The 'TCD' and 'LCM' schedulers add no new curve: the TCD behaviour lives in the sampler, not the sigmas (sampler_tcd.py:132-135, sampler_lcm_alt.py:83).

entries.name: normal
entries.plain: Spaces timesteps evenly from highest to lowest with both endpoints kept, converts to sigma, and appends 0. If the model's lowest sigma is already about zero, it adds a step and skips the appended zero so the requested number of real steps survives.
entries.math:
t_i = linspace(t(σmax), t(σmin), steps); σ_i = model.sigma(t_i); final 0.
If model.sigma(t(σmin)) ≈ 0 (abs_tol 1e-5): steps += 1 and no zero is appended.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Optimal Steps (OSS)
entries.plain: Hard-coded flow-range schedules for FLUX (10 steps), Wan (20) and Chroma (40), from the source named in the header comment (bebebe666/OptimalSteps). Other step counts use the same log-linear resample as AYS. The tables are absolute sigmas and the node takes no model input, so the loaded model's shift setting has no effect on them.
entries.math:
Table τ for model_type. If steps+1 ≠ len(τ): σ = loglinear_interp(τ, steps+1).
Keep last round(steps·denoise)+1; last forced to 0.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The Wan table spends 13 of its 20 steps between 1.0 and 0.946 and the table's first value is 1.0, so high noise gets most of the budget (nodes_optimalsteps.py:25).

entries.name: polyexponential
entries.plain: Exponential schedule with a power applied to the ramp, so the log-sigma descent is curved. ρ=1 is identical to exponential. Node only; not in the KSampler scheduler list.
entries.math:
r_i = linspace(1,0,n)^ρ.
σ_i = exp(r_i·(ln σmax − ln σmin) + ln σmin), then 0.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: SamplingPercentToSigma / percent_to_sigma
entries.plain: Converts progress percent to a sigma using the model's own mapping. Used for start_percent/end_percent style windows across core. At 0 and 1 the mapping returns sentinels unless the node's actual-sigma option is set.
entries.math: Discrete: p'=1−p; σ(p'·999). Flow: time_snr_shift(shift, 1−p). Flux: flux_time_shift(μ,1,1−p). EDM: exp(p'·(ln σmax − ln σmin)+ln σmin). p≤0 → 999999999.9 or 1.0 on flow types; p≥1 → 0.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: SDTurboScheduler
entries.plain: Fixed ladder of 10 timesteps (999, 899, … 99), slicing a window by denoise and steps. It is limited to 10 steps, defaults to 1, and sigma comes from the model's timestep map.
entries.math:
T = [999,899,…,99]; start = 10−⌊10·denoise⌋; pick T[start : start+steps].
σ_i = model.sigma(T_i), then 0.

family_fit.why: name of node; ladder hard-coded for that training spacing
family_fit.label: inference

entries.label: from code

entries.name: SetFirstSigma
entries.plain: Overwrites only the first sigma. Replacing a low starting value with a far higher one is a way to start a schedule from a much noisier state than the table reaches.
entries.math: σ'[0]=sigma; all others unchanged.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: sgm_uniform
entries.plain: Spaces timesteps evenly from the top to the bottom of the model's range using steps+1 points, drops the last one, converts each to sigma and appends 0. Compared with normal it never lands on the lowest timestep before the zero.
entries.math:
t_i = linspace(t(σmax), t(σmin), steps+1)[:-1]; σ_i = model.sigma(t_i); final 0.
On a discrete model t(σ) is an argmin index and sigma(t) log-interpolates between neighbouring table entries.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: simple
entries.plain: Walks the model's own sigma table (1000 entries on a standard discrete model) from the top at an even stride and copies out the entry at the floored offset, which is at or just above the exact position. No interpolation, so every sigma is a value the model was trained on when the model is discrete. It is the first entry of the scheduler list, and KSampler falls back to it for an unknown scheduler name.
entries.math:
S = model_sampling.sigmas (ascending), N = len(S), ss = N/steps.
σ_i = S[N−1−⌊i·ss⌋] for i=0..steps−1, then a final 0.

props.shape: even stride down model sigma table, then 0

entries.label: from code

audit.note: Two errors. (1) "1000-entry" is not general: the code walks len(s.sigmas) (ComfyUI/comfy/samplers.py:648), and that is 10000 on ModelSamplingFlux (model_sampling.py:426) and 50 on the LCM table (nodes_model_advanced.py:28). (2) "nearest lower entry" has the direction backwards: int() floors the offset from the top (samplers.py:650), so the chosen index is at or above the exact position in an ascending table, giving the nearest higher-or-equal sigma.

entries.name: SplitSigmas / SplitSigmasDenoise
entries.plain: Cuts a schedule at a step or a denoise fraction into a high part and a low part that share one boundary sigma, for two-stage or two-model sampling.
entries.math:
SplitSigmas: high=σ[:step+1], low=σ[step:].
SplitSigmasDenoise: k=round((len−1)·denoise); high=σ[:−k], low=σ[−(k+1):].
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: SplitSigmasDenoise at denoise=0 slices σ[:−0], which is empty, instead of returning the whole schedule as high (nodes_custom_sampler.py:247-249).

entries.name: Stable Cascade cosine + shift
entries.plain: Cosine ᾱ schedule with a logSNR shift, used by Stable Cascade. The sigma table is present only so other schedulers work. ᾱ is clamped so sigma cannot run to infinity or zero.
entries.math:
ᾱ(t)=cos²((t+s)/(1+s)·π/2)/cos²(s/(1+s)·π/2), s=0.008.
If shift≠1: logSNR += 2·ln(1/shift); ᾱ=sigmoid(logSNR).
ᾱ clamped to [1e-4, 0.9999]. σ=√((1−ᾱ)/ᾱ). Table has 10000 entries.

family_fit.why: stage C default shift 2.0, stage B 1.0
family_fit.label: from code

entries.label: from code

entries.name: VP (variance preserving)
entries.plain: Continuous VP-SDE noise schedule from the score-SDE line of work. It takes β parameters rather than a sigma range, so the top and bottom of the schedule come from the formula and not from the model. Node only.
entries.math:
t_i = linspace(1, eps_s, n).
σ_i = √(expm1(β_d·t_i²/2 + β_min·t_i)), then 0.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Node carries a code comment saying its default values need fixing (nodes_custom_sampler.py:190).

entries.name: Adept "AYS" SDXL table
entries.plain: Pack-labelled AYS table with entries for 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30 steps, normalised to 0..1, scaled to the sigma range. The values are near-uniform and do not match NVIDIA's table in core; the docstring credits NVIDIA. Other counts log-interpolate from the next larger row.
entries.math:
σ = τ_n·(σmax−σmin)+σmin, σ_0=σmax; τ has n entries; then 0.
Other n: log-linear interpolation from a reference row, with log τ_end forced to log τ_{end−1}−3.

claims.text: Based on NVIDIA's AYS paper
claims.label: from pack README claim

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Named AYS but the 10-step table is about 1, .875, .75, … in steps of .125, nothing like core's AYS SDXL values (adept_schedulers.py:488 vs nodes_align_your_steps.py:23).

entries.name: Adept Adaptive-Optimized
entries.plain: A fixed weighted sum of four curves. Nothing adapts at runtime despite the name.
entries.math:
u=.2t+.3t^.8+.2(t+.2 sin(2πt)(1−t))+.3/(1+e^{−3(t−.5)}); normalised.
Unless noted: σ_max ≤ 1 uses σ=σmax+u(σmin−σmax); otherwise Karras mapping with ρ=7 and u as ramp. Then 0.

props.shape: ramp warp mapped through Karras or linear

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Fixed weights: the 'adaptive' here is a constant blend (adept_schedulers.py:205).

entries.name: Adept AkashicAOS
entries.plain: Single curve: power-warped ramp plus sine bump, renormalised, and a limit on how much one step can shrink.
entries.math:
u'=u^.85+.08·sin(πu)(1−u/2); normalised. Ratio guard: σ_{i−1}/σ_i ≤ 1.5.
Unless noted: σ_max ≤ 1 uses σ=σmax+u(σmin−σmax); otherwise Karras mapping with ρ=7 and u as ramp. Then 0.

props.shape: ramp warp mapped through Karras or linear

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The 1.5 ratio cap overrides the requested endpoint, so at low step counts the schedule never reaches σmin before the jump to 0 (adept_schedulers.py:119-121).

entries.name: Adept AkashicAOS Alt
entries.plain: Stronger power warp and a tanh crossover. ρ rises at low step counts.
entries.math:
ρ=clamp(7+2·20/max(n,10),7,11). u'=u^.78+.07·tanh(4(u−.55)); normalised; ratio guard 1.5.
Unless noted: σ_max ≤ 1 uses σ=σmax+u(σmin−σmax); otherwise Karras mapping with ρ=7 and u as ramp. Then 0.

props.shape: ramp warp mapped through Karras or linear

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Adept AkashicEQFlow
entries.plain: Builds step positions from a density in log-SNR space, peaked near logSNR≈0, and inverts its CDF. Step placement adapts with step count. Code names EQ-VAE models as its target.
entries.math:
λ=−2 ln σ. center=.20+.15·clamp((n−16)/30,0,1); u_c=clamp((center−λmin)/Δλ,.12,.88); density(t)=1+c·exp(−((t−u_c)/w)²/2)+.15t^1.2+.10(1−t)^1.5, c=clamp(.8+n/20,1,2.2), w=clamp(.40−.003n,.22,.38).
u_i=CDF⁻¹(i/(n−1)), σ_i=exp(−(λmin+u_i·Δλ)/2); ends forced to σmax, σmin, then 0.

claims.text: Aimed at EQ-VAE SDXL models
claims.label: from pack README claim

entries.label: from code

audit.note: adept_schedulers.py:609 docstring says EQ-VAE models, not SDXL; SDXL appears only on other schedules (:86, :482). Math omits the u_c clamp at :633 and the forced end values at :669-670.

entries.name: Adept AOS-E
entries.plain: Three-phase ramp, slower start and quicker finish than AOS-V.
entries.math:
35%: u=.4·r^1.5; 35%: linspace(.4,.75); 30%: u=.75+.25·r^.7.
Unless noted: σ_max ≤ 1 uses σ=σmax+u(σmin−σmax); otherwise Karras mapping with ρ=7 and u as ramp. Then 0.

props.shape: ramp warp mapped through Karras or linear

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Adept AOS-V
entries.plain: Three-phase ramp aimed at v-prediction by name. A square-root fast start to 0.6, a linear middle to 0.9, a cubic end.
entries.math:
20%: u=0.6·√r; 40%: linspace(.6,.9); 40%: u=.9+.1·r³.
Unless noted: σ_max ≤ 1 uses σ=σmax+u(σmin−σmax); otherwise Karras mapping with ρ=7 and u as ramp. Then 0.

props.shape: ramp warp mapped through Karras or linear

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Adept Constant-Rate
entries.plain: Linear ramp plus a damped sine bump.
entries.math:
u=t+.3·sin(πt)(1−t).
Unless noted: σ_max ≤ 1 uses σ=σmax+u(σmin−σmax); otherwise Karras mapping with ρ=7 and u as ramp. Then 0.

props.shape: ramp warp mapped through Karras or linear

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Adept Cosine
entries.plain: Cosine ease of the ramp, slow at both ends.
entries.math:
u=(1−cos πr)/2.
Unless noted: σ_max ≤ 1 uses σ=σmax+u(σmin−σmax); otherwise Karras mapping with ρ=7 and u as ramp. Then 0.

props.shape: ramp warp mapped through Karras or linear

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Adept Entropic
entries.plain: Average of a linear ramp and a power ramp.
entries.math:
u=(r+1−(1−r)^p)/2, p=3.
Unless noted: σ_max ≤ 1 uses σ=σmax+u(σmin−σmax); otherwise Karras mapping with ρ=7 and u as ramp. Then 0.

props.shape: ramp warp mapped through Karras or linear

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Adept Exponential Tail
entries.plain: Power ramp up to a pivot, exponential after it.
entries.math:
r<p: p·(r/p)^γ. r≥p: p+(1−p)·(1−e^{−β(r−p)})/(1−e^{−β}).
Unless noted: σ_max ≤ 1 uses σ=σmax+u(σmin−σmax); otherwise Karras mapping with ρ=7 and u as ramp. Then 0.

props.shape: ramp warp mapped through Karras or linear

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Adept Hybrid JYS-Karras
entries.plain: Log-space blend of JYS with a golden-angle-jittered Karras, weighted by position.
entries.math:
w ramps .2→.6→.9 by position; ln σ=lerp(ln karras, ln jys, w); × (1−.05(1−pos)²).
Unless noted: σ_max ≤ 1 uses σ=σmax+u(σmin−σmax); otherwise Karras mapping with ρ=7 and u as ramp. Then 0.

props.shape: ramp warp mapped through Karras or linear

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Adept Jittered Karras
entries.plain: Karras with random offset per step, then sorted. The random draw is unseeded in this function.
entries.math:
u_i=clamp(i+.5+(rand−.5)·j,0,n−1)/(n−1); sorted descending.
Unless noted: σ_max ≤ 1 uses σ=σmax+u(σmin−σmax); otherwise Karras mapping with ρ=7 and u as ramp. Then 0.

props.shape: ramp warp mapped through Karras or linear

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The first u is i+0.5 based, so the top value starts below σmax, and the schedule changes per run (adept_schedulers.py:289-291).

entries.name: Adept JYS (Jump Your Steps)
entries.plain: Hand-built timestep ladder in phases: 1000→600 fast, 600→300, 300→200 dense, then the rest. It is a heuristic ladder computed from step count, not an optimised table.
entries.math:
t from _compute_jys_timesteps; u=(1000−t)/1000. Sorted.
Unless noted: σ_max ≤ 1 uses σ=σmax+u(σmin−σmax); otherwise Karras mapping with ρ=7 and u as ramp. Then 0.

props.shape: ramp warp mapped through Karras or linear

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Adept LogSNR-Uniform
entries.plain: Called log-SNR uniform; with σ_max>1 it is the same curve as exponential.
entries.math: σ=exp((2 ln σmax + u(2 ln σmin − 2 ln σmax))/2) = exp(ln σmax + u(ln σmin−ln σmax)). σ_max≤1: linear.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Algebraically identical to core exponential for σmax>1; on flow models (σmax≤1) it silently turns linear (adept_schedulers.py:240-244).

entries.name: Adept SNR-Optimized
entries.plain: Blends a sigmoid and a linear ramp in log-sigma space, which the code calls log SNR.
entries.math: t'=.7·sigmoid(3(t−.5))+.3t; σ=exp((2 ln σmax + t'(2 ln σmin −2 ln σmax))/2). σ_max≤1: linear with t'.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Sigmoid is not rescaled, so t' starts above 0 and ends below 1 and the schedule misses both σmax and σmin (adept_schedulers.py:160-164).

entries.name: Adept Stochastic
entries.plain: Base ramp with random perturbation: Brownian, normal or uniform. Sorted, with a monotonic guard.
entries.math:
u=clamp(base+noise·scale,0,1); sort desc; guard σ_i<σ_{i−1}.
Unless noted: σ_max ≤ 1 uses σ=σmax+u(σmin−σmax); otherwise Karras mapping with ρ=7 and u as ramp. Then 0.

props.shape: ramp warp mapped through Karras or linear

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Adept Tanh Mid-Boost
entries.plain: Tanh S-curve of the ramp, normalised to the endpoints.
entries.math:
u=.5(tanh(k(r−.5))/tanh(k/2)+1), k=4.
Unless noted: σ_max ≤ 1 uses σ=σmax+u(σmin−σmax); otherwise Karras mapping with ρ=7 and u as ramp. Then 0.

props.shape: ramp warp mapped through Karras or linear

entries.name: AIToolkit FlowMatch Sampler
entries.plain: Rebuilds an ai-toolkit trainer's sigma list for inference, by a formula path or an exact path that imports the toolkit's scheduler if present. Config table per model holds shift values.

t=linspace(1,1/n,n) (force_aitk_timesteps) or linspace(1,0,n+1)[:-1].
Resolution-aware: L=(w//16)(h//16), μ=line(L), σ=dynamic shift(μ,t). Else static shift.

entries.plain: Builds an AYS-style schedule from timestep indices rather than from sigma values, so it reads sigmas from the loaded model's table, with log-linear resampling for the step count. This is why, unlike the core AYS node, it does follow the loaded model.

entries.name: AsymFlux2 resolution square-root shift
entries.plain: A flow schedule whose shift grows with image size, linear in the square root of the pixel count. Unusually large values: 17 at 1024² and 34 at 2048².

entries.name: Beta presets (beta_33, beta_44, beta_53, …)

Same as core beta with (α,β): beta_33 (.3,.3), beta_44 (.4,.4), beta_53 (.5,.3), beta_54 (.5,.4), beta_57 (.5,.7), beta_32 (.3,.2), beta_43 (.4,.3), beta_42 (.4,.2).
n = steps + ⌊steps/20⌋ for 32 and 43; n = steps + ⌊steps/10⌋ for 42.

entries.name: bong_tangent (RES4LYF)
entries.plain: Two-segment arctangent-shaped scheduler registered under this name. Several other packs carry copies or rewrites. One-line fact only, under the licence terms for this pack.

entries.name: Boyo chaotic and non-monotonic sigmas
entries.plain: Experimental schedules. Logistic map or Hénon map values are scaled and sorted into a descending list, or random bumps are added to a simple schedule so sigma rises at some steps. Seeded. Non-monotonic mode really sends sigma upward.
entries.math:
Logistic: x←3.99x(1−x). Hénon: (x,y)←(1−1.4x²+y, .3x), normalised. σ=sort_desc(raw(1−σmin)+σmin), then 0.

entries.name: Detail Daemon schedule
entries.plain: Keeps the real schedule but tells the model the sigma is a little lower than it is, by an amount that follows a per-step ramp. The model removes less noise than the sampler expects, leaving more fine texture. Its ramp is a separate schedule: rises to a peak at bias between start and end, then falls. The original ComfyUI-Detail-Daemon pack has no source in the library; this is read from copies in other packs (compared by reading one, not diffed).
entries.math:
Ramp over steps n: mid = start + bias·(end−start); up-values on [i_start, i_mid], down on [i_mid, i_end].
v(u) = u or ½(1−cos πu) (smooth), then v^exponent, scaled to span offset → amount. Outside: start_offset / end_offset. All × (1−fade).
At model call with sigma σ: look up m(σ) by lerp between neighbouring steps' ramp values.
σ_model = σ · max(1e-6, 1 − 0.1·m(σ)·cfg). Real step uses unchanged σ.

props.shape: amount ramp per step, sigma multiplied at call
props.params: start, end, bias, amount, exponent, start_offset, end_offset, fade, smooth, cfg_scale_override

entries.name: Echo DMD sigmas + conditioning remap
entries.plain: Sigmas at preset points for a DMD-trained model, plus a node that rewrites a sigma list. Nearest snaps each value to the closest trained anchor. Interpolated returns the value unchanged inside the anchor range, because its lerp cancels out. entries.name: Fixed-shift flow one-liners (Iris, LLaDA turbo, Bernini, DMAD, AsymFlux2)
entries.plain: Many model packs write the same ramp-through-flow-shift formula with their own fixed shift, or a small variation at the top end. Listed once. Differences are the shift value, the starting t, and whether a zero is appended.
entries.math:
σ = s·t/(1+(s−1)t), t a linear ramp.
Iris: s=4, t=flip(1−linspace(1,.001,n+1)).
LLaDA turbo: s=3.
Bernini UniPC: t=linspace(.999,0,n+1)[:-1].
DMAD: s=model shift or 12, t=linspace(1,0,n+1).
AsymFlux2: s from a square-root function of pixel count.

entries.name: FlowMatch Scheduler (ai-toolkit style, with random types)
entries.plain: Multi-mode scheduler: linear, shift, shift_exponential, flux_shift with resolution μ, plus sigmoid and lognorm_blend types whose sigmas are random draws that get sorted. Those two types mirror training timestep sampling and change per run. Options add bell-curve weighting and terminal stretch.
entries.math:
linear: linspace(1,0,n+1)[:-1].
sigmoid: σ=sorted(1−sigmoid(randn(n))).
lognorm_blend: α·n draws 1−X/max X (LogNormal) ∪ linspace; sorted.
shift: e^μ/(e^μ+(1/t−1)) or μt/(1+(μ−1)t).
bell: y=e^{−2((i−n/2)/n)²}; w=(y−min y)·n/Σ; σ×w/mean w.
terminal: stretched=term+(σ−σ_{−2})·(1−term)/(σ₀−σ_{−2}).
Then 0 (or 1 if inverted).

props.params: scheduler_type, shift, base_shift=0.5, max_shift=1.16, shift_terminal, use_bell_curve, lognorm_alpha=0.75, lognorm_scale=0.333

entries.name: FlowMatch scheduler (DiffSynth-style)

entries.name: H3 second-pass staggered schedule
entries.plain: Builds a second-pass H3 schedule in two separate moves. The starting sigma is copied from a known scheduler, step count and denoise recipe, then a shorter front-loaded curve runs from there to near zero, so the first step does most of the work of removing the upscale grid. This avoids swapping the scheduler name in a trim, which its docstring says reaches a very different start sigma.
entries.math:
total = int(reference_steps/denoise) if denoise<1 else reference_steps.
σ_start = calculate_sigmas(base_scheduler, total)[−(reference_steps+1)].
σ_min = min(max(sampling.sigma_min, 1e-3), σ_start/2).
σ = karras | exponential | polyexponential(steps, σ_min, σ_start, ρ); higher ρ front-loads more.

entries.name: LC Detail Daemon (modes)
entries.plain: A rewrite of the Detail Daemon idea with the CFG multiplier removed and two extra modes. In look only, the answer is rescaled back to the real noise level. In keep structure, it runs the model twice and only keeps the high-frequency part of the difference.

entries.name: MD Hybrid Adaptive Sigmas
entries.plain: Single node with many modes, written as standalone formulas without reading the model's table. Several modes reuse core scheduler names for different curves, so results won't match core. Chunks can chain modes. The output usually ends at sigma_min, so a trailing zero depends on node options not read here.
entries.math:
ays: L=logistic(10(t−.5)) normalised; c=.7L+.3e^{−2t}; σ=σmin+(σmax−σmin)(1−c/max c).
beta: b=1−(1−t^α)^β; σ=σmax(1−b)+σmin·b.
simple: σ=σmax−(σmax−σmin)(3t²−2t³).
sgm_uniform: linear in σ. ddim_uniform: σmin+(σmax−σmin)√(t/T) over integer stride.
bong_tangent: θ=tπ/4; τ=norm(tan θ); σ=σmax(1−τ)+σmin·τ; final σmin (not 0).
poly: linear in σ^{1/p}. blended_curves: (1−b)karras+b·linear. variance_preserving, exponential, karras_rho, kl_optimal, linear_quadratic (threshold 0.0025) also.
Smoother: Gaussian, EMA or moving average blended by strength.

entries.surprise: Mode 'ays' is a logistic formula with no AYS table, 'beta' is 1−(1−t^α)^β rather than Beta quantiles, and 'simple' is smoothstep: same names, different schedules from core (hybrid_scheduler_core.py:134-176).

audit.note: Formulas match, with omissions a reader would misjudge. ddim_uniform as coded is ascending: flip(1000−k·stride) rises, so σ goes σmin→σmax unless reversed (MDMAchine__ComfyUI_MD_Nodes/core/hybrid_scheduler_core.py:154-162). ays does not start at σmax: c(0)=0.3, max c≈0.74, so σ₀≈σmin+0.6(σmax−σmin) (lines 144-152). "Chunks can chain modes" refers to split_schedule with mode_b (schedulers/MD_HybridSigmaScheduler.py:418-422); memory chunks reuse one mode (core:188-203). Plain "ends at sigma_min": karras and kl_optimal end at 0 (core:56-74).

entries.name: RALU NT-DM schedule fit
entries.plain: Fits per-stage shifts so the mixed-resolution schedule spends time where the normal schedule would, measured by Jensen-Shannon distance on a 1000 point grid. Used only when you give custom stage steps and ends; presets carry the fitted numbers. Needs scipy.
entries.math:
q_h(t)=h/(1+(h−1)t)². Each stage covers [s_k,e_k] with N_k steps.
Target p=(q_h₀+Σ_k (e_k−s_{k+1})·q_h₀|[s_{k+1},e_k])/(1+Σ(e_k−s_{k+1})).
Schedule Q=Σ N_k q_{h_k}|[s_k,e_k] /ΣN.
Minimise JS(p,Q) over h₁..₃∈[.5,10], Z∈[2,100], start [3,3,3,2].
Stage σ: linear in σ between warps of 1−s_k and 1−e_k.

entries.name: Sigma splice (sigmas_concat)
entries.plain: Replaces the tail of one schedule with the tail of another at an index. Its optional rescale multiplies by Σresult/Σσ₁, which pushes the sum further from the first schedule rather than matching it: matching would need the inverse ratio.
entries.math: σ = σ₁[:k] ++ σ₂[k:]. rescale_sum: σ·(Σσ/Σσ₁).
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The rescale factor multiplies by the ratio of sums rather than dividing by it, so a schedule whose sum grew gets larger still (sigmas_merge.py:209).

audit.note: The first draft said the rescale makes the sums match. The code multiplies by Σresult/Σσ₁, which does not.

entries.name: sigmas_* toolbox (RES4LYF)
entries.plain: A file holding 81 classes, of which 71 are named sigmas_*. By name they cover arithmetic, cleanup, splits, and shaping functions such as sigmoid, easing, hyperbolic, gaussian, Lambert W, plus exotic names (Collatz, Conway, persistent homology). These class names were read; the bodies were not. Short entry, see the tribute page.

entries.name: SigmasFunction (including plain cosine)
entries.plain: One node with a menu of unit-range curves. It's where the simplest cosine and exponential ramps live, plus Gaussian, polynomial fit of points, custom expressions and a Qwen Image 2.1 option.
entries.math:
exponential: linspace(1,0,n+1)^p. cosine: cos(linspace(0,π/2,n+1)). gauss: x∈[0,p], (G(x)−G(p))/(1−G(p)), G=e^{−x²} per label.
Also polynomial, polygon, custom, manual, qwen21; each scaled by scale.

props.params: function, steps, p, scale, points, custom_function, x_from, x_to, clip

entries.name: SigmaWaveForm generators
entries.plain: Generate a sequence from a sine, sawtooth, stepped, square or random wave rather than a monotonic schedule. Companion nodes do Fourier filtering, attenuation and a phase-locked loop on sigmas. Because the output isn't descending, the result only makes sense as an experiment or a modulation source.
entries.math: t=linspace(0,1,steps). σ=wave(t; amplitude, frequency) with optional damping and Fourier steps; 'unidirectional' subtracts min (plus min_sigma in the Advanced class).

props.params: steps, amplitude, frequency, damping_factor, waveform_type, enable_unidirectional, min_sigma

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: 'Unidirectional' only shifts the wave up so it is non-negative; it does not make the sequence descend (sigma_waveform_node.py:69-70).

audit.note: +min_sigma is not Advanced-only: SigmaWaveFormNode also has it (BenNarum__SigmaWaveFormNode/sigma_waveform_node.py:193-194, 342-343); only the Simple class subtracts min alone (line 69). The cited line 72 is the Simple class, which has no Fourier step.

entries.name: Sigmax model-aware profiles
entries.plain: A large pack composing schedules from named parts (base grid, shift, terminal policy) per model profile, with strict validity checks. Base grids and shifts were read. Profile choice and turbo presets were read only for the LTX table.
entries.math:
Base: (n−i)/n reciprocal, table-matching simple grid, or linear endpoints.
Shift: logistic(μ−e·ln((1−t)/t)), or ratio form 1/(1+(1−t)/(r·t)).
Terminal: preserve or append 0.
LTX table: (1, .99375, .9875, .98125, .975, .909375, .725, .421875, 0).
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The Sigmax LTX stage-1 table equals the PowerShift pack's BASE_SIGMA_POINTS with a final 0 (ltx.py:496; ComfyUI_PowerShiftScheduler __init__.py:17), so that 'default curve' is the LTX stage-1 ladder (equality read from both files; provenance inferred).

entries.name: Sigmoid Offset Scheduler
entries.plain: Picks table indices along a normalised sigmoid. square_k sets steepness, and base_c shifts the midpoint. Node adds a start_sigma rescale.
entries.math:
S(x)=1/(1+e^{−k((8x−4)+4·s)}), s=2(c−0.5).
n(x)=(S(x)−S(0))/(S(1)−S(0)).
t_i=rint((1−n(i/steps))·M), M=len(table)−1, skip repeats. Last sigma set to 0 if ≤σmin, else 0 appended.
Node: if start≠1, σ'=(σ−min)·start/(max−min).
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Simple sigma ops (invert, offset, scale to range, rerange)
entries.plain: Small transforms on an existing schedule. Note that invert here reflects values and is different from Flip.
entries.math:
Invert: max+min−σ.
Offset: σ+o.
Scale to range: (σ−min)(hi−lo)/(max−min)+lo.
Rerange (SpliceTools): new exponential between σ₀ and last nonzero σ.
Range slice (SV): lerp-sampled sub-range of a reference.
Flip adjusted (KJ): flip, then shift indices by offset_by, optional divide by last.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: SparkDiffusion CrossDistill
entries.plain: Hard-coded mid timesteps per supported step count, with the start derived from sigma_max. Unsupported counts raise an error.
entries.math: t = (rf_start(σmax), MID_T[n]…, 0); consecutive pairs are Euler steps.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: tan_scheduler family (RES4LYF)
entries.plain: Node forms of the arctangent curve, with one-stage and two-stage versions, sgm and pad options. Takes steps, slope, offset and range directly with no model input. Short entry under the licence terms.
entries.math: Math not reproduced. See the RES4LYF tribute page.

props.params: steps, slope, offset, start, end, sgm, pad

entries.label: from code

entries.name: TBG split-aware detail enhancer
entries.plain: A lie based on neighbouring schedule points, on every third or so step: the model runs twice, once at a sigma pulled toward the next (or previous) entry in the full schedule by a chosen amount and once at the true sigma, and the two outputs are mixed. Uses a split-aware step counter to keep the place across split runs.
entries.math:
Only when counter % ceil(steps/3)=0 and counter>2; else D(x,σ).
e>0: σ_m = σ + |e|·(σ_next−σ); out = .7·D(x,σ_m)+.3·D(x,σ).
e<0: σ_m = σ + |e|·(σ_prev−σ); out = .3·D(x,σ_m)+.7·D(x,σ).
entries.label: from code

audit.note: TBG_sampler_split_aware.py:136-150: the lie applies only when counter % ceil(steps/3)==0 and counter>2. On those steps the model runs twice, at the moved σ and the true σ, and the outputs mix 0.7/0.3 for e>0 or 0.3/0.7 for e<0. The entry reads as a single lied call on every step.

entries.name: The Golden Scheduler
entries.plain: Crossfades between sigmax and sigmin using two powers of the golden ratio, in plain sigma space. No table walk, so it reads only the model's range. The sgm option drops the last value before the zero.
entries.math:
y=i/(steps−1), φ=(1+√5)/2.
σ_i = (1−y)^φ·σmax + y^φ·σmin, then 0.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: TS Shifted Sigmas
entries.plain: Takes raw few-step distill timesteps as text and bends them by the diffusers dynamic shift for the latent's token count, plus a final zero. Docstring says it was written for a Qwen Image 2.1 turbo LoRA.
entries.math: L=tokens from latent (16 px grid). μ=base+(max−base)(L−256)/(8192−256). σ=e^μ/(e^μ+(1/t−1)), then 0.

entries.name: TwinFlow Kumaraswamy schedule
entries.plain: Linear time warped by a Kumaraswamy function. With the baked-in (1,1,1) control it stays linear, so in practice this is a linear ramp with a large gap at the low end.
entries.math: t=linspace(.001, 1−g, N), g=.6 for N≤2, else .5. t←(1−(1−tᵃ)ᵇ)ᶜ, a=b=c=1. σ=1−t, then 0.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Two-scheduler split (SimKarr, Segmented)
entries.plain: Run one named scheduler for the first part of the steps and another for the rest. SimKarr builds each on its own step count. Apt computes both at full length and joins at a split, smoothing the join.
entries.math:
Apt: σ=A[:k]++B[k:]; σ_k=(1−s)σ_{k−1}+s·σ_k; σ_{k−1}=mean of neighbours.
SimKarr: first_steps=⌊n·ratio⌋ with one scheduler, the remainder with the other (join not read).

props.params: split_step, scheduler_1, scheduler_2, smooth_strength / split_ratio, mode

entries.name: Ultimate Detail Sigmas
entries.plain: Inside a centred window, warps step density and adds a boost to sigma amplitude, then restores monotonic order. Helpers were read by name only.
entries.math: mask window(start_p,end_p); σ→warp(σ,factor,mask); σ→boost(σ,boost,mask); enforce monotonic.

entries.name: WeightFerry TORS
entries.plain: A precomputed flow table by step count, with step counts absent from the table linearly interpolated from the 30-step row.
entries.math: If n in table: σ=T[n]. Else σ=interp(j/(n−1), T[30]). Then 0.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Zipf and Zeta schedulers
entries.plain: Weights steps by a power law of rank, with the exponent drifting per step, and descends by the cumulative weight. Big early jumps and a long tail. Zeta adds path shapes for the exponent.
entries.math:
Zipf: α_r=linspace(x_start,x_end,n); w_r=r^{−α_r}, normalised. c=[0, cumsum w]; σ=(1−c)(σmax−σmin)+σmin; last=σmin. No trailing 0.
Zeta: α by path linear, poly, cosine, exp, or a pivot; w=(r^{−α})^γ (rest of the function not read).

props.params: x_start, x_end; zeta: x_start=.5, x_end=3, path_type, kappa, gamma, pivot, clip_frac, range_scale

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Adaptive Projected Guidance (core)
entries.plain: Splits the guidance direction into a part along the positive prediction and a part across it, then weights them. It optionally averages the direction over steps and caps its norm. In core it rewrites cond before linear CFG, so later hooks see a modified cond, and the result carries one more unit of guidance than the Sana pack: with η=1 and no cap, core gives the effect of cfg s+1 even though its tooltip says default CFG behaviour. The Sana pack returns x̂_c+(s−1)·g' directly.
entries.math:
g = x̂_c − x̂_u
momentum β≠0: v ← β·v + g, g ← v (v reset when sigma rises)
threshold T>0: g ← g·min(1, T/‖g‖₂) over last 3 dims
g∥ = (g·û)û with û = x̂_c/‖x̂_c‖ over last 3 dims; g⊥ = g − g∥
g' = g⊥ + η·g∥
x̂_c' = x̂_u + g' + (x̂_c−x̂_u)/s, then linear CFG.
Core result: x̂_cfg = x̂_u + s·g' + (x̂_c − x̂_u) = x̂_c + s·g'
Sana pack: x̂ = x̂_c + (s−1)·g', norms over [C,H,W] on 5-D latents in its default hw mode.

providers.author: smthemex
providers.note: Video norm dims chosen by mode hw (default), thw or t; momentum buffer and threshold as in core; rest of body not read

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The update has an extra (x̂_c−x̂_u) term beyond s·g′: the code adds (cond−uncond)/s to cond, so after CFG an unprojected guidance step at scale 1 remains. Effective form s·g′+Δ, not s·g′ alone.

audit.note: The math is right for core, but it is presented as one method with the Sana pack, which differs. Sana returns x̂_c + (s−1)·g' (Sana/diffusion/guiders/adaptive_projected_guidance.py:144), while core reduces to x̂_c + s·g' (ComfyUI/comfy_extras/nodes_apg.py:93 then samplers.py:598), one more unit of guidance. Sana on 5-D latents defaults to dims [C,H,W] (mode hw, lines 113, 119-120), not the last 3 dims. Plain's "aiming to allow high cfg with less over-saturation" is not stated in the code it cites. Core consequence worth stating: with η=1 and no threshold the result is x̂_u+(s+1)(x̂_c−x̂_u), although the eta tooltip says default CFG behaviour (nodes_apg.py:28).

entries.name: Basic Guider (cond only)
entries.plain: A guider with only one conditioning. Its inherited cfg stays 1.0, so the negative pass never runs. Used for models that embed guidance (Flux and similar) or for no-CFG sampling.
entries.math: x̂ = x̂_c (CFGGuider default cfg = 1.0; negative is absent so sampling_function gets uncond = None).

entries.name: CFG++ (sampler mechanism)
entries.plain: Not a node but a change in the sampler step: the x0 jump uses the guided prediction, while the re-noising direction uses the negative prediction. This lets it run at small cfg (the sampler's direction is not amplified). The trick is a post-CFG function that captures x̂_u and forces the negative pass at cfg 1.
entries.math:
euler_ancestral_cfg_pp, with α=σ·exp(λ(σ)):
d = (x − α_s·x̂_u)/σ_s
σ↓,σ↑ = ancestral(σ_s/α_s, σ_t/α_t, η); σ↓ ← α_t·σ↓
x_t = α_t·x̂_cfg + σ↓·d + α_t·ξ·s_noise·σ↑ (when η,s_noise>0).
η=0 for euler_cfg_pp: x_t = α_t·x̂_cfg + σ_t·d.
dpmpp_2m_cfg_pp: x_t = x̂_cfg + mix + e^{−h}·x with mix = −e^{−h}·x̂_u (first or last step), else −e^{−h}·x̂_u − expm1(−h)/(2r)·(x̂_cfg − x̂_u,prev).
gradient_estimation_cfg_pp: here d = (x − x̂_u)/σ_s with no α; x_t = x̂_cfg + d·σ_t, plus (γ−1)(d−d_prev)·dt from step 2.

audit.note: The gradient_estimation_cfg_pp line reuses d, which the entry defines with the α_s factor, (x−α_s·x̂_u)/σ_s. That sampler has no α: d=(x−x̂_u)/σ_s (sampling.py:1563), so the formula is wrong on flow models where α_s≠1. It also applies only when σ_t>0 and i≥1 for the correction (sampling.py:1569-1582).

entries.name: CFG++ history sampler (cfgpp_ud10_ab)
entries.plain: A core-side CFG++ step with two-step Adams-Bashforth blending of the derivative. The step is built from the guided x0 and the negative's direction, then lerped with a linear-multistep estimate. An optional zero-sigma extrapolation adjusts the last step.
entries.math:
d_u = (x−α_s·x̂_u)/σ_s, optional + w_u·(dt/dt_prev)·(d_u−d_u,prev)
E = α_t·x̂_cfg + σ_t·d_u − x, d = E/dt
x_t = x + lerp(E, c₁d + c₂d_prev, w_h)
Optional zero_weight blend at the final step uses history of denoised (order 1 or 2).
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Unlike other CFG++ samplers, it does not disable the cfg 1 skip; it falls back to cond_denoised when uncond is None.

entries.name: CFG-Zero★ (optimized scale, core)
entries.plain: Rescales the negative prediction by the amount that best matches the positive, before CFG mixes them. The core node has no zero-init of early steps, only the optimized scale. It takes no parameters.
entries.math:
α = ⟨x−x̂_c, x−x̂_u⟩ / (‖x−x̂_u‖²+1e-8), per batch item
x̂ = x̂_cfg + (α−1)·x̂_u + s·(1−α)·x̂_u
which equals α·x̂_u + s·(x̂_c − α·x̂_u).
α is measured in x−x̂ space and applied to x0 predictions.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Core has no zero-init phase despite the name; alpha is computed on x−x̂ and applied to x̂.

entries.name: CFGNorm (attenuating, post-CFG)
entries.plain: Limits the guided prediction's channel-wise norm to the positive prediction's norm, so high cfg cannot grow its magnitude. The strength here is a plain multiplier on the whole result, not a blend.
entries.math:
scale = clamp(‖x̂_c‖₂,dim=1 / (‖x̂_cfg‖₂,dim=1 + 1e-8), 0, 1)
x̂ = x̂_cfg · scale · strength
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: strength multiplies the whole x0 prediction: strength 0 gives x̂=0, not plain CFG. Compare the pre_cfg mode, which blends.

entries.name: CFGNorm pre_cfg mode (norm-scaled CFG)
entries.plain: A second, separate behaviour inside the same node. It works on the noise-side difference, replaces the CFG line, and can raise as well as lower magnitude. The tooltip says it matches models like Lens.
entries.math:
c = x−x̂_c, u = x−x̂_u, m = u + s·(c−u)
r = ‖c‖₂,dim=1 / max(‖m‖₂,dim=1, 1e-12), or 1 if ‖m‖ = 0
f = strength·m·r + (1−strength)·m; x̂ = x − f

claims.text: matches norm-scaled CFG used by Lens
claims.label: from pack README claim

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Despite the name pre_cfg, it installs a sampler_cfg_function, not a pre-CFG hook.

entries.name: Classifier-free guidance (linear)
entries.plain: The default mixing rule every guidance scale in ComfyUI goes through. The model is run on the positive and the negative conditioning, and the result is pushed along their difference by the cfg number. At cfg 1 the negative pass is skipped unless a sampler or hook disables that shortcut, so the negative prediction is all zeros. A custom cfg function replaces the line, and post-CFG functions run afterwards on its result.
entries.math:
x̂_cfg = x̂_u + s·(x̂_c − x̂_u)
x̂_c, x̂_u = cond and uncond denoised (x0) predictions, s = cond_scale.
If model_options has sampler_cfg_function f: x̂_cfg = x − f({cond: x − x̂_c, uncond: x − x̂_u, ...}), so f works in x − x̂ space.
Then for each post-CFG function g in order: x̂_cfg ← g({denoised: x̂_cfg, cond_denoised, uncond_denoised, ...}).
entries.label: from code

audit.note: Plain says the model is run on both conditionings, which is false at cfg≈1: sampling_function drops uncond unless disable_cfg1_optimization is set (ComfyUI/comfy/samplers.py:610-613). x̂_u is then an all-zero tensor, and hooks receive that zero tensor as uncond_denoised. The line still gives x̂_c at s=1.

entries.name: Dual CFG Guider, nested style
entries.plain: Same three conditionings, but CFG is applied inside CFG: the first positive is guided against the second, and the result is then guided against the negative. It always runs all three.
entries.math:
x̂_text = cfg_function(cond=x̂_p, uncond=x̂_m, s₁)
x̂ = x̂_n + s₂·(x̂_text − x̂_n)
Here post-CFG hooks run on the inner step only, not on the final line.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The cfg1 skip is not available in nested style: all three conds are always evaluated.

entries.name: Dual CFG Guider, regular style
entries.plain: Two positive conditionings with their own scales. The second positive is compared against the negative by normal CFG, then the first positive adds its own difference from the second on top.
entries.math:
x̂ = cfg_function(cond=x̂_m, uncond=x̂_n, s₂) + s₁·(x̂_p − x̂_m)
with plain cfg_function: x̂ = x̂_n + s₂·(x̂_m − x̂_n) + s₁·(x̂_p − x̂_m)
x̂_p cond1, x̂_m cond2 (middle), x̂_n negative. s₁ = cfg_conds, s₂ = cfg_cond2_negative.

props.extra_model_calls: 3; negative dropped if s₂≈1, then middle also dropped if s₁≈1 too

entries.name: Dual Model CFG Guider
entries.plain: Runs the positive pass on one model and the negative pass on another. It is the core way to do CFG where the two sides are different checkpoints, and loads the second model only when cfg is not 1. This is a mix of model pair, not autoguidance by name.
entries.math:
x̂ = cfg_function(cond=M_main(x; c), uncond=M_neg(x; n), s).
No uncond model is loaded when s≈1 at start; if s≈1 on a step, only cond is returned.

entries.name: Epsilon Scaling
entries.plain: Divides the predicted noise of the final result by a constant slightly above 1, to fight exposure bias. Applied after CFG.
entries.math:
ε = x − x̂_cfg; x̂ = x − ε/k
k = scaling_factor (0 is replaced by 1e-9).

entries.name: Euler CFG++ node sampler (core nodes_advanced_samplers)
entries.plain: An alternative form of CFG++ in core, chosen by version=alternative on the Euler CFG++ sampler node (version=regular uses euler_cfg_pp instead). It is the plain Euler step whose derivative is taken with the x−x̂_cfg+x̂_u substitution.
entries.math: d = (x − x̂_cfg + x̂_u − x̂_cfg)/σ, x_t = x + d·dt (to_d with x replaced by x − x̂_cfg + x̂_u).

evidence.symbol: d = to_d(x - denoised + temp[0], sigmas[i], denoised)

audit.note: nodes_advanced_samplers.py:136-139: sample_euler_pp is what version='alternative' of the Euler CFG++ node selects; 'regular' uses ksampler euler_cfg_pp. Nothing in the code shows it is older, and the update is not the same as the regular form. Math is correct.

entries.name: FreSca (frequency scaling of guidance)
entries.plain: Scales the guidance difference differently in low and high Fourier bands before CFG, usually boosting highs. It leaves the negative alone. A center box is low frequency.
entries.math:
g = x̂_c − x̂_u; G = fftshift(FFT₂(g))
G ← G·mask, mask = scale_low inside center box ±freq_cutoff, scale_high outside
x̂_c' = x̂_u + Re IFFT(ifftshift G); then normal CFG.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Guidance hook pipeline (sampling_function)
entries.plain: The order in which all guidance hooks run for one model evaluation. Knowing it explains why a pre-CFG node sees different data from a post-CFG node, and why extra negative passes are skipped at cfg 1. Hooks reading the uncond output at cfg 1 get zeros, not the cond output.
entries.math:
1. If s ≈ 1 and disable_cfg1_optimization is false, uncond = None (one model pass; x̂_u stays an all-zero tensor, and cfg_function has no cfg=1 branch, so linear CFG gives 0+(x̂_c−0)·s).
2. outs = sampler_calc_cond_batch_function(args) if set, else calc_cond_batch(model,[cond,uncond],x,t).
3. For each sampler_pre_cfg_function: outs ← fn(conds_out=outs,...). Output space is x0/denoised.
4. cfg_function(outs[0], outs[1], s): custom sampler_cfg_function or linear, then post-CFG list.

props.extra_model_calls: 1 (cond only) or 2 (cond + uncond) by default, plus whatever hooks add

entries.label: from code

audit.note: The first draft said uncond output equals cond at cfg 1. It is zeros.

entries.name: Latent Apply Operation CFG
entries.plain: Runs any LATENT_OPERATION on the guidance difference (or on the only output, when cfg is 1) in a percent window, before CFG.
entries.math:
Two outputs: x̂_c ← op(x̂_c−x̂_u)+x̂_u
One output: x̂_c ← op(x̂_c)

entries.name: LTXAV identity guidance
entries.plain: Encodes reference audio and adds a positive pass without it, so the difference pushes toward the reference voice.
entries.math:
x̂_nr = M(x; c without ref_audio)
in window: x̂ = x̂_cfg + w·(x̂_c − x̂_nr)

entries.name: LTXAV modality guidance
entries.plain: A pass with audio-video cross-attention cut in both directions; the difference pushes the two modalities to agree more.
entries.math:
x̂_m = M(x; c, a2v=False, v2a=False)
in window: x̂ = x̂_cfg + (w−1)·(x̂_c − x̂_m)
entries.label: from code

entries.name: LTXV Dual CFG Guider (video/audio scales)
entries.plain: Separate cfg numbers for the video and audio part of a packed AV latent. Equal scales or a non-AV latent fall back to normal CFG.
entries.math: f = u + s_v(c−u); for elements after the video size: f[v:] = u[v:] + s_a(c[v:]−u[v:]).

entries.name: LTXV Spatio-Temporal Guidance (core)
entries.plain: An extra positive pass with self-attention disabled at selected blocks of LTXV. It uses a transformer option, not a patch replace.
entries.math:
x̂_p = M(x; c, stg_self_attn_blocks=B)
in window: x̂ = x̂_cfg + w·(x̂_c − x̂_p)

family_fit.why: Relies on stg_self_attn_blocks transformer option of LTXV

entries.name: Mahiro (Positive-Biased Guidance)
entries.plain: Blends standard CFG with a pure positive extrapolation. The blend weight comes from how similar a compressed negative leap is to the merged result: similar means more ordinary CFG, dissimilar more positive leap. No parameters.
entries.math:
L = s·x̂_c, U = s·x̂_u, M = (L + x̂_cfg)/2
normU = sign(U)√|U|, normM = sign(M)√|M|
q = mean cosine_similarity(normU, normM) (dim=1)
k = 2(q+1)
x̂ = (k·x̂_cfg + (4−k)·L)/4
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Normalized Attention Guidance (core DiT form)
entries.plain: Applies a negative prompt inside attention rather than at the end, so it can work on models run at cfg 1. Core reads both cond and uncond tokens at each self-attention output, extrapolates, caps the L1 norm ratio, blends, and overwrites. Because it needs both in the same batch, it disables the cfg 1 skip.
entries.math:
z̃ = z₊·φ − z₋·(φ−1)
r = max(‖z̃‖₁,1e-6) / max(‖z₊‖₁,1e-6), norm over last dim
ẑ = z̃·min(r,τ)/r
z = α·ẑ + (1−α)·z₊
z₊,z₋ are attention output tokens for cond/uncond. Only applied when both cond and uncond are in the batch. With img_slice both batch parts are overwritten; without it only the positive part is.

entries.surprise: Core runs NAG on attn1 output with the normal negative in the batch, where the original fork family uses a separate NAG negative through cross-attention.

entries.name: Perp-Neg
entries.plain: Removes from the negative prompt's effect the part that points along the positive prompt, so a negative cannot cancel what the positive asks for. It needs a third, empty-prompt pass as the base.
entries.math:
p = x̂_c − x̂_∅,  n = x̂_n − x̂_∅
n⊥ = n − (⟨n,p⟩/‖p‖²)·p   (the dot and norm are over the whole batch tensor, one number)
x̂ = x̂_∅ + s·(p − w·n⊥)
w = neg_scale, s = cfg.

props.extra_model_calls: 3; deprecated PerpNeg node adds one extra pass inside cfg function; guider drops neg if w≈0 and empty too if s≈1

entries.name: Perturbed-Attention Guidance (core)
entries.plain: An extra positive pass with one self-attention block disabled. The difference between the normal and the broken pass adds structural guidance on top of CFG. The core node is locked to the SD UNet middle block.
entries.math:
x̂_pag = M(x; c) with attn1 of block middle/0 replaced: attn(q,k,v) → v
x̂ = x̂_cfg + w·(x̂_c − x̂_pag)
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The patch is keyed to UNet middle block 0, so on DiT models with no such attn1 key it does nothing except cost a pass (inference from the patch key).

entries.name: RenormCFG (Lumina2, core)
entries.plain: Lumina's CFG: it splits off extra output channels, applies CFG only only below a sigma limit (cfg_trunc), and caps the norm of the result relative to the positive. At or above the truncation value, which is compared with sigma, it returns the positive only (the negative still costs a pass).
entries.math:
σ<cfg_trunc: e = u + s(c−u) on the first in_channels; ‖e‖≥ρ‖c‖ → e ← e·ρ‖c‖/‖e‖ (when ρ>0)
σ≥cfg_trunc: e = c
result channels = cat(e, cond's extra channels)
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Comparison t<cfg_trunc is on the raw timestep arg, which at this point is sigma-scale, so cfg_trunc units depend on the model sampling (inference).

audit.note: comfy/samplers.py:594: cfg_function passes the sampler sigma as args['timestep'], so nodes_lumina2.py:33 compares sigma with cfg_trunc, not a model timestep or time. Also the inputs here are x0 predictions, despite the _eps names.

entries.name: RescaleCFG (core, v-pred and flow branches)
entries.plain: Pulls the standard deviation of the guided output back toward that of the positive, counteracting the burn-out from high cfg on zero-terminal-SNR models. Core converts to v-prediction space for ε-style models, and has a separate branch for flow models that works in x0 space.
entries.math:
Non-flow: v_c, v_u from x−x̂ with sigma; v_cfg = v_u + s(v_c−v_u)
ratio = std(v_c)/std(v_cfg) over dims 1,2,3
v_f = m·v_cfg·ratio + (1−m)·v_cfg; return as x−x̂.
Flow (CONST sampling): same formula on x̂_c, x̂_u directly, std over all non-batch dims, ro_cfg clamped ≥1e-8.

entries.name: Restore-CFG (core model patch)
entries.plain: Pulls the guided x0 toward a VAE round-trip of the reference latent, more strongly at high sigma.
entries.math: If σ > s_tmin: x̂ ← x̂ − (x̂ − x_ref)·(σ/σ_max)^ρ, σ_max = 14.6146 (hard-coded), x_ref = encode(decode(hint)).

entries.name: Self-Attention Guidance (core)
entries.plain: Saves the negative pass's self-attention map, blurs the negative's x0 prediction only where attention is high, re-noises it, and runs another negative pass. The difference adds guidance for the attended areas.
entries.math:
m = (GAP of attention scores, summed) > 1.0, upsampled to latent
x̂_deg = blur(x̂_u, 9×9, σ_b)·m + x̂_u·(1−m)
x_deg = x̂_deg + x − x̂_u
x̂_s = M(x_deg; n)
x̂ = x̂_cfg + w·(x̂_deg − x̂_s)

entries.plain: An extra positive pass with chosen transformer blocks skipped, for models with no attention map to swap. The difference is added on top of CFG within a sigma window, with optional rescale. Uses the patch keys double_block/single_block.

entries.name: Skip Layer Guidance Simple (uncond only)
entries.plain: Does not add a pass. It runs the negative pass with blocks skipped in place of the normal negative pass, so CFG itself carries the perturbation. Cheaper than SLG, but gives no separate scale.

In window: x̂_u = M(x; n) with listed blocks skipped; x̂_c normal; then normal CFG.
Outside window, and at cfg 1: normal batch.

entries.name: Tangential Damping CFG (TCFG, core)
entries.plain: Reshapes the negative prediction so it lies on the main axis shared by the positive and negative. It removes the negative's off-axis part before CFG. No parameters in core.
entries.math:
Per batch item, flat c=x−x̂_c, u=x−x̂_u, A=[u;c] (2×N).
SVD A = UΣVᴴ; v₁ first right singular vector.
u_td = (u·v₁)v₁; x̂_u' = x − u_td; then normal CFG.

entries.name: Temporal Score Rescaling (TSR)
entries.plain: Scales the score by a time-dependent factor r computed from SNR to change sample diversity. The result moves between x/α (no denoising) and the guided x0.
entries.math:
r = compute_tsr_rescaling_factor(snr, k, σ²_tsr), snr = exp(2·λ(σ)), α=σ·exp(λ)
x̂ = lerp(x/α, x̂_cfg, r)
No change when k=1, σ=0 or snr=0.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Video Linear CFG Guidance
entries.plain: Gives each batch element (video frame) its own cfg: lowest for the first frame, full for the last. Made for frame-as-batch video models. It has no effect in a single-element batch other than using min_cfg.
entries.math:
s_i = linspace(s_min, s, B)[i], B = batch size
f = u + s_i·(c − u)
In a batch of 1, torch linspace gives s_min, so the node's cfg is ignored (inference from linspace behaviour).

entries.name: Video Triangle CFG Guidance
entries.plain: Same idea with a triangle over frames: min at the start and end, full in the middle.
entries.math:
v = 2·|t − ⌊t+0.5⌋|, t = linspace(0,1,B)
s_i = v_i·(s − s_min) + s_min
f = u + s_i·(c − u)

entries.name: "NAG" in output space (RT-RareTools)
entries.plain: Named NAG and citing the NAG equations, but it runs on the model's whole denoised prediction, not on attention. It is CFG with an L1-norm cap and blend, done over the whole image.
entries.math:
g = x̂_c·φ − x̂_n·(φ−1)
r = ‖g‖₁/(‖x̂_c‖₁+1e-7), over all non-batch dims
if r>τ: g ← g·‖x̂_c‖₁τ/(‖g‖₁+1e-7)
x̂ = α·g + (1−α)·x̂_c

props.extra_model_calls: 2 (RT_NAG_Guider), or 1 extra (model patch when no uncond is passed)

entries.name: "SMC-CFG" stateless sign bias (belgiangurista)
entries.plain: Labelled SMC but has no memory or sliding surface. It adds a fixed-size sign term based on current guidance to the noise-space result. The code comments admit it is an approximation.
entries.math:
e = c − u; f = u + s·e − k·sign(e)
smc_cfg_lambda and no_cfg_warmup_steps are accepted but unused.
Since c,u are x−x̂: x̂ = x̂_cfg + k·sign(x̂_u − x̂_c), i.e. a constant-size per-element nudge.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Lambda and warm-up widgets do nothing; correction is independent of s and of step history.

entries.name: AdaMaG (adaptive manifold guidance)
entries.plain: Projects guidance on the positive noise estimate, weights the parallel part down, and schedules cfg by a power of t.
entries.math:
n_c = x_t + (1−t)f_c; g=f_c−f_u; g∥ on n_c, g⊥ = g−g∥
ω = max(w_min, w·t^γ); f = f_u + ω(g⊥ + βg∥)

entries.name: Adaptive Guidance (cosine cut-off)
entries.plain: Stops CFG once positive and negative agree enough, so later steps save the negative pass. Decision is latched per sample.

entries.name: Adaptive Guidance guider with uncond-zero (asagi4 pack, patched here)
entries.plain: Measures cosine similarity of cond and uncond and turns CFG off for the rest of the run after it passes a threshold. In the CFG-off steps it can apply an uncond-zero style output. The patched copy on this box uses the least-converged image in a batch.

ts>start or past remembered timestep or cfg=1: x̂ = x̂_c, or with uz_scale>0: x̂ = x − (c/√std(c))·uz, c = x−x̂_c

entries.name: Adept combat CFG drift
entries.plain: Removes a share of the mean of the prediction, over all channels together, to counter colour drift. A one-line method inside the Adept sampler, called on denoised.
entries.math: x̂←x̂−mean_{C,H,W}(x̂)·k, or median by mode; the caller only uses mean, with k default .5.

entries.name: Adept spectral modulation in v space
entries.plain: Reworks the guidance difference in the frequency domain before applying the scale. It is converted to v-prediction first, using the same conversion as RescaleCFG. Amplitudes in the top and bottom percentile of log amplitude are adjusted. Docstring credits ComfyUI-Latent-Modifiers.
entries.math:
x=x_in/(σ²+1). v_c,v_u=((x−(x_in−c))√(σ²+1))/σ, likewise u. Δ=v_c−v_u.
F=FFT2(Δ), log|F| with quantiles at p and 1−p, percent p default 5.
v=v_u+s·iFFT(F·mult); return x_in−(x−vσ/√(σ²+1)).
Mult details beyond the quantiles (utils.py line 490 on) not read.

entries.name: Angle Domain Guidance (ADG)
entries.plain: Treats the whole latent as a vector and rotates the conditional by a capped angle, rather than extrapolating. The norm is bounded by construction.
entries.math:
θ = arccos(cos(x̂_u,x̂_c)); θ_w = min((w−1)θ, θ_max)
e = x̂_c − (⟨x̂_u,x̂_c⟩/‖x̂_u‖²)x̂_u
x̂ = cos θ_w·x̂_c + (sin θ_w/sin θ)·e; (w−1)e when sinθ≤1e-3

entries.name: Anima adaptive CFG by divergence
entries.plain: Sets the CFG scale each step from how far apart cond and uncond are: larger gap, lower scale, then clamps it. The gap is measured over the batch as a single number, so one scale applies to the whole batch.
entries.math:
d=mean over batch ‖c−u‖₂. s=base·(target/d)^a, clamped to [min,max]; if d<1e-8, s=base. x=u+s(c−u).
Advanced node: s=schedule(progress)·(target/d)^a, floored at 1.

entries.name: Anima post-CFG utilities
entries.plain: Three small post-CFG tools sharing one sigma-progress window. A frequency scale with a square low-pass box, a channel mean remover, and a noise add that rises and falls across the window. Names suggest model tuning; the code has no Anima-specific logic.
entries.math:
Freq: F(x̂)·mask, mask=low inside a box of half-size cutoff, high outside; scales ramp from 1 across the window.
Mean: x̂−=mean_channel(x̂)·k.
Sculpt: x̂+=n·k·sin(π t), t in the window. Note n is added to the denoised prediction, not to the latent.
Rescale: x̂=m·x̂·std(c)/std(x̂)+(1−m)x̂ on denoised, not v.

entries.name: APG Guider (rule-based, MD fork of blepping)
entries.plain: A guider with an ordered list of rules: for each sigma the first matching rule sets cfg, APG scale, momentum, blend. It can run APG as cfg function or pre-CFG per rule.
entries.math: Rule by σ ≤ start_sigma; matched rule with apg_blend≠0 and apg_scale≠0: disable cfg1, run rule.cfg_function (cfg=rule.cfg) or pre_cfg_function (cfg=apg_scale). Otherwise plain cfg=rule.cfg. Core update math is in apg_guider_core.py with momentum modes and lerp/slerp blends (partly read).

entries.name: APG_ImYourCFGNow (noise space, adaptive momentum)
entries.plain: APG implemented as a cfg function in noise space. Includes a built-in guidance limiter and an adaptive momentum that decays through the schedule. Projection is on the noise prediction, whereas core projects on x0.
entries.math:
c,u = x−x̂
β_t = β − β·a⁴·(1000−t) (floor 0; mirrored for β<0)
v ← β_t·v + (c−u); g=v
g ← g·min(1, T/‖g‖)
g' = g⊥ + η·g∥ relative to c
f = c + (s−1)·g'
Limiter on, outside window: f = c

entries.name: AutoGuidance + CFG guider (xmarre)
entries.plain: Runs CFG on a good model and a positive pass on a bad model, adding a capped push away from the bad one. Options choose the direction, a cap relative to the CFG update, a ramp over time, and how post-CFG hooks interact. Its paper mode mixes the weights instead of stacking them.
entries.math:
sequential_delta (default): w=max(w_ag−1,0)
d by mode: bad_conditional c_g−c_b; project_cfg: part of d along CFG update; reject_cfg: d minus that part; raw_delta: CFG_g−CFG_b
Δ=w·d; cap: Δ←Δ·min(ρ_t‖U‖/(‖Δ‖+1e-8),1); x̂=x̂_cfg+Δ
ρ_t=ρ(f+(1−f)ramp(progress)); default ρ=0.35

entries.name: Automatic CFG (per-channel range normalization)
entries.plain: Sets a separate cfg for each latent channel so the guided output reaches a target intensity based on top-k value range. Also has a large set of extras: skip or fake uncond, experimental functions, attention modifiers, latent centring. It also replaces core's sampling function.

R = (mean of top-k max + mean of top-k min-based)/2 per channel of a reference CFG (measure hard, soft, hard_squared, range)
d = reference_cfg·(reference last cfg/10)/R_c
f_c = u_c + d_c·(c_c−u_c)

entries.name: Bernini chained multi-condition guidance
entries.plain: A chain of guidance arms, each compared with the previous one, instead of all compared with one uncond. Each delta can be APG-projected. In the T8 port the rv2v branch uses plain deltas even though the upstream mode has APG in its name, per the comment there.

x̂=b+ω_i P(s−b, s)+ω_t P(t−s, t)+ω_g P(g−t, g).
P(d,r)=.2 d∥+1.0 d⊥ with respect to r over all dims of a batch item.

entries.name: CFG Megapack seven-stage plan
entries.plain: A framework that splits a guided step into stages: when to guide, a weak branch, how to combine, where to guide (bands or regions), magnitude correction, an angle governor, and measurement. Each stage has a node that writes to a plan stored in model options; paper nodes write the same plan. All guidance goes through one runtime.
entries.math:
Runtime guided_x0(x, x̂_c, x̂_u, σ, s):
1 when: w = schedule_value(shape, s, progress, t, ...), floor, inside-window test; outside: cond, plain, fixed scale, or rest of chain.
2 weak: x̂_w = perturbed_prediction (attention, skip, blur, shuffle), mode add or replace.
3 combine: registry function in its native space via to_space/from_space.
4 where: split_bands or region_map weights.

entries.name: CFG Three-Way Guider (separate null and negative)
entries.plain: A guider with positive, negative and a separate null prompt, running rules that core mixes up. negative_as_null reproduces plain CFG.

perp_neg: u + w((c−u) − s·P), P = (n−u) minus part along (c−u), per sample

entries.name: Channel incremental constrained guider
entries.plain: After CFG, decodes the prediction and takes the per-pixel change from the source image, keeping only its mean across RGB, so edits become grey-level and no hue changes. It is encoded again and pulled in with a strength that grows as timestep falls. Costs one VAE decode and encode per step.
entries.math: d=D(x̂)−I. I′=clamp(I+mean_rgb(d),0,1). x̂←x̂+k(1−t)²(E(I′)−x̂).

entries.name: Characteristic Guidance
entries.plain: Solves a fixed-point correction at each step that needs several extra model calls. Falls back to plain CFG if it does not converge.
entries.math:
Solve dx = P[(ε(x+w·dx;u) − ε(x+ω·dx;c))·σ], ω=w−1
ε = w·ε(x+ω·dx;c) − ω·ε(x+w·dx;u)

entries.name: ClampDenoised VAE round trip
entries.plain: Each step, decodes the denoised latent to pixels, clamps to 0-1, and encodes it again. It forces the prediction into the range of the VAE, and costs one VAE decode and encode per step. It does nothing on latents that are not 4D, so it skips video.
entries.math: x̂₀ ← E(clamp(D(x̂₀),0,1)), only when x̂₀.ndim=4.

entries.label: from code

entries.name: ClybGuidance (APG family with scale schedule and scalar projection)
entries.plain: A Chroma-oriented APG with many options: uncond scalar projection like CFG-Zero★, a sine-shaped guidance multiplier by time, an atan2-sin mixed uncond, EMA momentum, and a norm cap relative to cond.
entries.math:
Optional uncond ← lerp(uncond, sin(atan c)/cos(atan u), w_a)
Optional α = ⟨c,u⟩/‖u‖² (logsumexp variant); uncond ← α·uncond
GM = lerp(1, sin((1−t^shift)π), ratio); scalar = 1/s + GM·(s−1)/s; g = (c−u)·scalar
Momentum: v ← lerp(v, g, 1−β); g' = g + m·v, with renorm option
g⊥ + η·g∥ (projected on c)
Norm cap: ‖u+g·s‖ ≥ T‖c‖ → g ← g·T‖c‖/‖u+g·s‖
x̂_c' = u + g

entries.name: Dynamic Thresholding (mimic scale, cfg_function)
entries.plain: Runs CFG at a high scale but renormalizes values to the range of a lower 'mimic' scale, to get a strong guidance effect without color blow-out. Has schedules for both scales and several normalization choices.
entries.math:
M = u + Δ·s_m, C = u + Δ·s_c (x0 space, s_m,s_c from a schedule)
Flatten; center at per-channel means.
AD: R_m=max|M−μ_M|, R_c=quantile(|C−μ_C|,p); STD: std
ZERO: result = C·R_m/R_c
MEAN AD: Rmax = max(R_m,R_c); r = clamp(C−μ_C,±Rmax)/Rmax·R_m + μ_C
MEAN STD: r = (C−μ_C)/R_c·R_m + μ_C
phi≠1: r ← φ·r + (1−φ)·C
sep_feat_channels: per channel (first option on the full node); channels together on the Simple node.
s_c = s_m: plain CFG.

entries.plain: Splits positive and negative x0 predictions into a two-level Laplacian pyramid and applies a higher scale to fine detail and the normal cfg to coarse. Rebuilds the image afterward.

For each level: d = c_i − u_i; x_i = c_i + (w_i−1)·d

entries.name: Momentum Guidance (MG)
entries.plain: Pushes the guided output away from its moving average over the steps. No extra model pass, and it reads and stores state through the model options dictionary.

entries.name: NAG for Krea 2 (float32 norm, prescale)

z̃ = z₊ + φ(z₊−z₋); r = |z̃|₁/|z₊|₁ (clamp ≥ float32 eps)
ẑ = z̃·min(r,τ)/r; z = αẑ + (1−α)z₊. Evaluated in float32 and cast back.
z₊,z₋ share image Q/K/V and differ only in text.

g = z₊φ − z₋(φ−1); r=‖g‖₁/(‖z₊‖₁+1e-7); if r>τ: g←g·‖z₊‖₁τ/(‖g‖₁+1e-7); z=gα+z₊(1−α)

entries.name: NAG text energy compensation (Donut experiment)
