entries.name: Negative attention (Extraltodeus)
entries.plain: Adds to attention scores a term from the difference between positive and negative attention. It uses a linear layer created on each call, so the projection is random and untrained.
entries.math:
D = softmax(QKᵀ)V − softmax(QK_nᵀ)V
A = softmax(QKᵀ + Linear_new(D)·w); out = A·V
Linear_new is a new, randomly initialised nn.Linear each call.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The projection is a freshly random nn.Linear on every attention call, so the effect depends on torch RNG state.

audit.note: Second term uses the negative value tensor, not V: D = softmax(QKᵀ)V − softmax(QK_nᵀ)V_n, where K_n,V_n are the second half of k,v (Extraltodeus__Negative-attention-for-ComfyUI-/nodes.py:26, 49-53). entries.name: PAG Advanced with adaptive scale and rescale (sd-perturbed-attention)
entries.plain: A fuller PAG: choose blocks, sigma window, an adaptive decay of the scale, and optional rescale or saliency fusion with CFG.
entries.math:
w_t = w − w·a⁴·(1000−t), floor 0 (a=adaptive_scale)
x̂_p = M(x; c) with attn(q,k,v)→v on chosen blocks
G = (x̂_c − x̂_p)·w_t
rescale=ρ: f = ρ·std(x̂_c)/std(R) + (1−ρ), with R = x̂_cfg+G (full) or x̂_c+G (partial); G←G·f

entries.plain: A pack-invented variant: take the skip-pass prediction, remove its part parallel to the CFG output, and subtract the rest with a weight, then renormalize, with optional clamping.

proj = ⟨x̂_s,x̂_cfg⟩/(⟨x̂_cfg,x̂_cfg⟩+1e-6); O = x̂_s − proj·x̂_cfg

entries.name: PLADIS (sparse cross-attention extrapolation)
entries.plain: Replaces cross-attention's softmax with a mix extrapolating away from soft attention toward a sparse map. No extra model pass, no extra sampler hook, and it can be combined with others.
entries.math:
S = q·kᵀ·d^(−1/2)
A = λ·sparse(S) + (1−λ)·softmax(S), sparse = entmax1.5 or sparsemax
out = A·v
Default applies to all input/output cross-attention blocks; middle only with a list.

entries.name: PMC-CFG (posterior-mean cap)
entries.plain: Caps the extrapolation so the result norm cannot exceed G times the positive norm, using a closed form for the largest allowed step.
entries.math:
D=x̂_c−x̂_u; a=‖D‖²; b=⟨x̂_c,D⟩; q=‖x̂_c‖²
βcap = (−b+√(b²+(G²−1)aq))/a; β=min(w−1,βcap)
x̂ = x̂_c + βD

entries.name: Sigma-shift self guidance

entries.name: Skimmed CFG (sign-masked fallback, megapack reimplementation)
entries.plain: Pulls back only the elements where guidance would overshoot in the same direction as the value, using a lower scale there. The original Skimmed_CFG pack source is not on this box, so this entry is the megapack reimplementation.
entries.math:
skim(A,B,k,s): D = B + k(A−B)
M = [sign(A−B)=sign A]∧[sign D=sign A]∧[sign D=sign(D−x_t)]
on M: A ← A − (k−s)(A−B)/k
u′ = skim(x̂_u, x̂_c, w, s_neg); c′ = skim(x̂_c, u′, w−1, s)
x̂ = u′ + w(c′−u′)

entries.name: Skip CFG on first step
entries.plain: Drops the negative while sigma is above a percent threshold, saving a call in the first steps. Core fills the missing negative with zeros and still applies CFG, so those steps return the positive multiplied by the CFG scale unless CFG is 1.
entries.math: σ > percent_to_sigma(p): conds[1] = None, so x̂_u = 0 and x̂ = w·x̂_c (single pass; equals x̂_c only at w=1). Chains an existing calc_cond_batch function.

entries.name: SkipCFG Sigmas (aria1th)
entries.plain: Keeps CFG only inside a sigma mask and uses the positive prediction, or a blend toward CFG, outside it. The negative is still calculated.
entries.math:
m = σ_min ≤ σ ≤ σ_max
x̂[m] = x̂_cfg[m]
x̂[¬m] = x̂_c + ρ(x̂_cfg − x̂_c) if ρ>0, else x̂_c

entries.name: Sliding Window Guidance (SWG)
entries.plain: An extra positive pass is run on overlapping tiles, not the whole latent, so the model sees less context. The difference from the whole-image prediction becomes guidance. Tile sizes are in pixels divided by 8. The cost is one model call per tile.
entries.math:
For each tile T: x̂_T = M(x|T; c), accumulated and divided by overlap count = x̂_w
x̂ = x̂_cfg + w·(x̂_c − x̂_w)

props.params: scale=5.0, tile_width=768, tile_height=768, tile_overlap=256, sigma_start=-1, sigma_end=5.42

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The window step uses tile_width·i..tile_width·(i+1)+overlap, while tile count uses width−overlap, so the extra tiles past the edge are empty and skipped; overlap is less than the count suggests.

entries.name: SMC-CFG (adaptive gain, velocity space)
entries.plain: Keeps true sign switching but makes the gain follow the size of the guidance, to fight the texture chatter that a fixed gain gave. Built for Anima velocity prediction.
entries.math:
v = (x−x̂)/σ; e = v_c − v_u
S = (e−ẽ)+λẽ; k = a·mean|e| (≥1e-12)
Δ = −k·sign(S); store raw e; drop history if shape changes
v̂ = v_u + s(e+Δ); return σ·v̂

entries.name: SMC-CFG (tanh, blurred, noise space)
entries.plain: A smoothed version aimed at avoiding speckle: tanh in place of sign, a 5×5 box blur on the correction, and a K scaled down by √cfg. Works on x−x̂ divided by sigma, with a warm-up that returns cond alone.
entries.math:
e = (c−u)/σ
S = (e−ẽ) + λ·ẽ; K' = K/√max(s,1)
u_sw = −K'·tanh(S/max(std(S),1e-6)); u_sw ← avg_pool5×5(u_sw)
f = u + s·(e + u_sw)·σ
Stores raw e. Warm-up steps: f = c. Resets if sigma rises >10%.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: SMC-CFG (unit-norm, x0 space)
entries.plain: Treats guidance as a control problem: a sliding surface built from current and previous guidance error adds a correction before CFG. This version replaces sign with a unit-norm vector because the author says sign did not work.
entries.math:
e = x̂_c − x̂_u; ẽ = stored (first: e)
S = (e − ẽ) + λ·ẽ
Δ = −k·S/‖S‖₂
e' = e + Δ; store e' (the corrected value)
x̂ = x̂_u + s·e'
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Stores corrected error, while ethanfel explicitly stores raw error to avoid accumulation.

entries.name: Smoothed Energy Guidance (SEG)
entries.plain: Instead of removing self-attention, it blurs its queries. Blurring Q smooths the attention energy, and the difference from the normal pass is added as guidance. Blur sigma below 0 means flatten Q completely to its mean.
entries.math:
σ_b≥0: Q' = gaussian_blur(reshape(Q), size⌈6σ_b⌉ odd, σ_b)
σ_b<0: Q' = mean of Q over space
x̂_s = M(x; c) with attn(Q',K,V)
G = w(x̂_c − x̂_s); x̂ = x̂_cfg + (rescaled G) (or SNF mode).

props.params: scale=3.0, blur_sigma=-1, unet_block=middle, unet_block_id=0, sigma_start, sigma_end, rescale, rescale_mode

entries.name: Sonar reference latent guidance
entries.plain: Nudges the latent toward a reference latent during sampling, after shifting the reference to the current mean and std. Either a plain blend, or an Euler step aimed at the reference.
entries.math:
r_s=r·std(t)+mean(t), t=x (linear) or x̂ (euler).
Linear: x←lerp(x,r_s,f). Euler: x←x+(x−r_s)/σ·(σ_n−σ)f. f default .2; only inside start and end steps.

entries.name: Sonar wavelet CFG
entries.plain: Performs CFG in the wavelet domain, so low and high bands get their own scales through a rule list. The low band and detail bands can use different blend modes.
entries.math:
C,U=DWT(c),DWT(u), each optionally scaled by rule. D=C−U band by band, then scaled.
R=blend(U,D,yl_factor=difference_blend_strength(pcts)), then final scale. x̂=iDWT(R).

entries.name: STG guider (Lightricks, pos-based with std rescale)

entries.math:
n = c + (s−1)(c−u) + w(c−p)
ρ≠0: f=ρ·std(c)/std(n)+(1−ρ); n←n·f

entries.name: AddNoise node (sigma span renoise)
entries.plain: Takes a NOISE source and adds it to a latent at a chosen sigma, outside the sampler. Lets you renoise a finished latent to re-enter sampling midway. Uses the span of the given sigmas as the amount, not the first sigma.
entries.math:
scale = |σ_0 − σ_last| if len(sigmas)>1 else σ_0.
z' = process_latent_in(z) unless z is all zeros.
noisy = noise_scaling(scale, ε, z'), then process_latent_out, then NaN and inf replaced by 0.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Scale is the difference between first and last sigma: passing a sigma list ending at 0 gives σ_0, ending at 5 gives σ_0−5, not σ_0.

entries.name: BrownianTreeNoiseSampler / BatchedBrownianTree
entries.plain: The per-step noise used by DPM++ SDE family. A Brownian tree gives noise consistent across different step counts because each interval's noise depends on the interval, not the call count. Makes SDE results converge as steps rise.
entries.math:
W(t) via torchsde.BrownianTree(t0, w0=0, t1, entropy=seed), with one tree per seed if a seed list is given.
noise(σ,σ_next) = sign · (W(t1) − W(t0)) / √|t1−t0|, where t = transform(σ) (identity by default).
Division by √|Δt| makes each sample unit variance.

props.distribution: standard normal, correlated across overlapping sigma intervals
props.spectrum: white in space; Brownian in sigma

providers.note: normalized=False; just calls core tree

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The tree is on CPU for plain dpmpp_sde and 2m/3m SDE (cpu=True) and on the device for the _gpu variants (cpu=False), so the two give different noise for one seed.

entries.name: default_noise_sampler (per-step white noise)
entries.plain: The per-step noise used by ancestral samplers. Independent Gaussian per call with a generator seeded once. Draws on the latent's own device, so results can vary between GPU and CPU; it also shifts the seed by one on CPU.
entries.math:
gen.manual_seed(seed + 1 if device is cpu else seed).
noise_sampler(σ,σ_next) = randn(x.shape, device=x.device, generator=gen). Arguments are ignored.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Seed gets +1 only when x is on cpu (sampling.py:81), so CPU and CUDA ancestral streams differ by design even with the same generator type.

entries.name: DPM++ SDE noise term
entries.plain: The 2M and 3M SDE samplers compute the noise term from the half-logSNR step, not from an ancestral split, and it scales with eta. The plain dpmpp_sde sampler is different: it uses an ancestral split in lambda space.
entries.math:
With h=λ(σ_next)−λ(σ), λ=half-logSNR (non-flow: h=log(σ/σ_next); flow: λ=−logit σ), x ← … + ε·σ_next·√(1−exp(−2hη))·s_noise·noise_scale, if η>0 and s_noise>0.
ε = BrownianTree by default.
entries.label: from code

audit.note: sampling.py:921-922,937: h is the half-logSNR step λ_next−λ, which equals log(σ/σ_next) only for non-flow models; CONST uses −logit(σ) (sampling.py:154-157). sampling.py:844-849: sample_dpmpp_sde does use get_ancestral_step (in λ space), so the plain claim does not hold for the whole sde family.

entries.name: ER-SDE noise scaler
entries.plain: ER-SDE uses a nonlinear noise scaler function of the noise-to-signal lambda (σ/α) as a custom noise schedule. The noise amount is set by a chosen function rather than by eta.
entries.math: default scaler f(x) = x·(exp(x^0.3) + 10). λ=σ/α, r=f(λ_t)/f(λ_s). Noise term: x ← x + α_t·ε·s_noise·√(λ_t²−λ_s²·r²) per sampling.py:1654.
entries.label: from code

audit.note: sampling.py:1613: er_lambda is σ/α = exp(−half_log_snr), a noise-to-signal ratio, not a log quantity, so 'logSNR-style' misdescribes it. Formula and sampling.py:1654 are right.

entries.name: get_ancestral_step (VE ancestral noise split)
entries.plain: Splits one step into a deterministic move down to sigma_down and a fresh noise addition sigma_up, so the combined variance lands exactly on the target sigma. eta scales how much of the step is stochastic.
entries.math:
σ_up = min(σ_to, η·√(σ_to²·(σ_from²−σ_to²)/σ_from²)).
σ_down = √(σ_to²−σ_up²). If η=0: (σ_to,0).
Then x ← x + d·(σ_down−σ) + ε·s_noise·σ_up.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: LCM renoise with s_noise ramp and noise clip
entries.plain: LCM replaces x by the prediction each step, then fully re-noises it to the next sigma using the model's noise_scaling. This core version adds a linear ramp on the noise multiplier and an optional clamp of injected noise.
entries.math: x ← x0. If σ_next>0: ε = sampler(σ,σ_next); if noise_clip_std>0: ε clamped to ±noise_clip_std·std(ε). s_i = s_noise + (s_noise_end−s_noise)·i/(N−1); ε←ε·s_i; x ← noise_scaling(σ_next, ε, x).

props.normalizes_variance: no: clipping reduces variance and nothing restores it

entries.math: ε = 0 (zeros_like latent, on cpu). With CONST flow scaling the latent is still multiplied by (1−σ) at start: x = (1−σ)·z.

entries.name: noise_mask / KSamplerX0Inpaint (masked denoising)
entries.plain: How masked sampling works in core: at each step the region outside the mask is replaced by the original latent noised to the current sigma with the same noise tensor, and the output is composited with the original at the end of each call. So noise is confined in effect rather than masked at the start.
entries.math:
mask m (1=denoise). x ← x·m + noise_scaling(σ, ε, z)·(1−m); out ← model(x,σ)·m + z·(1−m).
ε is the initial noise tensor kept for the whole run.

entries.name: noise_scaling (how noise meets the latent)
entries.plain: Each model's sampling class decides how the noise tensor is mixed with the latent at sigma. This is where any custom noise amplitude actually lands. Variance-exploding models add σ·ε; flow models interpolate; some image-to-image model types ignore noise completely.
entries.math:
EPS, V_PREDICTION, X0, V_PREDICTION_DDPM: x = z + σ·ε; if max_denoise: x = z + √(1+σ²)·ε.
CONST (flow): x = σ·(s·ε) + (1−σ)·z, where s = model_sampling.noise_scale (default 1).
COSMOS_RFLOW: x = z + σ·ε (max_denoise ignored).
IMG_TO_IMG_FLOW, IMG_TO_IMG_VELOCITY: x = z, noise discarded.
Inverse scaling: CONST divides final latent by (1−σ); EPS returns as is.

props.normalizes_variance: no: a non-unit-variance custom noise scales the effective start level directly

entries.name: prepare_noise (default initial noise)
entries.plain: The default starting noise in ComfyUI: plain standard Gaussian made on the CPU from one seed, so a seed gives the same starting noise regardless of GPU. With batch_index it draws and discards earlier batch items so item N can be reproduced alone.
entries.math:
ε ~ N(0,I), shape = latent shape, generator = torch.manual_seed(seed), device = cpu.
With noise_inds: for i in 0..max(inds): draw one item ε_i of shape [1,...]; keep if i in inds; output reordered by inds.
Nested latents: one shared generator advances through each sub-tensor in order.

props.normalizes_variance: no; sample statistics left as drawn

entries.surprise: Noise tensor is always CPU-generated by default, while per-step ancestral noise is drawn on the latent's device, so they use different RNG streams.

entries.name: Rectified-flow ancestral renoise (RF variants)
entries.plain: Flow models cannot use the VE split, so core has a separate rule. It shrinks x toward the prediction, rescales up by alpha ratio and adds noise so the marginal is right at next sigma. Note the eta semantics differ from the VE version.
entries.math:
ratio = 1 + (σ_next/σ − 1)·η; σ_down = σ_next·ratio. α_next=1−σ_next; α_down=1−σ_down.
c = √(σ_next² − σ_down²·α_next²/α_down²).
x ← (σ_down/σ)·x + (1−σ_down/σ)·x0; if η>0: x ← (α_next/α_down)·x + ε·s_noise·noise_scale·c. Last step returns x0.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: s_churn (Karras churn)
entries.plain: Before evaluating the model, raises the noise level a bit by adding fresh noise, then integrates from the raised level. A simple form of noise injection on non-ancestral solvers. In ComfyUI it is 0 by default on KSampler.
entries.math:
γ = min(s_churn/(N), √2−1) if s_tmin ≤ σ_i ≤ s_tmax else 0, N = len(sigmas)−1.
σ̂ = σ_i(1+γ). x ← x + ε·s_noise·√(σ̂²−σ_i²).
Then x ← x + d(x,σ̂)·(σ_{i+1}−σ̂).
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Churn draws torch.randn_like and ignores the sampler's noise_sampler, so sonar or PNS noise never reaches it and the global RNG sets it.

entries.name: VOID optical-flow warped noise (core)
entries.plain: Moves Gaussian noise along RAFT optical flow so noise sticks to moving content across video frames, for temporally consistent refinement. Keeps Gaussian statistics when pixels merge or split using regaussianize. Ported in core from R. Burgert's code for the VOID pipeline.
entries.math:
State per pixel: [dx,dy,ω,noise]. For each flow:
Expansion: nearest-neighbour remap by −flow. Shrink: scatter-add to new positions.
Regaussianize groups of duplicated pixels: n' = n/√count + (f − mean_group(f)), f ~ N(0,I).
Shrink channels: scat(n·ω)/√scat(ω²). ω renormalised to mean 1, ω=(ω+1e-5)^0.9999.
Frame done at internal size (resize_flow·resize_frames·H), output = area_pool(n, 1/D)·D with D=downscale_factor (default 32).

props.spectrum: white in space; correlated along flow in time
props.normalizes_variance: yes, statistically: regaussianize and ×D after area pool

entries.name: 1/f noise with alpha, sonar (onef)
entries.plain: FFT filter over height and width with the exponent as a parameter. Pinkish and greenish names exist as preset alphas, mix variants subtract two draws.

P=(fx²+fy²)^(−α/2); if k≠0: P=k/P; P(0,0)=base_power. F=fftn(ε); F←F/√P (or /P); out=Re ifftn(F).
Amplitude ∝ |f|^(−α/2)/√k for k≠0.
ONEF_PINKISH α=−.5; ONEF_GREENISH α=.5. Mix: ½(−n₁+n₂) of same alpha.
Then normalized.

entries.name: Affine pattern noise (bias added to Gaussian)
entries.plain: Takes standard noise and adds a procedural pattern as an offset, then clamps to ±3. Pattern can be normalized first. Variance rises by the pattern's contribution, less what the clamp cuts.
entries.math: base=prepare_noise. m=pattern; if normalize: m=(m−μ)/std. result = clamp(base + m·affine_scale·affine_bias, −3, 3).

entries.name: BFS shot-coherent noise
entries.plain: Video start noise with several shaping options: replace coarse-block averages from a shot seed so shots match in composition, tilt the spectrum over space and time, and add pyramid. Uses careful unit-variance formulas throughout.
entries.math:
replace_coarse: each (time block, y, x) cell mean is replaced by a shot-seed draw, then rescaled to unit noise.
tilt_spectrum: power ×|f|^(−α) over T,h,w; then zero mean, unit std.
mix: √(1−w²)·x + w·signal.

entries.name: Block-correlated noise for latent upsample (RALU, Pyramid-Flow)
entries.plain: When a latent is upsampled during sampling, new pixel groups need noise whose average matches an existing value. Draws noise in small blocks with a weak negative correlation so that block means have reduced variance.
entries.math:
Σ_block = I + γ·11ᵀ. RALU: γ = −1/z² + 1e−6, block=2×2; n = ε·chol(Σ)ᵀ.
Pyramid-Flow: MultivariateNormal(0, I·(1+γ) − γ·11ᵀ) per 2×2 block.

entries.name: CADS (noise on the condition, not latent)
entries.plain: Adds noise to the prompt embedding rather than the latent during the early steps, then rescales to original mean and std. Used for diversity. Stronger early and fading as sampling proceeds.
entries.math:
γ = clamp((σ_s−σ)/(σ_s−σ_e),0,1), active when σ ≤ σ_s.
y_n = √γ·y + scale·√(1−γ)·N(0,I).
y' = ((y_n − mean(y_n))/std(y_n))·std(y) + mean(y). Applies to c_crossattn and c_concat, on every model call.

props.normalizes_variance: yes: per-sample, mean and std of the embedding restored

entries.name: Clip-wide noise sliced per chunk
entries.plain: Chunked video rendering usually reseeds per chunk, so the overlap holds two unrelated noises for the same moment. This asks the NOISE object for one tensor for the whole clip's length, then gives each chunk its slice, so neighbours start with identical noise in their overlap. The docstring says this is what stops double exposure in the cross-fade.

chunk noise = ε_clip[overlap-consistent slice] for each stream.

entries.name: CNS wavelet-band colored per-step noise
entries.plain: Per-step noise whose subband energy is decided by what the latent has already built. Haar-transforms x, measures energy per band, and gives more noise to bands that are unresolved. Total energy kept by RMS normalization.
entries.math:
E_b = energy of band b of x_t; γ_b=clamp(E_b/ΣE/γ_scale,0,1); β_b=(1−γ_b)^power; β_b←β_b/√(mean β²).

entries.name: Coupled Initialization (batch repulsion)
entries.plain: Makes the noises of a batch negatively correlated so a batch of images spreads out more. First item is unchanged. Each marginal stays standard Gaussian.

result_i = ρ·ε_0 + √(1−ρ)·(ε_i − ē) + √((1−ρ)(1−s))·ē, ē = mean of ε_1..K−1 (second term only for s<1).

entries.name: Cross-hatch power fractal (PowerNoiseSuite)
entries.plain: Sums axis-aligned sinusoidal hatch patterns over octaves. The base class then applies color mapping and blur. The angle input is stored but never used. A structured, line-like initial noise rather than a random field.
entries.math: Octave sum of sin(x·f·π) and sin(y·f·π) grids, each min-max scaled and weighted persistence^k; angle unused. Linear variant: f·gain, plus noise·tolerance (latent_noise.py:290,440), then stepped mapping. Normalized to [0,1].

entries.name: FFT colored noise, PowerNoiseSuite (blue/green/pink share one filter)

P(f) = (fx²+fy²)^(α/2); P(0,0)=1. F=fftn(ε).
out = Re ifftn(F/√P). Amplitude ∝ |f|^(−α/2), power ∝ |f|^(−α).

entries.name: Golden Noise (NPNet)
entries.plain: Passes the Gaussian start noise and the prompt embedding through a small trained network that outputs a better starting noise. Pre-model, one forward pass and no sampler changes. entries.name: H3 drift control: schedule-matched prefix noise
entries.plain: A chained H3 segment normally keeps its carried video prefix fully clean, which the author measured as building up contrast and texture error along a chain. Inject: n=(z+ε)/2 if average else z+ε·s; optional n/std(n); mask lerp; mix_randn_amount adds fresh randn.

entries.surprise: normalize divides the noised latent, not the noise, by its std: this rescales the image signal too, not just noise.

entries.name: KoO pink, blue, high and low frequency noise
entries.plain: Simple spectrum filter. Pink is one over root radius, blue is root radius, with a clamped floor for DC. Also blur-based high and low frequency variants. Values rescaled by filter mean, not variance.
entries.math:
r=max(√(fx²+fy²),1/max(h,w)). pink s=1/√r, blue s=√r; s←s/mean(s). out=irfftn(rfftn(ε)·s).
high_frequency: ε−blur(ε,1.5). low_frequency: blur(ε,4).

props.normalizes_variance: no: filter mean only, so std ≠ 1, and low_frequency has much lower variance

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Laplacian, Student-t, distro zoo (sonar)
entries.plain: Heavy-tailed alternatives to Gaussian. The Laplacian adds a quarter of Gaussian so it is a mixture. The Student-t is scaled, clipped by quantile and compressed by a square-root. A distro node exposes 26 torch distributions.
entries.math:
Laplacian: n = ε/4 + Laplace(0,1). normalized.
Student-t: t~T(df=1,scale=.2); q=quantile(|t|,.75)·nq; t←clamp(t,−q,q); out=sign(t)·|t|^.5. normalized=False.
Distro: exponential, cauchy, geometric, log_normal, normal, beta, continuous_bernoulli, dirichlet, fisher_snedecor, gamma, gumbel, inverse_gamma, kumaraswamy, laplacian, lkjcholesky, lrmvariate_normal, mvariate_normal, pareto, poisson, relaxed_bernoulli, relaxed_onehotcategorical, studentt, uniform, vonmises, weibull, wishart; optional quantile normalize.

props.distribution: Laplace + Gaussian mix; Student-t clipped; any torch distribution
props.normalizes_variance: Laplacian yes, Student-t no in sonar; BFS analytically

providers.author: ClownsharkBatwing
providers.note: Separate Laplacian and StudentT at beta/noise_classes.py:397,421; see RES4LYF tribute page

providers.author: MDMAchine
providers.note: generate_laplacian_noise, generate_student_t_noise (df=3) in core

providers.author: alisson-anjos
providers.note: Exact unit variance formulae: Laplace inverse-CDF ÷√2; t(5) via n/√(χ²₅/5)·√(3/5); uniform·√12

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The Student-t default df=1 is Cauchy, tamed by clipping at the 75th percentile: most mass of the tail is removed.

entries.name: LatentForwardDiffusion (additive regardless of model)
entries.plain: Adds Gaussian to a latent scaled by the sigma from a chosen step. Convenient for renoising before partial sampling.
entries.math: z' = z + ε·σ_start. If no sampler sigmas: σ from linspace(1,0,steps).
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Additive z+σε for every model, including flow models where core uses (1−σ)z+σε, and it does not call noise_scaling.

entries.name: LatentWalk norm-restored noise blending
entries.plain: Blends two NOISE objects by addition and then rescales the result to the norm a single noise would have. This avoids the shrinking that plain weighted addition gives, which the code comment says breaks sampling. A separate random walk adds norm-fixed steps with momentum.
entries.math:
blend = a·f_a + b·f_b; out = blend·‖ε_ref‖/‖blend‖.
Random walk: step = n·‖start‖·dist/‖n‖; curr = (1−m)·curr + m·(prev+step); renormalised to ‖start‖.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Mix and spatially shaped noise (cg-noisetools)
entries.plain: Chain-style NOISE wrappers. Mix blends two noise sources linearly with a very small default weight, for near-seed variation. Shape multiplies amplitude across the image by a sine or triangle profile, so noise can be stronger at the center. Optional renormalise.
entries.math:
Mix: m = ε1·(1−w)+ε2·w; with mask: m·mask + ε1·(1−mask).
Shape: profile(x)=2sin(πx/L)−1 or 1−|4x/L−2|; A(y,x)=(1+w·p(y))(1+w·p(x)); out=ε·A.

props.spectrum: as supplied, amplitude varies in space

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Mix noise with renormalize to base std (allans)
entries.plain: Adds a weighted second noise to a base and matches result's mean and std to the base, within a mask if given. A safe way to do small variations.
entries.math:
mixed = base·mask + mix·w (mask area).
normalized=(mixed−m')/s'; out=normalized·s_base+m_base.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Noise rotate in the model noise coordinate (GTE)
entries.plain: Branches a partly sampled latent by rotating its implied noise by an angle, then rebuilding the state via the model's own scaling. Valid for flow and additive model types alike, since it recovers eps through a probe of noise_scaling.
entries.math:
S,G = probe(noise_scaling) gives x=S+G·ε.
ε = (process_in(x) − S)/G; ε' = rotate(ε, θ, spread, count, seed).
x' = process_out(noise_scaling(σ, ε', x0)).

claims.text: Docstring reports a measured x0 component of 1.00 vs 0.125 valid at θ=90 under additive rotation of a flow model
claims.label: from pack README claim

entries.label: from code

entries.name: North Noise (reverse sigmas with injected noise)
entries.plain: An unsampler that walks flipped sigmas from low to high, but begins by passing strong Gaussian as the noise argument. It mixes model-driven inversion with an initial noise bump, optionally masked.
entries.math: ε ~ N(0,I)·strength (default 3), mask multiplies ε if given. σ' = reverse(σ[start..end+1]) + [1e-4]. Runs KSampler.sample(noise=ε, sigmas=σ').
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Default strength is 3.0×, and the sigma list ends with 1e-4 appended even though flipped sigmas ascend.

entries.name: Nukun recipe-weighted composite noise
entries.plain: Named recipes mix Gaussian, blue, violet, pink, brown and pyramid with weights that shift by a detail bias. The recipes have family names, such as Illustrious and Pony V7. Result is renormalized. Spectral part kills DC.
entries.math:
Colored: scale=|f|^(−α/2), scale(0,0)=0; out=Re ifftn(F·scale).
Recipe e.g. Illustrious texture: gaussian .42, blue .22+.34·h, violet .10+.25·h, pyramid .28+.22·l; l=1−h; h=detail_bias. Components weighted and summed, then (x−mean)/std; then strength.

claims.text: Recipes named for Illustrious and Pony V7, no evidence for fit in code
claims.label: from code

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Octave-sum pink noise (MD_Nodes)
entries.plain: A 'pink' noise that uses no FFT: sums bilinearly upsampled lower resolution Gaussians with 1/(octave+1) weights. Closer to a pyramid than true 1/f.
entries.math: num_oct=min(8,⌊log₂min(h,w)⌋). r=Σ_{k} (1/(k+1))·up(N(0,I)@h/2^k). r←r/Σw; r←r/std(r).

props.normalizes_variance: yes for pink; Auto-Norm is optional for blends

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Offset noise (per-channel DC term)
entries.plain: Adds a single random value per channel across the whole latent. Allows much darker or brighter outcomes because plain Gaussian has almost no DC component.
entries.math: ε = ε_w + offset·o, o ~ N(0,I) of shape [B,C,1,1].
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Orthogonal noise on rank-k conditioning
entries.plain: Decomposes a conditioning matrix by truncated SVD, keeps the top components, and replaces the residual with fresh noise that is projected out of those components and matched to the residual's std.
entries.math: M ≈ M_k (rank k SVD). R=M−M_k. n=randn·scale·std(R), with the top-k subspace removed. M' = M_k + n.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Perlin mapped to Gaussian by erfinv
entries.plain: Makes one octave of Perlin noise per channel, then multiplies its absolute value by a million and takes it modulo 11, scaled to [0,1). That scrambles the field to roughly uniform values, which go through the inverse normal CDF. The result is roughly Gaussian in value and has little Perlin structure left. A min-max helper exists but is not called.
entries.math: P=rand_perlin_2d(res=(1,1)); u=remainder(|P|·10⁶,11)/11; n=(1+detail/10)·√2·erfinv(2u−1); clamp ±5.

props.normalizes_variance: approximate; not exact because Perlin values are not uniform in [0,1]

providers.author: NeuralSamurAI
providers.note: Source header cites Extraltodeus noise_latent_perlinpinpin; that repo is not in the library

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Min-max gives exactly 0 and 1 at extremes, erfinv gives ±inf there, and the clamp hides it at ±5.

audit.note: No min-max scaling happens: scale_tensor (dimensional_latent_perlin.py:66) is never called. Line 63 does remainder(|P|·10⁶,11)/11, which scrambles the field into near-uniform values, so little Perlin structure should survive. Line 87 calls one octave at res (1,1), persistence 1. Structure claim is by reading, not run.

entries.name: Perlin power fractal (PowerNoiseSuite)
entries.plain: Classic 3D Perlin summed over octaves with an extra exponent on amplitude, then remapped into [0,1]. Used as initial latent noise or blended into a per-step noise.
entries.math:
n(p) = gradient noise, fade t ↦ 6t⁵−15t⁴+10t³.
M = Σ_k n(X·lac^k/scale,…)·(pers^k)^exp·pers^k. defaults octaves=4, persist=.5, lac=2, exp=4, scale=100.
M ← minmax(M,min,max); L ← (M+brightness)(1+contrast); L ← minmax(L). Z advances by evolution·frame or batch.

props.normalizes_variance: no: [0,1] output; PPFN latent adjust is a separate node

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Permutation table has size max(w,h)² rather than the standard 256, so memory and table differ with resolution.

entries.name: Pirog spectral and hierarchical noise
entries.plain: Pink, blue and hybrid filtering, plus a multi-scale hierarchy that bails out to plain Gaussian unless the latent has 4 or 16 channels. The hierarchical path has a final std normalize.
entries.math: pink: F·1/√|f| (DC=1); blue: F·√(|f|+.1). Hybrid and hierarchical: scales 1, .5, .25 mix per channel statistics.

props.normalizes_variance: hierarchical /std; spectral unknown past first lines

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Pointwise power-law remap (white, grey, velvet, violet, PowerNoiseSuite)
entries.plain: Despite the color names, these transform each sample's value and leave the spectrum flat. They change the histogram of the noise: with alpha near 0 values go toward ±1, with larger alpha the tails get heavier.
entries.math:
white: sign(n)·|n|^α·scale (default α=0, so ±scale).
grey: n·|n|^(α−1)·scale (default α=1, so Gaussian).
velvet: sign(n)·|n|^(1/α)/max|·|.
violet: sign(n)·|n|^(α/2)/max|·|.

props.normalizes_variance: no in PowerNoiseSuite; yes in sonar

providers.author: blepping
providers.note: sign(n) or n times |n|^α, optional divide by max, normalized by scale_noise. Named variants: white α=0 sign (so ±1), grey α=0 no sign (Gaussian), velvet α=1 sign (Gaussian÷max then renormalized, effectively Gaussian), violet α=.5 sign. See noise.py:2286.

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Sonar's 'white' is ±1 only (sign(n)·|n|⁰), and sonar's 'velvet' reduces to Gaussian since sign(n)·|n| = n.

entries.name: PPFN Advanced KSampler (BrownianTree hijack blend)
entries.plain: Replaces the core Brownian tree sampler class during sampling with one that nudges the Brownian tree result toward a blend with power-law, Perlin, or cross-hatch noise. A way of getting any of those noises into SDE samplers. The nudge is small, 3% of the blend difference, and sigma tolerance scales the blend factor; 0 turns it off.
entries.math:
Patch class comfy.k_diffusion.sampling.BrownianTreeNoiseSampler with PNSNoiseSampler.
sample_noise: tree = W(Δ)/√|Δt|. If sigma_tol=0, returns tree.
s=((σ−σmin)/(σmax/2−σmin))·tol/2; boost_leading_sigma: s×1.25, capped at 1, while noise_idx<steps//4.
No guide: out = tree ± 0.03·(blend(tree, sharpen(noise,.5), s) − tree), + when additive.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Hijacks the sampler class in module scope, not a noise_sampler argument, so it affects any SDE sampler during that run. Blend weight is a fixed 0.03 in the additive and subtractive branches.

audit.note: nodes.py:733-736 and the blend after it: the result is tree ± 0.03·(blend(tree, sharpen(noise,0.5), s) − tree), so only 3% of the blend difference is added, with a sign set by noise_mode. sigma_tol scales the blend factor; it does not control where the blend applies. The tonal-guide branch was not read past its first lines.

entries.name: Prepared noise tensor as NOISE (replay)
entries.plain: Wraps one already-made noise tensor as a NOISE object, so a sampler can be fed that exact tensor. The packs use this to guarantee that two passes share identical noise. These nodes only store and hand back a tensor; the distribution is whatever made it.
entries.math: generate_noise(latent) returns stored ε; raises on shape mismatch.

providers.author: xmarre
providers.note: Keeps a CPU copy, returns a clone. Planner use in nodes.py not read.

providers.author: teenu
providers.note: Generates on the torch device and reports a SHA-256 of the tensor in its output

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Pyramid noise (multi-resolution, sonar)
entries.plain: Adds lower-resolution Gaussian noise layers on top of white noise with decaying weights, to give more low-frequency energy. Random downscale factor at each iteration. The most common approach to multi-res noise.
entries.math:
n = ε. For i in 0..iterations(10): r~U(2,4); w←max(1,int(w/r^i)), h likewise (note the divisor compounds); n ← n + up(N(0,I)@h×w)·discount^i (discount=.7); break at 1.
Then normalized to unit std by scale_noise.
Highres: same with upscaling grids up to 15×, base uniform-based, then downsampled. r^i and U(2,4).
Mix variants: pyramid_mix: 0.2·P₁ − 0.8·P₂ (discount .6). pyramid_discount5: discount=.5.

props.normalizes_variance: yes in sonar and ULS and BFS; varies elsewhere

providers.author: ClownsharkBatwing
providers.note: See RES4LYF tribute page; adds cascade_B, interpolated, nearest, bicubic variants at beta/noise_classes.py:258-353

providers.author: PolyhedronAI
providers.note: discount .7 with _normalize

providers.author: alisson-anjos
providers.note: add_pyramid: levels halve; weight amount^i; bilinear; zero mean unit std per channel, 3D aware

providers.author: MDMAchine
providers.note: Pyramid and HiRes pyramid in core (see custom_noise_core.py); inspired by sonar per header

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Sonar's added layers call torch.randn without the seeded generator (noise_generation.py:632), so they follow the global RNG.

audit.note: "Highres: same" hides different defaults: iterations 4 (not 10), a uniform base, and grids growing up to 15×, compounding h,w (blepping__ComfyUI-sonar/py/noise_generation.py:527-561). Layers after the base draw randn without the seeded generator (lines 630-640), so they are not governed by the generator. "Most common approach" is opinion, not checkable from code.

entries.name: RES4LYF noise classes (short)
entries.plain: RES4LYF ships its own noise generator set for its samplers: colored fractal, pyramid families, Perlin, wavelet and more. Short entry only; see the RES4LYF tribute page.
entries.math: Facts: fractal density = k/f^(α·scale) in cycle-count frequency, default scale .1, k=1; names map brown α=2, pink 1, white 0, blue −1, violet −2, ultraviolet −3…−5. Gaussian output is explicitly (n−mean)/std. gaussian_backwards reseeds with initial_seed()−1.

providers.author: DazzleNodes
providers.note: Contains py/beta/rk_guide_func_beta.py with the same get_ortho_noise; name read only

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Default scale .1 means 'brown' and 'violet' are small tilts here: exponent α·0.1, not α.

entries.name: Restart renoise for rectified flow
entries.plain: A flow-model form of the restart jump. Variance-consistent because the signal scaling is included in the noise coefficient. Compare with the VE version in restart sampling.
entries.math: c=(1−t_max)/(1−t_min). x_max = c·x + √max(t_max²−(c·t_min)²,0)·z.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Restart sampling
entries.plain: Periodically jumps back up in noise level by adding a large amount of fresh noise, then re-solves that segment with a deterministic solver. Trades steps for contraction of earlier errors.
entries.math:
restart_list format {min_σ:[steps,times,max_σ]}. Auto: if steps≥20: 9 restart steps, 1 time (steps≥36: steps//4, 2 times), {0.1:[n+1,t,2]}; below 20 steps no restart.
Walk step_list; whenever the next σ_old > last σ: x ← x + ε·s_noise·√(σ_old²−σ_last²), then Heun step.

props.normalizes_variance: yes for the σ increase; injection uses global RNG, not a noise sampler

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: In auto mode it replaces your schedule: sigmas are rebuilt as Karras between sigmas[-2] and sigmas[0] (restart_sampling.py:48), so the chosen scheduler stops mattering when steps ≥ 20.

entries.name: Same-color noise (cross-channel mean match)
entries.plain: Shifts each noise pixel so its across-channel mean equals the reference latent's across-channel mean. Carries a rough luminance-like map from the reference into the start noise.
entries.math: ε' = ε + (mean_c(z) − mean_c(ε))·strength·channel_mask.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: SeededDisableNoise (RNG burn with no noise)
entries.plain: Returns zeros in place of noise but advances the global RNG by drawing and discarding noise from a seed, which fixes later per-step randomness while the start is unchanged.
entries.math: manual_seed(seed); random.seed(seed). For k in range(seed_offset): draw randn and discard. Return zeros.
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Sets the global torch and python RNG as a side effect (misc.py:54).

entries.name: SeedLab noise compositors
entries.plain: A library of NOISE objects that compose: seed interpolation, weighted blends with renormalise, per-channel seeds, masks, tiles, frequency split, drift, and using a latent as noise. Makes each noise a plain chainable source.
entries.math: Interp: slerp(a,b,t) or lerp. Blend: Σ w_i/Σw · ε_i, then /std. Drift: c←slerp(c,ε_{seed+i+1},drift) per frame. PerChannel: one seed per channel, derived beyond list. Masked: ε_in·m + ε_out·(1−m). Tiled: separate seed per tile. FreqSplit: F=F_low·(r≤cutoff)+F_high·(r>cutoff), ifft real, /std. LatentNoise: resized z, tiled, /std.

props.spectrum: low from one seed, high from another (freq split)
props.normalizes_variance: yes for Blend, FreqSplit, LatentNoise (/std); no for mask and tile

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Masked and interpolated variants do not renormalize: lerp at t=0.5 shrinks variance to ½, and mask edges have the same dip.

entries.name: Shader noise source and staged injection
entries.plain: Evaluates GLSL-style procedural shaders on the CPU as tensors (fractal, cellular, domain-warp, curl, tensor field and others), blends them with base noise, and can inject shader noise at interior steps.
entries.math:
blend_noises(base, shader, mode, strength). strength≤0 returns base; strength≥1 and normal returns shader. Modes applied in _apply_blend_mode.
Injection points: step_i = round((i+1)·T/(N+1)).
entries.label: from code

entries.name: Short-distance noise (best-of-K minimum distance)
entries.plain: Draws K noise candidates and picks the one closest to a reference latent by squared distance. A cheap way to get noise already aligned with the image, in the spirit of minibatch optimal-transport pairing.
entries.math: ε_k ~ N(0,I), k=1..K (default 32). ε = ε_k* with k* = argmin Σ(z − ε_k)².

props.spectrum: white with slight bias to reference

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Skoogeer latent procedural noises (std-relative)
entries.plain: Adds Perlin, simplex, Worley, fractal Brownian motion, swirl or reaction-diffusion patterns to a latent, with strength relative to that sample's std. Available in latent and image versions.
entries.math:
Base pattern p normalized (p−mean)/std in _normalize_noise_tensor.
scale=std(sample)·strength; z' = z + p·scale.
reaction-diffusion: Gray-Scott U,V: U+=(D_u∇²U − UV² + F(1−U))dt; V+=(D_v∇²V + UV² − (F+k)V)dt.

props.normalizes_variance: pattern unit std; final latent std rises

entries.label: from code

entries.name: Slerp, inject and unsampler toolkit (BlenderNeko)
entries.plain: A small node set for noise-as-latent workflows. Creates raw noise latents, interpolates them on a hypersphere, adds to a latent, and walks sigmas in reverse. Unsampler uses zero noise so the sampler's own solver acts as the inversion.
entries.math:
Slerp: ω=acos(n̂_a·n̂_b) by batch row; x = sin((1−t)ω)/sinω·a + sin(tω)/sinω·b; near-parallel falls back to lerp.
Inject: z' = z + strength·n, optional mask.
Unsampler: noise=0; sigmas flipped; sampler runs low→high.
GetSigma: (σ_start−σ_end)/scale_factor, a helper for correct inject amplitude.

props.normalizes_variance: no; slerp preserves norm only for near-orthogonal equal-norm inputs

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: GetSigma returns (σ_start−σ_end) divided by the VAE scale factor, so the inject strength it gives depends on the model's latent format.

entries.name: Sonar noise framework (normalization and chaining)
entries.plain: A library of 30+ noise types with per-call generators, composed by chain nodes and usable for ancestral and SDE noise or as a NOISE object. It treats normalization as a first-class flag rather than leaving it to each generator.
entries.math:
scale_noise(n): if normalized: mean, std; if |mean| > 2.5/√N: n←n−mean; if |1−std| > 2.5/√N: n←n/std. Optional dim-wise variant. Multiplied by factor.
Gaussian, Brownian, power_old, uniform, StudentT, pyramid_old and voronoi default normalized=False; most others default True.

props.normalizes_variance: yes by default, with threshold; see text

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: scale_noise only corrects when mean or std deviates past 2.5/√N, so near-normal draws are left untouched.

audit.note: Default-False list is incomplete: py/noise_generation.py:576 (pyramid_old) and 1352 (voronoi) also set normalized False.

entries.name: Structured noise (phase-preserving diffusion)
entries.plain: Builds noise from a reference latent: keep Gaussian-like magnitude from noise but take the Fourier phase from the reference at low frequencies. The result carries the reference's composition. Three ways to draw the magnitude are offered.
entries.math:
F_ref=fftshift(fft2(pad(z))), phase φ_r=angle(F_ref) then clipped; F_n from noise, or Rayleigh(√(N·σ²/2)) magnitudes with uniform phase (cdf) or √(u1²+u2²) (two-gaussian).
Mask M(r) = 1 for r≤cutoff, else exp(−(r−cutoff)²/(2·tw²)); no cutoff → all ones.
φ = M·φ_r + (1−M)·φ_n. out = Re ifft2(|F_n|·noise_std·exp(iφ)); pixels outside ±5 replaced by the raw noise; cropped.

props.spectrum: same magnitude as white on average; phase follows image

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: clip_frequency_magnitude is applied to the image phases (structured_noise_pytorch.py:126), clamping phases above their 95th percentile. Seed was not honored before the local patch at __init__.py:68.

entries.name: SUNoise (scaled uniform noise)
entries.plain: Ancestral samplers that alternate Gaussian and scaled-uniform noise by step, plus a NOISE node for initial noise. Uniform range depends on sigma_down. Multires variant adds half-resolution uniform values.
entries.math:
Per-step (called with σ_down): r=σ_down.item(); gen seeded with seed+int(1000·r) each call; n=U(−r,r) per channel. Multires: n=U(0,1) at scale 1 + nearest-upscaled U(0,1) at scale ½; then remapped to [−r,r] by min and max.
Initial: scale fixed; n=U(−scale,scale); seed+int(1000·scale).
Euler ancestral: x ← x + d·dt, then odd steps x ← x + su(σ_down); even steps x ← x + N(0,I)·s_noise·σ_up (sunoise.py:157).

props.normalizes_variance: no: uniform ±r has std r/√3, and odd steps ignore s_noise and σ_up

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: Even steps are plain Gaussian; only odd steps are uniform, and those skip both s_noise and σ_up (sunoise.py:157). The generator is reseeded per call from seed+int(1000σ).

entries.name: Temporal noise hold (AR(1) across frames)
entries.plain: Makes latent video noise correlated from frame to frame with an autoregressive filter, reducing boil. Each frame takes rho of the last one plus fresh noise weighted so variance stays one.
entries.math: n_t ← √(1−ρ²)·n_t + ρ·n_{t−1}, for t=1..T−1 in place on a 5D tensor. ρ=hold_to_rho(hold).

props.spectrum: white in space, low-pass in time

entries.label: from code

entries.name: TKG noise (color background shift)
entries.plain: Shifts selected channels of the start noise so a higher or lower fraction of values are positive, biasing the background to a color. A Gaussian mask keeps the center unshifted, so the subject stays neutral and the background takes the color.
entries.math:
For c with sign s: repeat ε_c += δ·s until frac(ε_c>0) ≥ frac₀ + shift·s (δ=0.1, shift=0.11).
G = exp(−(x²+y²)/(2·0.5²)), upsampled from grid_factor.
ε' = ε_shift·(1−G) + ε·G. Color table maps names to SD1 channel signs (green [0,1,1,0]).

props.distribution: standard normal with a channel mean shift outside center

entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: The loop test is one-sided (new_ratio ≥ target). For sign −1 the ratio falls but stays above target−, so it stops after a single δ step: negative channels move far less than positive ones.

entries.name: ULS empty-latent noise (colored, offset, fractal, character)
entries.plain: Empty-latent noise types with a cross-fade to white using the Gaussian sum rule. Pink, brown and blue use a proper radial filter with signed beta. The docstring acknowledges this has small effect at denoise 1.0.
entries.math:
Colored: w(f)=|f|^(−β/2), w(0)=0, spec×w, normalize. pink β=1, brown β=2, blue β=−1.
Character c: out = normalize(√(1−c²)·white + c·shaped).

entries.name: bislerp resize
entries.plain: Bilinear resampling where each 1D interpolation is a slerp of the channel vectors at a pixel rather than a lerp. It runs width first then height. Directions are slerped, magnitudes lerped, so per-pixel vector length is the lerped norm, which aims to avoid the contrast loss of plain bilinear.
entries.math:
For neighbour pair (b1,b2) with ratio r, over channel dim:
u1=b1/‖b1‖, u2=b2/‖b2‖ (zero norm→0), dot=u1·u2, ω=acos(dot)
res = [sin((1−r)ω)/sin ω]·u1 + [sin(rω)/sin ω]·u2
res *= ‖b1‖(1−r) + ‖b2‖r
if dot>1−1e−5 res=b1 (ignores r); if dot<−1+1e−5 res=lerp
ratios and indices come from interpolating a coordinate ramp with torch bilinear (align_corners false).

entries.name: common_upscale and LatentUpscale / LatentUpscaleBy
entries.plain: The shared resize used nearly everywhere. It flattens 5D video into 4D, optionally centre-crops to the target aspect, calls bislerp, lanczos, or torch interpolate, then restores the 5D shape. LatentUpscale takes pixel sizes and divides by 8 with a hard-coded factor of 8; LatentUpscaleBy multiplies latent size directly. No variance compensation for any mode.

crop center: trim round((old − old·(new_aspect/old_aspect))/2) from the wider axis.
mode bislerp → bislerp; lanczos → PIL lanczos; else F.interpolate(mode).
LatentUpscale: w//8, h//8 with min 64 px. If one is 0 the other is derived from aspect.

entries.name: LatentComposite with linear feather
entries.plain: Pastes one latent into another at an 8-pixel-grid offset. With feather on, it builds a linear ramp mask only on edges that do not touch the destination boundary. Corners multiply the two ramps, so they fall off faster than edges.

entries.name: LatentInterpolate (direction-and-magnitude blend)
entries.plain: Core's LatentInterpolate is not a lerp or a true slerp. It normalises each latent per pixel across channels, lerps the unit directions, renormalises, then applies a lerped magnitude. This keeps per-pixel vector length at the blended magnitude rather than shrinking it as a lerp does. This per-pixel behaviour holds for a batch of 1; the norms are taken without keepdim, so larger batches fail on broadcasting (inference from the code, not run).
entries.math:
m1=‖s1‖₂ over channel dim, m2=‖s2‖₂
u1=s1/m1, u2=s2/m2 (nan→0)
t = u1·ratio + u2·(1−ratio)
out = (t/‖t‖)·(m1·ratio + m2·(1−ratio))
ratio=1 returns samples1, ratio=0 returns samples2.
m has no kept channel dim, so this holds for batch 1 only (inference from broadcasting).

entries.name: LatentOperationBlend
entries.plain: Operation that pulls the latent toward a fixed reference by lerp, resizing the reference with nearest neighbour if needed. Via LatentApplyOperationCFG it would drag the guidance delta toward a latent, not the prediction.

entries.name: LatentOperationSharpen
entries.plain: Sharpens direction, keeps magnitude. It unit-normalises per pixel, convolves with a kernel built from a negative Gaussian with a compensated centre, then multiplies magnitude back. The result is not renormalised, so the norm drifts slightly.
entries.math:
L=‖x‖₂+1e−6, u=x/L
k = −10α·G(r·2+1,σ); k[c,c] ← k[c,c] − Σk + 1
out = L·conv2d(reflect_pad(u), k) per channel
G is built on a −1..1 grid, so σ is relative to kernel extent, not cells.
entries.label: from code

entries.name: LatentOperationTonemapReinhard
entries.plain: Compresses overly large latent vector magnitudes while keeping directions. The white point comes from per-sample stats of the magnitude map. It can go through LatentApplyOperationCFG to act on guidance. The formula always compresses, including at low values, since it is plain Reinhard with no knee.
entries.math:
m=‖x‖₂ over channels (+1e−10), u=x/m
μ,s = mean, std of m per sample
top=(5s+μ)·multiplier
m′ = (m/top)/((m/top)+1)·top
out = u·m′

entries.name: tiled_scale_multidim feathered tile accumulation
entries.plain: Core tile engine for VAE and upscalers. It runs the function on overlapping tiles and accumulates with a linear edge feather, dividing by the accumulated mask. entries.math:
orthogonal: Q from QR of a seeded Gaussian matrix, x′=Qx
reflect: v unit; x′=x−2v(vᵀx)
shear: u,v unit; x′=x+αu(vᵀx)
also signed permutation, gating, quantize, clip, dropout, packed-slot transforms

entries.name: Circular edges and seamless tile makers
entries.plain: Methods to make the left and right edges meet. HYWorld blends the first columns toward the last columns and crops them away, for panoramas in IMAGE. Quilting offers latent seam makers through patch search. Content-aware tiles build Wang or dual tile sets for inpainting boundaries. Quilting and content-aware internals were read at node level only.
entries.math:
HYWorld: w=linspace(0, 1−1/b); out[:b]=right(1−w)+left·w; crop right b
Quilting: seam-finding over overlapped patches (not derived here)

entries.name: Clamp and outlier limiting
entries.plain: Limits extreme values. spacepxl clamps at k standard deviations per channel. valkymaera clamps to a fixed range. Sparknight LatentClamp does not clamp at all despite its name: it multiplies values outside the range by a factor, optional noise added, so it can still leave them outside. JTrigger Huberise keeps tails with a reduced slope.
entries.math:
spacepxl: clamp(x, μ−kσ, μ+kσ) per sample and channel
Sparknight: x<min or x>max: x·m_out+n; else x·m_in+n; n=randn·extra·(1−m)
huberize: c,h from quantiles lowQ,highQ over whole tensor; x outside c±h → c±h + slope·excess

entries.name: Contrast-limited detail boost
entries.plain: Difference-of-Gaussians band, normalised by local RMS so flat areas and busy areas gain alike, tanh-limited, then gated down on strong edges. Passes audio of nested latents through unchanged, so it is one of the few that know H3 packed latents.
entries.math:
dog=G(s)x−G(l)x; rms=√G(rms_σ)(dog²)+floor; n=dog/rms
d=tanh(n·lim)/lim
edge=σ((|∇E|/max − t)/s), E=G(|x|mean); gate=1−p·edge
out=x+gain·d·gate

props.params: sigma_small=.6, sigma_large=1.4, gain=.35, limit=1.25, rms_sigma=1.2, rms_floor=.06, edge_protect=.45, edge_sigma=.8

entries.name: DCT spectral expand upscale
entries.plain: Upscale in the cosine domain: embed the DCT coefficients in a larger zero grid, fill the new high band with sigma-scaled noise through a taper, and inverse transform. It also rescales the signal and returns an aligned sigma, so sampling can continue at matched noise. Three blend modes; hard and linear are identical in the code.
entries.math:
F=DCT(x); Fe=zero grid with Fe[:H,:W]=F; mask=1 low, cosine taper near old edge
linear: mask·Fe+(1−mask)·σ·s·ε
variance_preserving: mask·Fe+√(1−mask²)·σ·s·ε
t=σ/(1+σ) if edm; t′=rt/(1+(r−1)t); κ=r/(1+(r−1)t); x′=κ·IDCT
lowpass start: x_low=IDCT(F[:th,:tw])

entries.name: FFT phase/magnitude split and combine
entries.plain: Puts magnitude and phase each into a LATENT wire so other nodes can operate on them, then combines with polar and takes the real part. Skoogeer keeps raw magnitude. CampB stores log1p magnitude as an option and adds swap, shaping and scramble nodes, but its core/freq.py is in neither the library copy nor the deploy backup, so swap and band formulas are not verified here.

entries.name: Five-band spectral EQ
entries.plain: Radial Gaussian bands with gains in dB, applied in ortho rfft2, keeping DC unchanged and optionally restoring per-sample RMS. Written for noise, but the maths is general; noise family has the applied form.

entries.name: Gaussian low-pass FFT blend for dilated refinement
entries.plain: Merges a low-resolution refinement with a full-resolution latent: low frequencies from the refinement, highs from the original. Cutoff derives from the downscale factor. Multi-frame video falls back to a plain lerp.
entries.math:
σh=h/(2f), σw=w/(2f); LP=exp(−½((x/σw)²+(y/σh)²)) in shifted space; E=LP·blend
F=Fo(1−E)+Fd·E

entries.name: Geometric median and spherical mean of N latents
entries.plain: Two ways to average many latents without plain-mean norm collapse. Geometric median uses Weiszfeld iterations and resists one outlier. Spherical mean averages unit directions per channel and rescales to the mean norm. Pack is a lab pack in the local library; core/freq.py etc. are absent from the patched copy.
entries.math:
median: est₀=mean; wᵢ=1/‖xᵢ−est‖ (min EPS); est=Σwᵢxᵢ/Σwᵢ; up to 24 iterations, stop at allclose 1e−6
spherical: per channel, flatten, u=x/‖x‖, d=mean(u), out=d/‖d‖·mean(‖x‖)

entries.name: High frequency noise re-entry at upscale (H3)
entries.plain: After spatially resizing video latents, adds fresh noise containing only frequencies above the previous resolution, scaled by RMS, so upscale stages do not lack high-frequency energy. Keeps old low frequencies untouched by construction.
entries.math:
ε fresh; low=resize(resize(ε,prev),cur); high=ε−low
out=x+high·(σ·gain/rms(high))

entries.name: Latent Normalized Lanczos Resize (decode, lanczos, encode, moment match)

entries.name: Radial band split on an unshifted FFT (bands swapped)
entries.plain: Two nodes build a radial mask centred at (h/2, w/2) and multiply it onto an FFT that was never fftshift-ed. In an unshifted FFT, DC sits at the corner and the centre holds the highest frequencies. So the output labelled low or macro holds the highest frequencies and DC lands in the high or micro band. masks do not sum to 1

entries.name: Slerp, one angle per batch sample
entries.plain: The classic latent slerp. Each sample is flattened to a single long vector, one angle is computed for it, and the raw (not unit) endpoints are mixed with sine weights. For near-orthogonal, equal-norm latents such as Gaussian noise the norm stays about constant, which is why it is used in place of lerp for noise. Norm is not explicitly restored when the two inputs differ in length.
entries.math:
per sample: û=a/‖a‖, v̂=b/‖b‖, ω=acos(û·v̂)
out = [sin((1−t)ω)/sin ω]·a + [sin(tω)/sin ω]·b
near-parallel handling differs by provider (see providers).
Variance: at t=0.5, ω=90°, equal variances: weights are 0.707 each, so variance is kept. Lerp would halve it.

entries.name: Spectral band gain and progress-weighted trust
entries.plain: Band masks are built correctly from fftfreq. One function boosts mid and attenuates highest frequencies. Another reweights denoised output by progress, trusting highs less early. The "quantum" in the pack name is branding; this part is FFT gains with a golden-ratio exponent.

mask: L=σ(20(lc−d)), H=σ(20(d−hc)), M=clamp(1−L−H,0)

entries.name: Spectral power-law shaping and phase scramble
entries.plain: SpectralShape tilts the whole spectrum by a power of radial frequency, optionally restoring energy. PhaseScramble randomises phase by a seeded amount along the shortest arc while keeping magnitude, which destroys structure and keeps texture stats. The radius and decompose helpers live in the missing core/freq.py, so only the node-level maths is confirmed.

entries.name: Tonemap on channel 0 only (Reinhard, Möbius, ACES-like)
entries.plain: Same white-point recipe as core but applied only to channel 0, treated as luminance, with a choice of three curves. On a one-channel slice the vector norm is just |x|, so the sign is kept and the magnitude is compressed. Treating channel 0 as luminance is the pack's assumption.

entries.name: Variance-aware blends: pythagorean lerp, orbit, RMS, cosine, cubic
entries.plain: bleh has blends that handle variance loss on purpose. Pythagorean lerp rescales weights so squares sum to 1 at the default, the right correction for independent inputs. Orbit moves on a quarter circle so endpoints are a and b. RMS interpolates in a power domain. Cosine and cubic only reshape t and do not correct variance.
entries.math:
pythagorean: raw=(|1−t|^p+|t|^p)^(1/p), p=2; mag=raw^growth_power (default 0→1, optional soft clamp); w=(1−t,t)·mag/raw
orbit: a·cos(tπ/2)+b·sin(tπ/2)
rms: (lerp(a^p,b^p,t))^(1/p), sign from blended or chosen input, p=2
cosinterp: ((a+b)−(a−b)cos(πt))/2
cuberp: a+(b−a)(3t²−2t³)
weighted_average: (a+t·b)/(1+|t|)
entries.label: from code
entries.surprise: growth_power default 0 makes mag=1, so pythagorean_lerp defaults to true variance preservation for independent inputs; orbit has no denominator, so it matches that shape without an eigen-check.

entries.name: WAS BlendLatents, output rescaled to 0..1
entries.plain: Twelve image-style modes on latents, and the result of every mode is min-max rescaled to 0..1 over the whole tensor. That removes negative values and the original scale of the latent, so downstream sampling sees a very different distribution. The docstring states the rescale, so it is intended.

add: a·f+b(1−f); multiply: (a·f)(b(1−f)); divide; subtract
overlay: (a·f)(2ab)+(b·f)(1−2(1−a)(1−b))
screen: 1−(1−a)(1−b)(1−f)
soft_light with √a (NaN for a<0)
out=(x−min)/(max−min)

entries.name: μ-centred slerp
entries.plain: Slerp around a population centroid rather than the origin. It subtracts μ, slerps directions, lerps the radius, adds μ back. Useful when the latent has a non-zero mean, because origin-centred slerp then bends through a different arc. When μ is not given, the function uses per-channel mean over batch and space.

entries.name: Block-Sparse Attention (Sol-Attn / SLA / VSA)
entries.plain: Replaces dense self-attention with a block-sparse kernel from comfy_kitchen, where each query block attends exactly to a chosen subset of key blocks. Three selection modes: an adaptive per-head threshold (sol-attn), a fixed top percent (sla), and 3D video-cube tiling with a learned coarse branch (vsa). Falls back to the dense backend outside the sigma window, under the token minimum, on listed blocks, or when dtype/head_dim/device don't fit.
entries.math:
Dense if σ∉[σ_end,σ_start], tokens<min_tokens(12288), block∈dense_blocks, mask given, not CUDA, kernel unavailable, dtype∉{bf16,fp16,fp32}, head_dim≠128, q,k,v shapes differ.
Otherwise ck.sol_attn(q,k,v,tau,topk_ratio,sink_blocks,sink_q,token_aug). Block size 64 tokens. topk_ratio=0 for sol-attn, keep_percent/100 else. The kernel itself is in comfy_kitchen and was not read here.
MiniMax H3: block replace feeds a chunked qkv producer (4096-token slices) with pooled kmean/vscale carried from the previous step, per (block,n,uuids).
H3 sinks: packed text/audio/ref rows kept exact for every query; exact_kv_and_rows also keeps audio query rows dense.
VSA: 4×4×4 cubes padded to 64-row tiles, requires an H3 layout; extra_tokens forced to 0.

entries.name: Differential Diffusion (soft mask)
entries.plain: Lets a greyscale mask act as a per-pixel denoise strength. At each step only pixels whose mask value exceeds a falling threshold can change, so regions join the edit at different times. Core adds a strength blend back to the soft mask.
entries.math:
thr = (t(σ) − t(σ_to))/(t(σ_0) − t(σ_to)), σ_to = max(sigma_min, σ_last), t = model_sampling.timestep
m_bin = (m ≥ thr)
strength∈(0,1): m' = strength·m_bin + (1−strength)·m; else m' = m_bin
Consumer KSamplerX0Inpaint: x ← x·m' + noise_scaling(σ,ε,latent)·(1−m'); out ← out·m' + latent·(1−m').

props.architectures: Any model through the KSampler inpaint wrapper; needs a denoise mask.

entries.name: EasyCache
entries.plain: Skips whole model forwards when predicted output change is small, then adds the cached output−input difference to the current input. It estimates output change from the measured input change and the last-seen ratio of output change to input change. Needs no per-model calibration, unlike TeaCache.
entries.math:
On first-cond model call, in the start/end window:
Δin = mean|x↓ − x_prev↓| (8× subsample of first cond's slice)
r̂ = R·Δin/‖y_prev‖₁, ‖·‖₁ = mean abs; C += r̂
If C < τ and every cond's diff exists: skip, y = x + diff_uuid for each cond. Other conds follow via skip_current_step.
Else C=0, run model. After a run: R = mean|y↓−y_prev↓|/Δin; diff_uuid = y − x.
LTX2 lists [video,audio] handled together; shape mismatch cuts from the start and logs nothing.

props.architectures: Model-agnostic at the DIFFUSION_MODEL wrapper; first output_channels (latent_channels) only. LTX2 AV lists supported.

entries.name: FreeU (v1)
entries.plain: Rescales UNet decoder features before they merge with the encoder skip: the first half of the backbone channels gets a flat gain, and the skip's low frequencies are attenuated in FFT space. Used to shift the balance between backbone denoising and skip detail on SD-style UNets.
entries.math:
Only when the output-block channel count C(h) equals mc·4 (uses b1,s1) or mc·2 (b2,s2), mc=model_channels from the unet config.
h[:, :C/2] ← h[:, :C/2]·b
ĥ = fftshift(FFT2(hsp)); ĥ[centre ±1 bin box] ×= s; hsp ← Re(IFFT2(ifftshift(ĥ)))
Fourier threshold is fixed at 1, so a 2×2 centre box. No sigma gating: applies every step.

props.architectures: UNet with model_config.unet_config['model_channels'] (SD1.x/SD2/SDXL-style). Reads that key directly, so a DiT with no model_channels raises KeyError at patch time.

entries.name: H3 PDD output-head bank fusion
entries.plain: A distilled H3 LoRA can carry several stacked output heads, one per fine training step. An actual sampler step spans several fine steps, so the output head used on that step is a dt-weighted mix of those heads. Core handles a converted bank natively; several packs instead load the official files and fuse the heads themselves, and they differ on what the stored heads mean and on which schedules they allow.
entries.math:
Fine grid g_j on [1,0], n+1 points; d_j = differences of (1 − s·g/(1+(s−1)·g)), with s = stream shift (12 video, 3 audio).
w_j = d_j / Σ d over the fine steps inside this sampler step.
Core, _pdd_head: head = H_0 + Σ_{j≥max(start,1)} w_j·H_j (row 0 is a full head, later rows are offsets).
CineConIA, fuse_heads: head_block = Σ w_j·H_j over each block of 4, treating every row as a full head.
Deno: same weighted mean, weights from overlap of the requested σ interval with the bank's trained grid, recomputed per schedule.

entries.name: HiDream-O1 Patch Seam Smoothing
entries.plain: Runs the model extra times on circularly shifted inputs and blends the unshifted predictions to hide the 32-pixel patch grid. Costs one extra model call per extra shift, inside a percent window. Edge rows are feathered back to the unshifted prediction to hide wraparound.
entries.math:
For each shift (sy,sx) in preset: p_i = roll(F(roll(x,(sy,sx))),(−sy,−sx)). Blend: mean, Hann window weights, or median.
Out = pred·(1−m·strength) + avg·(m·strength); m = edge ramp, 0 in P px strip then ramp over 4 px.
Ramp modes pick 2,4,8 passes by phase (t_start−t)/(t_start−t_end).

entries.name: HyperTile
entries.plain: Splits self-attention query tokens into a grid of tiles to cut attention cost at high resolution. At the default swap_size of 2 the grid is fixed, because the last candidate can never be drawn; it only varies per call with swap_size 3 or more and enough divisors. Only the query is rearranged by this patch; keys and values are passed back untouched.
entries.math:
For token count n in {H·W/4^i, i=0..max_depth}: h=round√(n·ar), w=round√(n/ar), ar=W/H.
nh = random divisor pick: candidates d of h with d ≥ max(32,tile_size)//8·f; n = h//d, first swap_size candidates, idx=randint(0,len−1) with exclusive high so the last is never picked; same for nw. f=2^i if scale_depth else 1.
If nh·nw>1: q is rearranged into batch b·nh·nw of (h/nh · w/nw) tokens; output patch rearranges back. RNG is torch.randint so it follows the torch seed state.

props.architectures: UNet-style models where attn1 tokens relate to original_shape by a 4^i factor; applies only on token counts that match exactly.

entries.name: ModelSampling prediction-type overrides
entries.plain: These nodes swap the model's sampling object, telling the sampler how to read model output. Shift values are covered by the scheduler pages; this entry records the prediction maths. Using the wrong type gives broken results, since x0 is computed differently in each one.
entries.math:
x = model input, F = output, σd = sigma_data, x0 = denoised:
eps: x0 = x − F·σ; c_in = 1/√(σ²+σd²); noise: x + n·σ (max_denoise n·√(1+σ²))
v_prediction: x0 = x·σd²/(σ²+σd²) − F·σ·σd/√(σ²+σd²)
edm: as v but plus the F term
x0: x0 = F
img_to_img: x0=F, input not scaled
const/flow: x0 = x − F·σ; no c_in; noise: σ·(s·n) + (1−σ)·x_lat; inverse x/(1−σ)
img_to_img_flow: x0=F; noise_scaling returns latent; inverse 1−latent
img_to_img_velocity: x0 = x − F
cosmos_rflow: s=σ/(σ+1); c_in=(1−s); x0 = x(1−s) − F·s
v_prediction_ddpm (CogVideoX): x0 = x/√(σ²+1) − F·σ/√(σ²+1), unscaled input
lcm: x0_eps = x − Fσ; t=10·timestep; x0 = c_out·x0_eps + c_skip·x, c_skip=.25/(t²+.25), c_out=t/√(t²+.25); base resamples sigmas to 50 steps.

props.architectures: Set by the node, not checked. ModelSamplingDiscrete / ContinuousEDM / ContinuousV / SD3 / AuraFlow / Flux / StableCascade build a new class from base+type each call.

entries.name: RenormCFG (Lumina2)
entries.plain: A replacement CFG function that does classic CFG only below a limit compared with sigma (the args key is named timestep but holds sigma), and caps the guided output's norm at a multiple of the conditional's norm. Above the limit it just returns the conditional. It only operates on the first in_channels; other channels pass through from cond.
entries.math:
If σ[0] < cfg_trunc (args["timestep"] holds σ): e = u + s(c−u) over first in_channels; if renorm_cfg>0: M = ‖c‖·renorm_cfg, if ‖e‖ ≥ M then e ← e·M/‖e‖.
Else e = c.
Result is x − cat(e, cond rest), since a sampler_cfg_function returns x − denoised form.

entries.name: Sequential vs batched CFG
entries.plain: Whether cond and uncond are run in one batch or one after the other. Core decides this itself by memory, so no flag exists in stock KSampler: it fits as many as free memory allows. entries.name: Temporal Score Rescaling (TSR)
entries.plain: Post-CFG rescale of the score that steers output diversity by a signal-to-noise dependent ratio. The node text says lower k gives more detail and higher k gives smoother results; k=1 turns it off.
entries.math:
snr = exp(2·half_log_snr(σ)); r = (snr·σ_t²+1)/(snr·σ_t²/k+1), r=k when snr=+∞
D' = lerp(x/α, D, r), α = σ·exp(half_log_snr)
Skip if k=1, σ=0 or snr=0.

entries.name: ToMe (Token Merging, tomesd port)
entries.plain: Merges similar self-attention query tokens before attention and restores them after, so fewer queries run. Speeds up sampling at some detail cost. Only runs on the highest-resolution attention blocks, and the core port leaves keys and values at full length.
entries.math:
Each 2×2 cell randomly gives one dst token; the rest are src. Similarity = cosine(src,dst) on q. r=int(N·ratio) src tokens with the highest best-match score are merged by mean into their dst (scatter_reduce); others stay.
Unmerge copies dst values back into the merged src positions.
Only when downsample = ceil(√(H·W // N)) ≤ 1. Comfy uses q as the metric where upstream uses block input x (comment at line 167).

entries.name: Cache Accelerator: fixed-interval x0 extrapolation (Wtl)
entries.plain: Runs the model on a fixed rhythm inside a step window and predicts the x0 of the skipped evaluations from the last three real ones. It has no change threshold, so the speedup is set in advance. The prediction shrinks towards holding x0 when the recent motion reversed, and it keeps fine detail from a plain linear guess while taking coarse structure from the careful one.
entries.math:
τ = continuous step index found by interpolating −log σ on the schedule.
follow r = clamp(⟨m2,m1⟩/⟨m1,m1⟩, 0, 1), m1,m2 = x0 slopes per unit τ over the last 3 anchors.
guess x̂ = x0_cur + r·(τ−τ_cur)/(τ_cur−τ_prev)·(x0_cur − x0_prev).
With two conds (cond,uncond): extrapolate uncond and (cond−uncond) separately, each with its own r, then add.
linear ℓ = x0_cur + min(t, cap)·Δx0, cap = clamp(1/(4‖Δx0‖/‖x0‖ + 0.5), 0.5, 2).
Final for 4D+ latents: ℓ + G(x̂ − ℓ), G = spatial Gaussian blur σ=2 latent px.
Skip when (eval index in window) mod cache_interval ≠ 0; needs 3 anchors, else runs for real.

entries.name: CachedSearch: best-of-N seeds on cached drafts
entries.plain: Uses a step cache to make seed search cheap instead of to make the final render fast. Every candidate seed is sampled with core EasyCache, decoded and scored by an image-reward model, then the winning seed is sampled again with the cache off. Sampling is seeded, so the delivered latent is a plain full-compute render of that seed.
entries.math:
For s in seed..seed+N−1: draft_s = sample(EasyCache(model), s); score_s = mean ImageReward(prompt, frames) over up to 8 evenly spaced frames.
winner = argmax score. commit on: return sample(model, winner). commit off: return draft_winner.

entries.name: First Block Cache (FBCache)
entries.plain: Runs the first transformer block every step, and compares its output or residual to the previous step's. If they barely changed, the remaining blocks are skipped and a stored tail residual is applied. It uses a real model output as the signal, so needs no per-model calibration, at the cost of one block per step.
entries.math:
Base: δ = mean|f_t − f_prev| / mean|f_prev|, f = first block residual or output. Skip if δ<τ; out = x + R_tail.
No accumulation between steps in these implementations.
H3 (duckyshell): f = first block residual; optional temporal guard adds per-latent-frame max of δ; also requires hits < max_consecutive(2); window by sigma; tail residual per uuid context.
Lightning: f = first block img output; numerator over the current value rather than the previous.

entries.plain: A MiniMax H3 cache that always computes leading blocks and may skip the trailing portion, using sigma gap, a consecutive limit, and a content score from the warm-prefix output. entries.name: H3 pruned-base AdaLN LoRA reinjection
entries.plain: Pruned H3 checkpoints replace the time embedder with a small curve table, so a LoRA's AdaLN update has no matching weight to patch. Two routes were found. One recovers the missing embedding at run time from a bundled grid and adds the update to each projection's output. The other refits the update into the pruned curve space by least squares, once, and rejects a poor fit.

Turbo route: st = E[nearest row of adaln_t_table to t_emb], or lerp of E at unique t; x ← linear(t_emb) + B·A·st.
CineConIA route: solve E(t) ≈ c + table(t)·Vᵀ by least squares, reject if relative residual > 5e-4.
Then Δweight = (α/rank)·B·A·V and Δbias = (α/rank)·B·A·c, applied as ordinary diff patches.

entries.name: H3 PTD per-step adapters (WAS)
entries.plain: Applies a Parametric Trajectory Distillation file so H3 samples in 4 to 8 steps. entries.name: H3 whole block-stack residual cache (DaSiWa)
entries.plain: Skips all H3 transformer blocks at once on some steps and adds the block stack's last residual to the current input instead. The decision compares a thin sample of the stack's input between steps, so no block has to run to decide. It needs a replaced model forward, because core has no patch point around the whole block loop.
entries.math:
sig(h) = mean over the first 64 hidden dims of |h|, taken on about 100 evenly spaced rows of each audio and video segment (text excluded).
On each eval with a cached residual: A += mean|sig(h) − sig_last| / (mean|sig_last| + 1e-6), where sig_last is from the last computed eval and stays fixed across skips.
Skip when start_percent ≤ step/total ≤ end_percent, A < reuse_threshold, consecutive skips < max_steps: h_out = h + R.
Otherwise run blocks, R = h_out − h, A = 0.
Progress is a step fraction (counted on timestep change), not a sigma percent.

entries.name: HiDiffusion RAU-Net
entries.plain: Resolution-aware UNet hack: during early sampling, replaces a chosen downsample conv with a dilated stride-4 version and upsamples by matching interpolation, and also scales features at chosen cross-attention blocks. entries.name: HyperFlow two-time (t, r) conditioning
entries.plain: Conditions each H3 denoising step on the interval it integrates rather than on one time point. The port swaps the time embedder for a mix of the normal embedding of t and a second embedding of the step's endpoint r, built from raw weights plus a LoRA. r_v = 1 − σ_next; r_a = 1 − shift(σ_next); conditioning and masked rows pin r = t.

Row tags are remapped as row·3+tag so that colliding t values with different r become separate rows.

entries.name: MagCache (magnitude-ratio cache)
entries.plain: Skips based on a precomputed table of how the residual's magnitude changes step to step, rather than on the live input. Error accumulates as the running ratio drifts from 1, with a hard cap on consecutive skips and an initial retention window. Needs a ratio table for the model, or a calibration run.
entries.math:
γ_i from table by call count. r *= γ_i; e += |1−r|; n += 1
Skip if e ≤ thresh and n ≤ K: x = x_in + R.
Else r=1, e=0, n=0; run; R = out − in.
Enabled when step index ≥ int(retention·len(sigmas)). Past the table's end: no skipping.

entries.name: MeanCache
entries.plain: On skipped steps it uses an estimate of the average velocity over the interval, built from a finite difference of past velocities, instead of repeating the last velocity. JVP ≈ (v_t − v_r)/(σ_r−σ_t). û = v_cache + (σ_cache−σ)·JVP.

entries.name: Radial attention (sparse by frame distance)
entries.plain: Sparse temporal self-attention where each token attends to nearby frames densely, and to far frames in narrow windows that shrink with distance, plus occasional full far frames. Early dense steps are kept. The mask builds per sequence and runs through a block-sparse Sage kernel.
entries.math:
dist=|i−j|, group=bit_length(dist).
Window width: dist<1 → tokens per frame; dist=1 → half; else max(2^bits(T)/2^group·decay, block_size).
Diagonal split: decay_length=2^bits(T)/2^group, if ≥block_size full; else factor=int(block/decay); full only when dist%factor==0.
Block mask: a block counts if >60% of its nonzero columns have density>⅓.
Dense steps first; RadialSpargeSageAttn on block mask.

entries.name: Regional log-coverage cross-attention bias (bv)

entries.name: Regional tracked map with logit routing (Nynxz)
entries.plain: Keeps a region map that can move with the content during sampling, by reclustering canvas key features at a few middle blocks. entries.name: SeaCache
entries.plain: TeaCache-like accumulation, but the change metric is computed after a sigma-dependent spectral filter, so frequency bands the current noise level hides don't count. No polynomial calibration is needed in this pack. H3 gets a separate runtime with video and audio accumulators.
entries.math:
Filter per axis: g(f) = a·S/(a²S+b²+ε), S = 1/(|f|^p+ε), a=1−σ', b=σ', σ' = normalised flow sigma. Product over dims, normalised to mean 1, applied through full complex FFT.
A += mean|F(m)−F(m_prev)|/max(mean|F(m_prev)|,1e-16), run if A≥τ; per CFG branch.
H3: max(A_video, A_audio)<τ skips; audio unfiltered per the docstring; stride 4.

entries.name: Spectrum (Chebyshev feature forecasting)
entries.plain: Fits a Chebyshev-basis ridge regression through past outputs or features over time, and predicts them on cached steps, blended with a first-order extrapolation. Real steps get sparser as a flexible window grows. Implementations disagree on what is forecast: whole denoised output, or the feature just before the final layer.
entries.math:
Φ_ik = T_k(x_i), x∈[−1,1]; C = (ΦᵀΦ + λI)⁻¹ΦᵀY.
ŷ = w·(Tᵀ(x)C) + (1−w)·(y_last + k(y_last−y_prev)), k=(t−t_last)/(t_last−t_prev).
Real step if cache<2, step<warmup, or (cached+1)%floor(W)==0; W += flex each real step. Fixed: step%window==0.
benjiyaya: Y = model's denoised output across the whole wrapper, flattened per branch.
sorryhyun: Y = pre-final_layer feature captured by a pre-hook; replays final layer; optional SEA refresh: real if accumulated SEA distance ≥ δ with auto-δ calibration; tail steps always real.

entries.label: from code

entries.name: T-GATE (cached attention after a gate)
entries.plain: After a sigma gate, it stops computing cross-attention, and optionally self-attention, reusing the last computed batch's cached result, averaged over cond and uncond once CFG is off. Past the gate the uncond pass is dropped and cfg becomes 1. This saves the attention calls while still running conv blocks. It replaces the transformer block forward.
entries.math:
Cross: if σ<σ_gate and cached: n=attn2_cache; if only_cross or σ<σ_gate_attn1, n=mean of its chunks.
Self, only when only_cross is off: if σ<σ_gate_attn1 and cached: n=attn1_cache; if σ<σ_gate, n=mean of its chunks.
σ<σ_off (σ_gate if only_cross, else min of both gates): uncond=None, cfg=1. Gate σ from percent_to_sigma(start_at).

entries.name: TaylorSeer
entries.plain: Instead of reusing old features, it forecasts them with a Taylor series built from finite differences at earlier computed steps, per block and module. Steps alternate between full computation every N steps and forecasted ones. Memory grows with block count unless the Lite node is used, which forecasts one tensor.
entries.math:
Full step if step<first_enhance or counter=fresh_threshold−1 or step≥last_enhance.
On a full step: Δ⁰=f; Δ^{i+1} = (Δ^i − Δ^i_old)/d, d = steps between activations, up to max_order.
Forecast: f(x) = Σ Δ^i·xⁱ/i!, x = step − last full step.
Lite: once at stack output instead of each module.

entries.name: TC-Padé residual predictor
entries.plain: Predicts the whole transformer stack's residual from recent residuals using a rational (Padé-like) formula with a per-element stability factor. Predicts on all non-interval steps inside a range, regardless of how much the signal changed.
entries.math:
If start<step<end and step%interval≠0: x = x_in + R̂.
ω = exp(−5|R1−R2|/(avg+1e-7)); b0=2ω, b1=ω; a1=∓0.1ω by curvature sign.
R̂ = (b0·R1 − b1·R2)/(1 + a1·sign), clamped around .6R1+.4R2 by ±max(.5|R1−R2|,.1avg), blended with weight .7ω+.3.
Short history uses weighted extrapolation .4,.3,.2,.1.

entries.label: from code

entries.name: TeaCache (timestep-embedding-aware cache)
entries.plain: Skips the DiT block stack when the first block's modulated input has hardly changed since the last computed step, and re-adds the stored residual instead. The raw relative change is mapped through a per-model polynomial, then accumulated until it crosses the threshold. Polynomial coefficients are per architecture and per Wan variant, so the model_type must match.
entries.math:
δ = mean|m_t − m_prev| / mean|m_prev|, m = first-block modulated input (Flux: img_norm1·(1+scale)+shift; Wan: e, or e0 with _ret_mode; HiDream full: timesteps, else hidden_states)
A += |poly(δ)|, poly = 4th-degree per-model coefficient list
If A < rel_l1_thresh: skip stack; x += R
Else A=0; run stack; R = x_out − x_in
CFG models keep separate state for cond and uncond, but a batch runs if either wants to; Flux/HunyuanVideo keep one state.
start/end_percent by step index in sample_sigmas.

entries.name: Tiled Diffusion (MultiDiffusion, SpotDiffusion)
entries.plain: Splits the latent into tiles per step and calls the model per tile, then blends, to allow large images within memory. SpotDiffusion randomly rolls the latent each step so tile seams land in a new place and needs no overlap.
entries.math:
MultiDiffusion: out = Σ tile outputs / overlap count.
Spot: rng per timestep; x↷=roll(x,(h,w)); cond and ControlNet shifted proportionally; tiles without overlap; result rolled back.

entries.name: TurboTeaCache (TeaCache with quantized residuals)
entries.plain: A TeaCache variant that stores residuals through a vector-quantizer buffer to save memory, and optionally extrapolates from the two most recent residuals. The pack's Wan 2.2 coefficient is a stated proxy for 2.1.
entries.math:
δ = rel L1 of timestep embedding; A += poly(δ) (Horner, unsigned); skip if A<τ.
Residual on skip: R0, or R0 + α(R0−R1), α=clamp((t0−t)/|t0−t1|,0,alpha_cap).
Compression in TurboQuantMSE (turbo_quant.py); not traced in detail.

entries.name: TwinFlow (few-step with target-time embedder)
entries.plain: A few-step method where the model also knows the target timestep through a second time embedder. The pack loads extra embedder weights onto native Z-Image or Qwen-Image models and adds its own sampler. It needs a TwinFlow checkpoint.
entries.math:
Z-Image: adaln = emb(t') + emb₂((tt'−t')·1000)·|t'−tt'|, t'=1−σ, tt'=1−σ_target. Target passes in transformer_options, read by a forward pre-hook.
Sampler (Linear transport, UCGM-S): F=(x−D)/t; x̂=D; ẑ=x+(1−t)F
x_next=(1−t_n)x̂ + t_n(ẑ√(1−r)+n√r), r=stochast_ratio.
